Very Interesting and Cool

Disclaimer: I played Deus Ex: Human Revolution but none of the other games in the franchise.
Once again we take on the role as Adam Jensen yada yada, you know all this :)
The primary city hub – Prague – is massive this time around and did evoke a City 17-esque feeling while I was rummaging through abandoned apartments, run-down stores, etc. Every area seems to tell a story, whether through clever environmental storytelling or more plainly through emails and e-books.
Some of the areas outside of Prague are also incredibly detailed. I couldn’t believe how little time I spent in environments that were so obviously time-consuming to build. The amount of clutter and detail in Golem city alone is staggering.
This varied level design pervades through other areas of the game as well. In Human Revolution it often felt like you had exactly one stealth route, one passive route and a way to go through guns blazing. Mankind Divided’s levels blow your options wide open in this regard and enable you to switch your play style every step of the way.
I also feel like the side missions deserve a special mention. An inspection of an augmented body, for example, quickly becomes a full blown investigation with multiple suspects that goes way deeper than you’d expect. Very often these side quests also can’t be completed in one go and instead accompany you a good chunk of the game.
Of course not everything is gold – no pun intended - in Mankind Divided. The main story, while interesting, lacks oomph and ends rather abruptly. The oppressed augmented scheme also gets repeated by everything and everyone ad nauseam. It’s like everything in the game world exits solely to drive the mechanical apartheid point home.
The facial animation often times look weird or wooden, though you’ll probably automatically fade that out to an extent when you’re playing for a while.
All in all I enjoyed my time with Mankind Divided very much and if you’ve played and liked Human Revolutions this is essentially a must.

The Sims as a whole has always had some stability issues, if you accidentally find the trigger. The game itself has a stability issue over time. If you play in one neighborhood and let it grow, i.e let Sims reproduce, have new families added to the town, etc. you may eventually encounter so called "lag spikes". It's something comparable to your screen freezing, but only for 1-3 seconds, while the sound continues to work, the world will freeze shortly. These lag spikes are going to occur at a certain point, once your neighborhood is "full". There is no limit in theory, yes, but once there are too many entities in an actively progressing neighborhood, you will see that the game starts to have issues with that. Trust me, this is not a problem about your hardware being outdated, it is the poor coding and entity clearing/resetting of the game. I suggest keeping the amount of neighborhood sims and families to a lower level. Remember, you can always force them to die, either on a natural way, or through the debug console!
Can't fix your neighborhood, but at least want to keep your family with their house? Copy the entire household with building, then delete your neighborhood in the main menu and create a new one. You can then add the copy of your original family + house to any new neighborhood, regardless which map you picked and the game will run fluently again!
Not all are really good in content, value and stability, as I've figured through research and opinions from friends. I suggest the following for the best content and most fluent gameplay in combination with other expansions: Seasons, Supernatural, Pets and Generations. You won't need any other, in my opinion. Island Paradise should be completely ignored, it's known to be one of the most problematic ones.
: The more expansions you buy and the more DLC you add to the main game, the more unstable it will become! This is no joke, even if your computer is "overkill" for this game, the game will still♥♥♥♥♥♥itself. Blame the developers...
I suggest to research the web with Google to find free downloadable content such as maps, hair styles, clothes and items, since Origin is one greedy crowd of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Takes you less than 5 minutes. Check out the blogs of Sims gamers, since any other kind of site will most likely add a virus to your file - that includes downloads from Youtube video descriptions too!
Personally I play on a high-end machine, which is why I do not encounter the casualties of hardware compatibility problems. In case you have some, focus on having a good processor and video card (graphics card). 4k RAM is enough if you don't run anything else and 4k RAM is the least people own nowadays - the very least. If yours is above the "minimum" suggested by the developer, but your game feels sloppy and performs badly, you may make changes in the games settings for improvements. Alternative you may have to upgrade your hardware or buy a new PC if you can't do that by yourself. However, it's Sims we are talking about and a good processor should do the job.
You can lower the graphics settings tremendously in this game, which will help you a lot if playing on an older PC. Additionally you may turn off the active neighborhood progression setting in the game options. Then your neighborhood is not going to "play" in the background and will only change if you are in range of these Sims.

For years now, the WRC branded games have been nothing but disappointment. The last one I played properly was WRC 3, and that game was just hateful. Rubbish physics, nasty graphics and a soundtrack that could give a deaf person a migraine.
Years later, I expected something better, especially given the rights have changed company. I also read a few other reviews before buying and it sounded somewhat promising. I didn’t go into this game expecting a full simulator like Dirt Rally, but I did expect better.
Firstly, the stages are rather poor, as they really don’t represent the rally they are for well at all. There is still an over-reliance on hairpins to make the stages seem longer. I also expected better real stages. The game boasts that they have represented real WRC stages in the game. Don’t be fooled by that, they have only rendered the short spectator stages.
The physics have come a long way from WRC 3. There is a decent feel to the cars in the flowing sections of the stages, but they are far too loose in the sharp turns, defaulting to a drift very quickly (even the front wheel drive DS3s). It just ruins the feel with the car and prevents you having any confidence in the car.
The pacenotes are pathetic. Games from 10 years ago did a better job than this. They are very robotic. You can tell the developers recorded the bare minimum and stitched them together. This means they are very jerky and lack any flow at all. They are also wrong in places and the timing is appalling, even after changing the delivery time. Once again, it just prevents you from having any confidence in the notes.
There are good features. The graphics aren’t too bad (but Dirt Rally has it beaten) and the career mode is decent, but the game just doesn’t feel finished. The AI is too easy, and there are just some moments that make you feel like the game just isn’t a polished product. For example, in a head to head super special stage, I crossed the line behind the AI car in the other lane. It then said I won the stage by 20 seconds. Amazing.
Finally, the little “facts” on the loading screens are just stupid. They didn’t need to be! It only requires a bit of reading into the sport to get those right, but most of them are just pointless or wrong. For example, the fact I got before Portugal was saying the rally is run solely on gravel (which is true), but the Portuguese stage I did had a tarmac section in it! It almost feels like the game developers have absolutely no idea about the sport they are representing at all.
When will the WRC realise that Codemasters do a far better job at games like this and give them the rights to the championship!?

In the year 1995, the First Person Shooter genre was going strong. Wolfenstein 3D... Doom... Heretic... They all put id Software on the map, and defined the genre. And then Apogee Software blew the FPS concept to tiny bloody chunks, and rebuilt it into something totally ludicrous. Enter Rise of The Triad. Starting out as a sequel to Wolfenstein 3D, Rise of The Triad was revamped into a whole new experience. Featuring five unique playable characters, a massive arsenal of deadly firepower, an actual narrative, dog mode, god mode, shrooms mode, one incredibly deadly baseball bat, enemies who begged you to spare their lives (before flopping over to play dead so they could stab you in the back as soon as you turn around), and enough ludicrous gibs to earn it the billing of "most violent game ever", RoTT was an amazing experience when played alone. Add to that the amazing "COMM-BAT" multiplayer experience, it's pretty clear that Rise of The Triad hit a home run.
But let's head back to a time two years before Rise of The Triad came to be. In 1993, JAM Productions created a new game franchise centered around a hero named Blake Stone, and had Apogee Software publish it. A sci-fi thriller to the core, Aliens of Gold saw the titular secret agent Blake Stone facing off against his nemesis, an insidiously corrupt and morally bankrupt geneticist named Dr. Pyrus Goldfire. Technologically it built on the Wolfenstein 3D engine, adding in new features such as friendly NPC characters, working vending machines, and most impressively for the time, floor and ceiling textures. Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold actually managed to beat id Software's Doom to the market by one week and achieved modest popularity because of it, but was unfortunately overshadowed by the explosive popularity of id's smash hit.
The release of Doom and subsequent decline in sales of the first Blake Stone did not faze JAM Productions however, and in the following year of 1994 they released a new entry, Blake Stone: Planet Strike. Picking up immediately after Aliens of Gold, Planet Strike continues Blake's pursuit of Dr. Goldfire and this mutant army. Not only did it introduce more levels, more weapons, and more monsters, Planet Fire also included a fully functional automap feature, a handy too for those who tended to get lost in the mazelike levels. It's a more than worthy conclusion to an awesome as hell duology, and it definitely earns its place in this fine compilation.
When you take these three classic games and compare them to the stale FPS games of this generation, it becomes quite clear that a helluva lot more consideration was put into the level design and gameplay back in the days of yore. These three oldschool masterpieces gain massive amounts of replayability from the fact that back then the devs took time to design secrets and challenges to keep players coming back for more, unlike today's cookie cutter cinematic borefests. Another thing that is clear is how much time and effort Interceptor put into polishing these gems so that they shine on modern PCs. They are all lovingly wrapped in a DosBox-based frontend, and run natively in widescreen from the get go, no need for fiddling around with configuration to get these oldschool beauties running. They've even thrown in the original Rise of The Triad soundtrack, and the Extreme RoTT expansion at no extra cost. So what are you waiting for? Go get this primo can of whoopass!

Massive improvement over GTA 4 in many respects. There's still plenty of room for improvement however.
Likes:
+ Great variety of vehicles including bikes, cars, armoured vehicles, helis and aircraft
+ Some of the vehicles sound pretty decent, and engine noise is linked directly to RPM rather than being a looping audio effect (SaintsRow3)
+ First person driving is really awesome, shame you can't change FOV though
+ Mouse/Keyboard commands for driving are actually really good and i've not been using my controller at all
+ Vehicle handling is much more fun imo than GTA4
Dislikes
- Total lack of crouch button in exchange for horrible cover system, still can't go prone
- Clunky controls
- Sluggish and unresponsive movement animations, which I guess were created like that deliberately for immersion but suck for gameplay
- Combat is not the greatest; enemies take way too much damage, including direct headshots, they always zerg rush you and they're super accurate even when you or they are moving at high speed
- Radio stations are absolute trash imo - of course subjective but these ones are of very poor quality unless you like pop music. Vice City is vastly superior in this regard.
- Lack of custom character in single player, lack of female character in single player, lack of body customization in either single or online mode
- Police in this game are horrendous, there's far too many of them, they have infinite spawns including helicopters, they zerg rush you like absolute morons and they home in on  you when you're hiding yet should have no idea you were there.
In summary this is well worth the money at the sale price. Decent story but you're forced to use the characters they designed and are forced to use specific characters to progress the storyline. Online is fun but kinda low population nowadays it seems.

I love this game soo much. It's no replacement for the Famed Super Smash Bros., But it's a close 2nd. Super Smash has always been one of my fav games to play growing up, and Brawlhalla is the "it" game bringing it to the PC.
Sadly, they (creators) keep trying to forcibly add this awful "dash" mechinic replacing dodge and it's awful, useless and until they rework it...they've legit made the game UNPLAYABLE.
Expect some stiffness, while grounded weak attacks don't offer as much mobility and angling as Super smash. Ex: Don't expect to be able to hit Up, down, Left, or Right with a basic (weak) attack and it actually hit in those directions.
The jumping mechanics are nice, with some bugs and issues, but it's still a new game Beta testing and growing.
Some critiques have:
1: You have to pick up your weapons (which is fine) but the design of the pickup is generic. Seeing how each toon wields two weapons, it would be nice if the generic sword had color assosations. Ex: Blue means primary weapon while Red means secondary.
2: Even though you can buy "Skin Sets" with a toon outfit and 2 weapons, I wish you could also choose to buy the weapons seperately as well. I also wish the "base" skins that the toons start off with were also added to the "archival" collection so anyone else can use those skins as well.
3: The prices and items are a bit steep, so dont expect reasonable prices to get a collections of items. They only offer preset amounts you can buy which also sucks. I wish they added a custom amount where you could type in any amount you wanna get while still offering the presets.
4: They resently disabled completing dailies through custom play which I think personally stinks.
5: Community wise, the creators don't seem very customer friendly or socially available to the fans who play it.
6: They have a great selection of maps, but I wish they added custom map building.
7: I wish when you played 2v2 ranked or generic "online play" (1v1v1v1) Only the Big maps were selected.
Overall though, I enjoy the ever expanding selection of toons similar to League or Smite. I enjoy the multiple different play styles. There's still some map selection/game options that can be worked out a little better, but great game.
I would totally recommend this game to anyone interested in that Super Smash style. But don't expect it to play as smooth as Super Smash.

The 80's was a trippy time - drug use was commonplace, evreything was rainbow-coloured, and lazers were an essential component of one's daily diet.
is very much a game from that era, made for today's audience. It's a window into the 80's culture, and what a fantastic time those people lived in.
The best way to describe this game is: Sgt. Rex Power Colt (yep) is on acid and thinks he's a Cyborg super-soldier. He runs around an island, shooting robotic soldiers and savig the world from an evil guy who wants to blow up the world. You've seen it all before - it's every 80's action movie rolled into one. It's so cliche that it makes red roses and heart-shaped chocolates on Valentine's Day look like a fresh idea. But that's where the beauty in this game lies - it embraces the cliche. Sgt. Rex Power Colt (yes, I will type that out in full every time) spits out awful one-liners every couple of minutes. And yes, there is the essential "damsel in distress" - her name's Dr. Darling. And yes, her and Sgt. Rex Power Colt do have sex.
The tihing that makes this game truly awesome, though, is that it is very much a Far Cry game. There is an open-world to explore, there are wild animals to kill (including Blood Dragons; essentially big dinosaurs that shoot lazers, because lazers), you can ambush enemies patrolling the wild, and there are multiple ways to approach each objective. So therefore, because
simply builds on the winning formula of
, the only fault one could really find witht the game is that it's too short, or perhaps too easy due to it's over-the-top ridiculousness (remember, you're a Cyborg super-soldier). If Ubisoft Montreal could have some more spare time, it would be wonderful if they could push out some more of these - something with swords and castles really should be on the cards next, in my opinion. mod can make fun of fantasy films like
makes fun of 80's action films, I don't think I'll ever need to play another video game again.

While I think Deus Ex: Mankind Divided (MD) is in many ways worth playing, I cannot in good faith offer a glowing recommendation. And this hurts me to do.
The full potential of the game remains locked up. The detail, beauty, and realism of it is indeed breathtaking; hours upon hours can be spent just exploring the rich environments; and the numerous side-quests available to players run deep and are intriguing -- maybe even as interesting if not more so than the main story itself.
However, there's a lot that MD leaves wanting. A lot. If players have experienced the awesome and ambitious previous release in the franchise, Deus Ex: Human Revolution (HR), they will be very disappointed with MD by contrast. I'll mention just two general examples (general enough to avoid any spoilers): (1) HR offers numerous, highly memorable, diverse and beautiful locations to visit; and (2) the story along with its conclusion is epic. MD does not deliver in either of these respects.
(1) While the main hub in Prague is rich, the player will spend nearly all his time there; MD is unfortunately highly localized there. The player will likely feel that s/he hardly leaves the city, which can in turn make the player feel that s/he is not really participating in an exciting global journey that concerns the fate of the whole world like in HR.
(2) The conclusion of MD does not live up at all to that of HR. The main mission at the end of the game, while very exciting in its own right, is also highly localized. By that I mean that the stakes of mission feel like very small potatoes compared to the global stakes at play in HR. Admittedly, it is of course difficult to conceive of how to top the epic ending of HR, but the conclusion of MD by contrast is abrupt and anti-climactic, only to leave the player feeling seriously unsatisfied -- feeling a sort of empty accomplishment that is completely absent in the masterpiece that is HR.
(In it's favor, however, one thing that I found notable about MD compared to HR are a few of the very heart-wrenching moral dilemmas that you are placed in within the game. Kudos for that.)
I seriously hope the makers of MD come out with something like a "part 2" DLC that will complete the game properly, but I won't hold my breath.

The Sims as a whole has always had some stability issues, if you accidentally find the trigger. The game itself has a stability issue over time. If you play in one neighborhood and let it grow, i.e let Sims reproduce, have new families added to the town, etc. you may eventually encounter so called "lag spikes". It's something comparable to your screen freezing, but only for 1-3 seconds, while the sound continues to work, the world will freeze shortly. These lag spikes are going to occur at a certain point, once your neighborhood is "full". There is no limit in theory, yes, but once there are too many entities in an actively progressing neighborhood, you will see that the game starts to have issues with that. Trust me, this is not a problem about your hardware being outdated, it is the poor coding and entity clearing/resetting of the game. I suggest keeping the amount of neighborhood sims and families to a lower level. Remember, you can always force them to die, either on a natural way, or through the debug console!
Can't fix your neighborhood, but at least want to keep your family with their house? Copy the entire household with building, then delete your neighborhood in the main menu and create a new one. You can then add the copy of your original family + house to any new neighborhood, regardless which map you picked and the game will run fluently again!
Not all are really good in content, value and stability, as I've figured through research and opinions from friends. I suggest the following for the best content and most fluent gameplay in combination with other expansions: Seasons, Supernatural, Pets and Generations. You won't need any other, in my opinion. Island Paradise should be completely ignored, it's known to be one of the most problematic ones.
: The more expansions you buy and the more DLC you add to the main game, the more unstable it will become! This is no joke, even if your computer is "overkill" for this game, the game will still♥♥♥♥♥♥itself. Blame the developers...
I suggest to research the web with Google to find free downloadable content such as maps, hair styles, clothes and items, since Origin is one greedy crowd of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Takes you less than 5 minutes. Check out the blogs of Sims gamers, since any other kind of site will most likely add a virus to your file - that includes downloads from Youtube video descriptions too!
Personally I play on a high-end machine, which is why I do not encounter the casualties of hardware compatibility problems. In case you have some, focus on having a good processor and video card (graphics card). 4k RAM is enough if you don't run anything else and 4k RAM is the least people own nowadays - the very least. If yours is above the "minimum" suggested by the developer, but your game feels sloppy and performs badly, you may make changes in the games settings for improvements. Alternative you may have to upgrade your hardware or buy a new PC if you can't do that by yourself. However, it's Sims we are talking about and a good processor should do the job.
You can lower the graphics settings tremendously in this game, which will help you a lot if playing on an older PC. Additionally you may turn off the active neighborhood progression setting in the game options. Then your neighborhood is not going to "play" in the background and will only change if you are in range of these Sims.
The modding / content creator community of Sims 3 is overall better and bigger as far as I've figured. Maybe it is because the game created a bigger boom when it came out unlike Sims 4.
I've always been a fan of this simulation series, and have played the following Sims games (in the same order): The Sims Bustin' Out, UrbZ Sims in the City, The Sims (1), The Sims 2, The Sims 3. I've never played Sims 4 due to obviously bad reviews, and I suggest you shouldn't either. All of the Sims games that I've played over the years, through my childhood up to being an adult myself, they were all great in their own way, but unfortunately none was perfect.
I hope that one day the developers will decide to actually create a quality Sims, that covers all of the most wanted features for the fans, without ruining the performance.

This is childhood nostalgia in the making.
PROS ABOUT THE GAME.
If you're a huge fan of the ORIGINAL Star Wars Battlefront, SOCOM, and of course....Army Men, then this game is your personal porn stash of glory. Using the unreal engine, this awesome game of plastic green vs tan toy soldiers is beyond expectations. It does not involve any kind of ranking system to unlock anything, nor does it include pay to win options. All weapons are available and is a jump in and jump out of based games. This game is a rare jewel among the pile of coal for video games and if you need that awesome replayable value of a game, then this is the choice. I will definitely be listing this game as one of my top 10 choices of 2015.
(Cons listed below)
PROS
- Beautiful Maps
- Smooth Animation
- Awesome Music
- Replayable Value
CONS ABOUT THE GAME
Certain suggestions for the game I would recommend is additional animations for the army men. RPG's blow up the soldiers into bits which is cool. However, it would be amazing if the fire from flame-throwers could melt you, or have bullets and pellets from rifles and shotguns blow chunks off of your character to show a more cool reaction from shooting/fighting. Dodging animation into walls/objects sometimes have clipping issues and camera glitches where your camera is forced into different directions. Another issue that is a bit unsettling is random loud audio popping noises that happen throughout the game. Makes it a bit unsettling for the ears. Also, another suggestion would be for the RPG's. They do not cause self-inflicted damage like grenades do when shooting at an opponent at point blank range. Although it has a cool down timer per use, it allows a disadvantage for an opponent to run into the middle of a squad to shoot the ground and kill everyone except himself. Other than that though, this game is epicly amazing.
CONS
- Loud Popping Noises With Audio Randomly Throughout Matches
- Dodge Animation Sometimes Has Clipping and Forced Camera Moving Errors.
- AOE Self-Inflicted Damage Should be Applied to RPG's.
- Needs more dynamic deaths for your character models depending on weapons.
Anyways, i'll be playing this more on my show for Twitch. Check out the live broadcasts here :D.

I play WRC 6 with a T500 RS wheel and a TH8A sequential shifter, purely in cockpit view with maxed out graphic settings and in Simulation mode, i.e. will all assists off.
In the past I played DiRT Rally for more than 200 hours but really got bored at some point by its lack of content in terms of variety and amount of rally stages.
Please find below my list of pros and cons for WRC 6:
++ Big variety of stages
++ Comparatively big amount of stages. I think it will take quite long for me to memorize any stage.
++ Good sensation of speed including increasing car instability at very high speeds
+ Different road surfaces make a big difference in the amount of grip and the required braking distances. Loss of grip on icy sections or through ponds of water is quite credible.
+ Good FFB right out of the box
+ Good sound. Although I must admit that nowadays cars sound quite "meh".
+ I like the way flat tyres are simulated.
+ On sunny days the light effects are quite nice.
+ Credible physics in simulation mode (in my layman opinion)
o I don't like the German co-driver. Luckily the British one is quite ok.
- Only today's WRC cars available. No classics :-(
- Bad balance of AI strength between different rally events. On difficulty level "Difficult" in the WRC I managed to win a couple of rallies while at others I did not stand a chance without making any major mistakes and once was even worse than most of the WRC 2 drivers.
- The road surface is almost entirely flat without any potholes or significant camber. Especially the latter point is way better in DiRT Rally.
- Some rally events contain the same stage multiple times, and this so only in the same direction. Why no reverse direction?
And last but not least the most annoying points, which make this game sometimes really unlikable for me:
-- At the Super Special Stages, where you are racing directly against another opponent, this other car's engine is louder than your own car's engine. This is quite annoying if you are using manual gear shift and would like to shift according to your engine's rev sound.
-- The image brightness in the game is generally way too dark. Since the game does not provide a gamma correction or brightness feature in the graphics settings, the only way tweak the brigthness is via the monitor's settings. Even on sunny summer stages at midday you sometimes can get the feeling of driving in the twilight. What makes things worse is that the car's headlights have a felt reach of only about 5 metres in front of your car. Foggy stages or stages at night time are like a blind flight and thus become a real pain to drive. Under such weather conditions I don't stand a chance against the AI's stage times.
-- On some gravel stages the windscreen gets more and more dirty over time. This, in general, could have been a quite nice and immersive feature. But it is not: the screen gets dirty quite quickly even on straight sections under dry conditions. On twisty sections it's even worse so that I sometimes drive with my wipers active all the time, which is quite ridiculous under dry weather conditions and even more annoying in combination with the game's already quite bad overall brightness.
-- The cockpit view offers 5 different camera positions with varying distances to the windscreen. For some cars (like the Polo) there is only one position where it's actually possible to see the gear indicator all the time. For other cars another position may have to be configured in order to see the gear indicator. At the same time the broad sun protection strip at the top of the windscreen makes the already dark road environment even darker. So there may be no perfect camera position where you can see at the same time the gear indicator and where the sun protection strip disturbs you the least.
After having just finished a Rally Portugal event under mostly very frustrating visibility conditions, I am quite annoyed at the moment and give WRC 6 a rating of 6 out of 10.
Update on 2017-01-07: After having permanently switched from cockpit to bonnet view some of the aforementioned negatives are no longer disturbing so that I change my rating to a 7 out of 10.

Do you like RPGs? Like, real RPGs, with a large world, plenty of characters, factions, and most importantly decisions that have REAL consequences?!? Then this game is for you!
Mount & Blade: Warband is an open world, sandbox RPG that turns you loose in a fictional yet highly realistic medieval world. Pick your backstory from a list of mix/match options of your choosing (be careful though! These can either help or hinder your in-game progress depending!), then begin your adventure towards fame or infamy! Lordship or degeneracy! (The important thing is YOU get to CHOOSE!)
Throughout the game you will come across many villages, towns, forts and cities along with bandits, renegades, vassles and Kings (with their armies) and it is up to you to create allegiances or enemies. Gather a band of merry men and grow it into an army of your own! Buy land, marry into royalty, become a King!
Mount & Blade is just as much a strategy game as it is an RPG. Command your troops on the battlefield, manage and upgrade your properties, buy and sell goods in the dynamic economy. Know that every decision you make has consequences, so plan and manage accordingly!
Pros:
-Immersive
-Large world
-Plenty of quests, missions and possible outcomes
-Living dynamic world
-Make-your-own storyline
-intuitive combat system
-Highly addicive gameplay
Neutral:

-Travelling sequences can feel long and drawn out
Cons:
-Dated graphics/animations
-Clunky UI at times
Overall Score: 8/10

I'm pretty happy I was able to play this. It felt like fresh Half-Life content came back for a brief moment.
Transmissions: Element 120 throws you into the unknown. You don't know who you are, why are you here, what's your goal. Your incentives are your own. Your methods, well...
There's a couple new mechanics (some aesthetic, some functional) you can explore in a couple levels. The one that stands out the most - a modified gravity gun, allowing you to rocket-jump and a bit more. Although, there's more to find before you get there. I particularly liked neon text in the dark. Charging it with a flashlight was subtle, but smart. A pretty little detail, really.
Level design is, for the most part, good. It looked pretty, it played fairly well
, though I must admit, there was a place or two where I got stuck on, because I couldn't find the place I had to go through. Looking at you, vents.
To be fair, though, the scripting was pretty decent. AI seemed to know what it was doing, even with the environment. Striders ducked under obstacles to get a shot on me, and they were definitely able to barrage walls.
I do have to mention a bug in the physics concerning destructable walls
, and I had no idea if I could change my difficulty (visual bug - I didn't see any changes after clicking in the difficulty options), but it's a free game. I don't expect triple-A title quality. (besides, some high-profile games recently have been riddled with bugs on release. I feel like a bug or two in a free game isn't something deal-breaking.)
If I'd rate a regular game, this'd get a solid 7.5/10 - Short and imperfect, but smart, and it sure felt like Half-Life.
The low - I mean, no - price-tag makes it a 9/10, though.
If you've got an hour or so to spare, check it out. It's a 1.7GB download.

you can play with up to 16 players locally (or with bots) in a tournament that is very great for when you are having a party. In
you can duel with other players.
In
you can also play Memory, which is basically an increasing amount of button prompts that you have to remember. The player who remembers all of them or that makes the least amount of mistakes wins. This game mode was very damn fun, especially when you get to 9 or more buttons to remember.
The AI is very easy to beat in the standard mode, unless you are playing against the Very Hard bot: he presses every button extremely fast, and he won't make a single mistake, so if you want a good challenge offline I recommend playing with him. Also, playing Memory against the AI is just too weird, and I recommend having a human player to play it with.
The soundtrack is amongst the best of western video games, bringing you back in time, making you feel nostalgic and never feeling derivative. The voice acting of the narrator is a spot-on Sam Elliot impersonator, and the sound effects of the guns are great.
There is plenty of replayability here: beating
is not an easy task, and if you have friends that come over you can play four or five rounds in about two or three minutes total. There are also 25 Steam achievements to unlock, and, with the addition of Steam Workshop support, more duelists to play with and more stages to battle on.
Overall,
is an excellent party game that works very well as a single player experience. For its very cheap price of 5$ I highly recommend this game to pretty much everyone. Being their first game, the guys at Bandit-1 have a long road ahead...

Western Press is Bandit-1’s first ever game on Steam while it is publisher Surprise Attack’s tenth. This time around they’ve delivered one of the most ingenious games that I have played this year in a gun toting wild west game that will be all over in a matter of seconds. The concept isn’t new it’s the delivery that is. Players – and you can play as a single player against a competitive AI –  aim to beat a row of controller presses as quickly as possible. It’s a wild west shoot out as the quickest to ‘draw’ is the winner just as it was back in the days of the wild west partner.
There’s not a whole lot to the game – the above is what you do – but the presentation makes the game addictive. The presentation with the setting is what makes the game. If you’ve ever wanted to know what it’s like to virtually have a quick draw at high noon then this is your opportunity. The game quickly becomes addictive – even playing against the AI – and you will find yourself playing round after round given that they are so short (less than five seconds and highly likely under three when or if you become proficient enough at the game). I appreciated the art work and the overall narration. I thought that they were terrific additions to the game and key components in what makes the game addictive. The characters have great senses of humor.
The game is newbie friendly but as great games are it is insanely difficult to master. I have yet to complete the skills challenges (the player Vs AI part of the game) because it just gets too darn quick for my reflexes which I thought were fine. I get to the 2.5 second level and that’s about the best that I can muster. I’d really love to see gameplay videos of the very best players. I think it would be insane. The way that the game has been designed leaves it very open for tournaments – which is, in fact, a primary multiplayer component of the game.
I have yet to play using keyboard controls but I’ve seen reports that they need to be tweaked a little bit. I believe that the game was clearly made to be played with a controller as those controls are fantastic. This might impact your play if you don’t have any controllers.
The game has been Steamified with trading cards and achievements. There is cross-platform support for the game which should enrich the multiplayer experience.
I loved my time with Western Press and look forward to arranging a local multiplayer tournament for the game soon.

I played Far Cry 3 and loved it.  I saw this on the horizon, and to be honest, I thought it'd be awful: a gimmicky tie-in that looked absolutely ridiculous.  And it is absolutely ridiculous.  But it is impossibly well executed!  Don't get me wrong, Far Cry 3 was a fantastic game but there were things that made the game just a wee bit tedious at times - impossibly sensitive fall damage, some skills that just seemed pointless, swimming sections.
Blood Dragon streamlines all the realism (because this game leaves all reason at the door) in favor of making the game fun.  The plot is ridiculous and a lovely send-up of all those glorious 80s sci-fi/action movies - and who better to provide the voice for the main character than 80s action hero luminary, Michael Biehn (see: Terminator, Aliens)?  He's more grizzled here in the distant future of 2013 (when the game came out), but holy crap, he is phenomenal with the voice work and his one-liners and dialogue that he delivers throughout the game make it so much more viscerally enjoyable to run around like a commando - scratch that, CYBER Commando - all over the island.  Yeah, you're on an island like in Far Cry 3 and this one's much smaller, has an 80s VHS tracking haze that I'm not complaining about because it goes with the theme, and everything is muted or neon.  Why? Because it's awesome, that's why.  If you don't understand that perhaps you and your haughty airs might enjoy a nice quiet evening listening to NPR.
So yeah, fall damage is gone, you can breathe forever in water and run pretty much as fast as you could drive a car making getting around the island a breeze.  The enemy types are a bit lacking since they basically fall into the categories of 1) palette-swapped wild animals from FC3, 2) Motocross guy with an assault rifle 3) Welder-mask guy with molotovs 4) Heavy weapons guy with a minigun or flamethrower or 5) the eponymous blood dragons.   And while there's some gauntlets and set-piece missions you'll play through, there aren't really any 'boss fights' to speak of unless you count fighting blood dragons or conquering outposts.
Those are really the only negatives I experienced in this game and they don't detract too much from the fun you have playing an avatar of death known as Rex 'Power' Colt.  Play Far Cry 3, appreciate the beauty and realism and survival challenge.  After you do that, play this game for the fun and sense of empowerment as all of Jason Brody's weaknesses are eliminated for the sake of having a good old 80's action movie complete with cheesy but fun dialogue, 16-bit cutscenes, and dinosaurs that shoot lasers out of their eyes.

ok.. let's see if i can explain this... this is a metaphor.... this game is the offspring you would get if a fat cow and a ♥♥♥♥♥ mated.. it is a fat cow ♥♥♥♥♥ of a game... for example.. lets say you started to play and oh look everyone is playing tf2 right now.. lets save and quit... good luck bro... it literally takes takes 5 minutes... save.. now you have to LOAD the main menu.. thats a minute... then escape/quit... it seems immediate.. but wait... i cant do anything... my hard drive is spinning like a motherf... and i cant click anything on my desktop.... this will happen for upwards of 4 minutes....
ok so that's a little taste... now let's actually play the game... wow this is fun... exploring and hacking and looting woo.. good times... wait we have to go to prague now.. cool... *goes to subway/travels* we're talking a 3 minute load for the next area... good grief... fine.. we loaded it... run around looting.. exploring.. hacking.. missions... then what happens is this gradual decline in frames per second.... now first of all i didnt tell you what the fps was to begin with... we're not getting +60fps or even 50fps.. we were running at 40ish fps... and when you're used to always having 60+ all the time it takes getting used to... ok so we're not talking 40fps now.. we're talking 35 dropping to the teens back up to 45 down to the teens... its like mud sometimes and its aggravating.. it gets progressively worse the longer you play... not to mention this is the quintessential save scum type of game... oh crap that dude saw me... load quicksave.. go... again... again... so you're just adding layer upon layer of sloth... eventually it gets to the point where you want to just reboot your pc...

The hours that Steam has logged as me playing this game do not equal the amount of hours I have put into this game.  This is through no fault of Steam, I started playing LotRO around 3.5 years ago, and was not using Steam for part of that, and I can tell you that my hour count probably is closer to 1,000.  That should be a good indicator of what I think of this game.
If that is not enough, then let me simply go off on a paragraph or two of love for this game.
I have tried other F2P MMOs out there, jumping here and there, but none of them really did it for me.  They were all missing something, or some things, and I couldn't quite put my finger on it.  Then, one winter break, my brother sent me an IM, telling me we should give it a go, it looked like fun.  Again, that was 3.5 years ago.  I haven't looked back, and I will be forever grateful to him for introducing me to this game.
For starters, the game is fairly true to its word, it is Free to Play.  There are many players who have gone through the entire game content, buying quest packs, expansions, and fun little extras without paying a cent in real money.  The game allows players oppertunities to "earn" turbine points, the buyable currency, through the completion of "deeds," little meta quests.  In order to look "cool" within the game, one only needs to complete a few skirmishes, or take a browse through the auction house to aquire neat looking gear.  Want a horse?  No problem.  The player initially uses turbine points to buy the riding trait from the store, but upon the creation of your first character (perhaps even on each server, not simply first account character), you are granted 100 tp to buy this skill.  Afterwards, one can purchase nearly ever horse availible within the game using the in game currency of gold, silver, and copper.  Long story short, the game does not bar players from looking great, getting around as fast as their companions, and joining their companions in their adventures, simply because they don't want to shell out some cash.
Secondly, the content is really nice.  Everyone has their least favorite areas (ugh, Lone Lands...), but the way the story plays out and takes you through zones is really fun!  Within the game, you are not riding alongside the Fellowship, but working in other parts of the world, because there are more things happening than just the discover of the One Ring.  The main story line (or Epic Quest, Book Quests, ect) is interesting and enthralling, and you will find yourself getting caught up in certain places, feeling for the characters you meet (the end of the Shadows of Angmar books is a doozy, watch your step!).  Along side the epic quests are side quests, like most games, which are equally interesting and often provide a deeper look into the lore of Middle Earth, and a closer look at the story of Lord of the Rings.
But I think the most...wonderful, really, part of LotRO is how it looks.  It is perfect.  Visually stunning even in the early zones, and outragiously beautiful as you get to the most recently released areas, it is easy to simply spend time roaming around the fields of Bree, bundling up and sliding down an icy hill in Forochel, or poking around dark corners in Moria.  There are tiny details everywhere, and it all seems to be carefully considered and designed, and is a vision of Middle Earth that I am more than happy to adopt as my default.  There are so many hidden nooks and crannies, little scenes, and secrets to find, and it's well worth it to just take a day to wander and forget about questing.
I think, in the end, that's what really keeps me coming back to LotRO.  It's a game that has a solid amount of everything.  Exploration, crafting, roleplay, raiding.  The community is wonderful, I've made so many friends, and I cannot recommend this game highly enough.
If you have any more questions, or want to see screenshots from the game, head over to
.  I hope to see you in Middle Earth!

Overall, one of the best Deus Ex games of the series.
The gameplay mechanics are the best of any of the four main series games (granted this would be the case when compared to deus ex or invisible war). Combat is much improved and stealth is just as good if not better than HR.
The story is not as grand as the previous games and its sudden end has annoyed alot of people. It's not so much of a cut to black, just the execution seemed poor.
Its not a short game by any means. I clocked in at 30ish hours, that was on a pacifist run and doing all the sidemission (that I found).
I would compare this game to mass effect two if HR was the only other game of the series. Much like ME2 (when it first came out), this game has the best gameplay mechanics, much improved graphics, smaller scale story and an ending that  felt a little rushed and making you want more.
It is definitely a game that is worth buying. However the DLC and possibly the season pass is something to think twice about. So far the DLC released is a bit short for my liking, though they have introduced some new mechanics which are awesome.

Starting off from release, the game ran like thick molasses on a cold day. But I will say this has improved drastically in my case with the DX-12 beta release. The game runs an average 55fps on max settings on my rig, I'll drop the specs below. Otherwise, if you played Human Revolution and liked it, you'll probably enjoy Mankind Divided. I sure enjoyed myself, but I can't deny the game does nothing to really blow your mind. The control scheme between key/mouse and gamepad, in this case an Xbox 360 controller, is pretty much the same. However it's polished. Combat and stealth both are much more fluid and the overall mechanics feel tuned as good as they can be.
However these improvements don't deny the games shoddy port to PC with terrible performance during the first couple weeks until a patch comes out that may solve the issue for a number of people, but not all. Bugs haunt the game as well, though most are very minor in my experience, having done two full playthroughs. Only a few game breakers came along which resulted in either simply reloading a checkpoint to having to start a new game entirely. Luckily, these game breakers occurred very early in the game and never came back up during my playtime after some graphics tweaking.
On the whole of the matter, I'd say Mankind Divided is a good game. Not great 'nor a pile of steaming♥♥♥♥♥♥ but good. It's a competent game which sets a well detailed (but questionable story) which barely manages to stand on its own baring the fact that once the story seems in full swing, the climax seems sudden and you're left a bit confused. I'd recommend the game if you're already a fan of the series and enjoyed the previous title Human Revolution. Just be wary that your computer is somewhat up to date. This game isn't for potatoes.

Just finished my first play through. I enjoyed the game quite a bit. I didn't really touch on many side quests but the main story kept me interested. It's silly to see all of these negative reviews come through due to the DLC situation. I'm not really upset about it. The ending wasn't the best and yes, you can clearly see that there's more on the way. That's exciting though.
I understand how game companies can be put under stress and pressure to put out games earlier and it is what it is. Games are getting more expensive to produce yet we're still paying the same price for years and years. A game company is not a charity. It's a company. Something has got to give somewhere. So it doesn't bother me. I'm okay with paying more for games at this point. Heck, I paid more for N64 games back when they could get up to $70-$80. So again, the pricing and overall package is fine by me. I knew what I was getting into before I bought the game.
The overall feel to the game is what truly makes it shine. The presentation is pretty solid. The mechanics are a little iffy. I don't know why but the game felt strange playing with a mouse and keyboard. It seems rather floaty. So I switched over to my controller. No need for precision here, so no worries.
Overall, I feel pretty positive about this game and I would recommend the game for anyone who enjoyed Human Revolution. It's a competent shooter with a few RPG aspects.
If I could put a number on this game I would give is a solid 8/10. I'm looking forward to seeing how the DLC plays out and the next few iterations.

If you are actually "in-the-know" of gaming communities or have at least played enough games you will likely understand the humor otherwise most of the game will likely go over your head. Overall, a very enjoyable sit back and have a few chuckles game with decent 2D scrolling coin collecting to make it well worth its cheap price point.

Honestly, This game is almost perfect.
This game is great for those who like Super Smash Bros. Brawlhalla
is one of those games where it's gonna last a while before anyone gets
bored of it. (as you can tell I have 230 hours sooo...)
The game handles great, you have a variety of moves you can do with each
character and weapon, and the controls are pretty easy to use. You can use
a controller if you really want to also.
The game has lots of great gamemodes you can use. Strikeout.
Brawlball, Snowbrawl. Etc, etc. If you want to start gaining competition
you can go into ranked and start gaining ELO or play with a friend
and do 2v2's ranked.
The animations are great. The animation have a very smooth look to them,
if you do a move it looks like they meant to put every string of moves together
and get a combination of animations.
You can buy skins, taunts, and KO effects from the store. You can pay real
money for in-game things, like mammoth coins (which you use to buy everything).
I know what your thinking, "So it's pay to win?" No it's not. Everything you buy in
the game is cosmetic, if you buy something like a KO effect, whenever you kill
him (or her) then off the screen causes an explosion or something. It all depends on
skill and how good you are at the game.
The developers are very into the community and care what you think. They
add a new character every month, and a balance update every 2 weeks. I won't
forget to mention all the holiday updates and skins you can get whenever a new
holiday comes around.
The only bad thing I have noticed about this game is whenever your playing
ranked, you always run into the saltiest person you could imagine. They completely
ruin all the fun you are having when they say "Wow, your trash." or something.
All in all, I would say it's a super great game with benevolent developers
that are always trying to add something to the game.
9/10 Would waste 230 hours again.

Rise of the Triad itself is still surprisingly solid and fun, but like a lot of older first-person shooters, the bulk of the late-game maps tend to drag on far too long and the "puzzles" in them can become a bit too arbitrary and frustrating, involving too many key hunts and weirdo "press the hidden button on this wall" tricks that got old even in Doom.
I wouldn't call this pack or even Rise of the Triad essential. It's a fun curiosity, but the other games you know from this specific era of PC gaming are just better. Even Rise of the Triad's over-the-top nature isn't enogh to really make it stand the test of time like Doom, Duke 3D, and Quake have.

It's an even bigger departure from it's simulation namesake, however Red River still holds it's own as a decent squad based tactical shooter. The player retains the role of a USMC Fireteam Leader as they guide their fellow Marines and command them to complete the varied mission objectives thrown at them during the campaign.
Pros:
- Game offers a decent amount of tactical flexibaility with it's command system.
- Players will work alongside seperate AI Fireteams as part of a larger Squad, making the player feel a part of a larger war effort.
- Friendly AI now have their own personality, the voice acting is much less robotic than previous games and the natural banter increases immersion.
-The new voice acting comes with a script full of excessive swearing and less than politically correct comments. It may be confronting at first but I feel it is a realistic and accurate representation of military banter, adds to the immersion and makes the player feel like they're part of a human squad of soldiers.
- Players can now unlock new weapons and equipment, and customise their loadout prior to each mission.
Cons:
- Missions are more linear than the previous game.
- AI still occasionaly glitch or bug out.
- Lack of Mission Editor (a staple of the series) hinders replayabilty.
- The new voice acting comes with a script full of excessive swearing and less than politically correct comments. I personally have no problem with this as I found it to be an accurate depiction of military banter, but some players may find this uncomfortable.
I can reccomend this game for players looking for a more thought based shooter. While it's not as in depth as it's predecessors or rival series (ArmA) it still requires a little bit of patience and strategy to survive the firefights in this campaign.

This game is seriously one of the most unpleasant experiences I have had in a game. Most of it is perfectly fine, a nice little romp through the idyllic nordic countryside. There are some interesting and exciting settings, the brothers can interact with just about everything and you really get a feel for the world and the characters. It never really reached the level of the hype, but I was enjoying it. Besides the ungodly upper body strength of two children, nothing really stood out as exciting or awful.
The problem comes from the final experience of the game. No spoilers, but for a game that prides itself on no cutscenes, the game completely takes any semblance of choice away from you and forces you through a series of incredibly stupid actions. There's no way to avoid them, no way to just walk the other direction. There isn't even a cutscene to force the character to perform the actions.
Then the game punishes you in the cutscene for actions that are unavoidable. There's some "heart-wrenching" final action where you are forced through another series of unpleasant actions to show growth or something.
Considering how much people mock "Press F to pay respects", I don't see how this game got the critical acclaim it did.

I like rally, I like official content. This game gives you both, so I am satisfied with it. Real drivers, real cars (well done models), nice tracks - the Super Special Stages are really made 1:1 like in reality, the rest of Special Stages is fictional, however, I noticed they include some well known elements taken from real tracks, like Colin's Crest, Portugal Fafe's jump, Catalonia donuts, harpin etc. This is nice that those places are recognizable in game. Those tracks are narrow and bumpy, some are short sprints, some of them are over 10km long and take over 8 min to finish.  Some tracks miss curvature on gravel corners (are bit too flat) in my opinion, but generally stage design is very nice. You got standard career, "from zero to hero", with many nice flavors in it. Repairing your car, gravel/tarmac/snow setup settings, tires, everything is here. What is strange, I found there is no WRC 3 class in career, nor in whole game (there are: WRC Junior, WRC 2 and WRC).
However, there is almost as many disadvantages as advantages. Generally the framerate in game is quite decent. Even on my lower-end PC it runs on about 40 fps (low settings) which is great, but huge part ofcommunity suffers from suttering - freezig game for splitseconds (sometimes after that game speeds up to compensate time - depending how long freeze was) This is unacceptable in rally game, when 1 second of stutter makes you go off road, straight into a tree.
Devs realased a patch which should fix it, for some it does, for others it does not. I am in the second half of community in that case. At the beggining, for about 2 weeks after realase devs have been contacting players as they said "to make their product better" (such phrases appeared on almost every post) after what, they realased couple patches which did not introduce significant improvements. They just patch some critical bugs, which should never appear in final realase game. Also it is worth to say - first of them was critical patching for people who couldn't run game on realase day because of error - I was in those group agin. Now, on 8th of November - developers are keeping silent for around 3 weeks (last patch - 18th of October) leaving game unplayable for some people - some wheels doesn't work while they should - supported equipment list says that. However there is a slight chance they are keeping silent because working on patches, but I don't really belive (if it comes to be true and patch will be realesed I will add EDIT on the end of the review). We all are waiting for stutter fix and camera angles fix - the cockpit view is hardly playable - you can't see the track sometimes through strange (small) windshield.
To end with - multiplayer mode is badly designed - 90% of time you will get "connection error" which is caused by missing online players waiting in lobby, which is radical, not having enough online players 1 month after realase. Only if you open your own lobby some people might join; come on, we got 2016 year... - that suggest the match-making feature is badly designed.
This is what I found playing this game and also as being a part of it's community. Maybe you won't encouter those problems but I did.
On the other hand, if the game would be free from huge stutters, (probably due to my low PC spec; it could run better because framerate is smooth), I could 100% enjoy it, and reccomend it as a rally enthusiast - and that is why I give it a positive note. But in such state decision belongs to you.

I like this game. It plays fine, kinda like the Smash Bros. games, but with a far higher emphasis on items, which are all pretty well balanced (you won't find any smash balls here), although it's a bit shallower than the previously mentioned series. All of the weapon styles' light attack are the same across their users, with their signature moves being unique for all the characters, with animations for each character that give them their own touch. It's simple to grasp, hard to master.
The game looks very nice, especially the backgrounds on different stages. I also like the animations - especially the heavy attacks. I would've prefered, though, if they were drawn frame by frame - you could give Asuri a gun and nobody who hasn't played her before would notice something is off - but I understand why they did them how they did.
Now, the players themselves... They can be pretty toxic, at least here in AU. Lots of players spam heavy attacks in 4 player Free For All (especially some Ember/Orion players), which admittedly, I did too a while ago. It can be pretty annoying. Things get better on 1v1 Strikeout, but here's where the toxicity comes in to play. While a lot of more skilled players will try to help you get better at the game, some others will simply call you bad and leave without saying anything else - it's kinda funny, to be honest. Some just get salty and call you a sig spammer even if you unbound your heavy attack button (it helps get a better understanding of light attacks, I swear I'm not dumb).
Overall, it's a pretty fun game, especially with friends - if they're not too busy playing League of Legends to play with you (definitely not projecting anything here).

I've played my fair share of MMOs from World of Warcraft to Global Agenda and each one had the same problem, I wasn't invested in the monotonous questing. LoTRO has found a way to breath energy into the questing by giving them purpose and a general sense of importance. There are just kill and collect quests but instead of filling the leveling experince with them they are used in the form of tasks to be completed for faction rep which makes them completely optional. The biggest difference i've found is i was mind numbly bored as i quested or dungeoned my way to multiple 90s in world of warcraft, with LoTRO i am parterning of with random people who are out for the same goals as me and when we finish a fellowship quest or a group suggested area we can break up again without feeling bad because thats how its built to work. On the other hand if you want to quest with a friend that is entirely possible and standard features like quest sharing are added to by the ability to see who in your fellowship (party) has completeled which quests or who is available for the quests. I am by no means at the end game content for the current expansion but with atleast six expansions already released there is hours of main quests let alone optional side areas and storylines. The game is Free to Play and through hard work you could unlock everything in the game for free, or if you just want to experince the core game and end game content quickly you can pay for membership that unlocks all the content for as long as you remain a member. As a member you will recieve turbine points and earn even more, these can be used to unlock content permanently even if you decide to end your membership.
Overall i would say the game is well worth trying and if possible make or bring friends to the game and increase the possibilities at your disposal.

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided, what did i think?
Note 1: I have never played any Deus Ex games before so i went into this completely unbiased.
Note 2: This review was influenced in format as you are able too tell by "The Black Hokage" i would suggest you go check out his review if you want a little more in depth or you just don't like to read.
[STORY From what i gathered and a little research:]  You play as Adam jensen in a cyberpunk themed dystopian world in 2029, after terrorist attacks commited by "augs" [the augmented/partly cyborg people] the naturals become afraid of the augs and jensen goes on a wild chase trying to find the people behind these attacks. The world is altered by many things like people fearing the augs and what they are capable of doing, Then you also have the mysterious illuminati in the backround. Again having not played any previous games you are able to watch a video before starting the game explaining everything that happened previous to this game, this was very helpful and allowed me to get some sort of understanding of the story here, and man is it such a great plot. You will go through the main and side missions on the edge of your seat wondering whats gonna happen next.
[CHOICES] This game allows you to really play how you want to play it has variation of dialouge that will pave your story but what i really thought this game excelled in was the different ways you can engage situations. This game allows you to go in completely stealth or guns blazing and i found each way to be equally as fun.
[EXPLORATION] Is a very big part of this game you may not even notice this at first but if you exolore you will find hiddden  airvents, Terminals,Passwords and more that will make the way you play unique and the way you get through places your own. Also there is much to explore outside of missions like being able to go through peoples apartments and living spaces which will allow you to find credits, supplies and read emails on computers that will give you a little inside on the persons life, and through out the game you will be able to unlock various upgrades to allow you to explore areas you were previous unable too.
[CHALLENGE] Is certainly an element in this game you will have to be strategic about every move you make cutting cameras, hacking terminals and computers to gain passwords and shut off turrets etc, this is helped in a pretty cool way by using emp rounds that will shut off cameras and other things too help you. Enemies will be different in the way that some enemies will be armored but they will all have a weakness for you to exploit. I played this game on a pretty normal difficulty and i can see how playing on a harder one can make you a little angry.
[OTHER] Something i really liked was that the game had an inventory allowing you to pack your own arsenal. The game also had a little variety when it comes to choice in weapons from pistols to rifles, to shotguns, to snipers it allows you too engage in different ways. The credit system was also something here this was basically the currency allowing you to buy ammo, weapons and lots of other things. The game also allows you to complete it without killing anybody by having stun guns, tranquilizers and allowing you to make people unconcious rather than killing them.
[CONS] The loading to different places through the "metro", it wasn't too long but after a couple times you will notice it. Game can be a little confusing at times. Im not really one to talk about graphics and audio so ill unfortunately have to let you guys be the judge of that. I thought the game was a little short as i completed the game in around 15 hours doing what i think were MOST not all side missions. The end was leaving me to want more leaving itself at an obvious cliff hanger. I would also have like the city to be a little bit bigger, i felt that the game had a lot more potential than what it had.
[CONCLUSION] The game has a very interesting world, Tons of choice including engagement options, allowed you to customize your character the way you want to with upgrades, has a good challenge. But it also had a little too long of loading screen, can get a little confusing at times, ending. I would recommend this game but not for 60 dollars, i think it may have been a little better at 30 to 40 dollar.

As the sequel to Human Revolutions, this game had high expectations. Although Mankind Divided doesn't quite meet the quality of its predecessor, it is hard to deny that this game is good in its own right. Mankind Divided improves on the gameplay of Human Revolution by the addition of new augs that enhance game play, and the expansion of the open-sector exploration aspect. The game contains a great deal of details, both in terms of graphical/level design and in-game text found by hacking computers and picking up pocket secretaries.
The greatest flaw of Mankind Divided is that the main story never wraps up, and is also quite a bit shorter than the main story in Human Revolution. The brevity of the main story gives off the impression of the game being a sequel hook. However, this factor alone does not warrant a negative review, because the game excels in the gameplay, the details and the sidequests.
A frequently cited criticism is the presence of microtransactions. However, the cash shop is purely optional. This game isn't that challenging, and the whole game can be easily completed with minimal augs/gear. If there is an in-game necessity to use microtransactions, it would be a different matter, but as it is, microtransactions aren't a big deal.
Game performance heavily strains mid- and low-end systems, so I hear, but there are graphics options. Although optimization leaves a bit to be desired, I would definitely not consider this game to poorly optimized (just underoptimized). I run with a GTX 1080, and play on high at 1440p, with a very stable framerate and the graphics look amazing. However, even if you set the graphics to low, the game looks really good even on the lower graphics settings.

There have been a few consistent complaints with the game, and I do understand where they're coming from.
- There's the complaint about microtransactions being in the Breach mode, but I haven't even touched it yet so it has very little relevance to me, and doesn't particularly bother me as a business practice, as loads of other gaming companies do it.
- The choppiness: this I actually do get, and it definitely does deter from the immersive experience, and is a little surprising that it happens in some areas sometimes, but not all the time. There doesn't seem to be a particular amount of consistency for it. Recommend high settings for GTX 970 cards and the like, runs at 60FPS almost always.
- The ending, to me, didn't seem like that much of a letdown. It was definitely a cliffhanger ending that's supposed to lead into the DLC, and I do have questions that remain unanswered, but it does make me want to get the DLC in order to find out the end of the story. I'm not a particularly big fan of this sort of thing, though, so this both a positive an a negative.
Positives:
- The graphics themselves are actually quite lovely, especially with the black lines removed, and there are a lot of toggleable options, allowing for better optimization and more specific tweaking
- The gameplay doesn't feel that clunky on the keyboard, and the controls didn't take much getting used to, with a little bit of customization, I had the cat in the bag
- Character design was quite good, and the whole environment itself has a mesh of realism, like what one might expect when visiting Prague, as well as the notorious HR-like jagged design on interiors and clothing. Important characters have distinct character design, and really do stand out in the world
- Difficulty-wise, sometimes I found the game too easy, but there are quite a few sections where it was challenging to get through it without killing anybody, especially earlier on in the game. A lot of the late-game levels also have a lot of complications to get around. I would recommend not taking the stealth aug, though; it makes it far too easy.
Negatives:
- Inconsistent framerate took me out of the experience sometimes, and made me stop playing for a few days when it got so bad
- Lack of weapon variety: I really only used a silenced stun gun, silenced pistol with EMP rounds, and a silenced tranq rifle. I didn't feel like any of the other weapon upgrades were really all that useful, especially in a game where you're getting up close and personal. Perhaps in my next playthrough the other upgrades will provide more variety when I change the weapons I tend to use
- Lack of credits: While I didn't need to buy stuff very often, by the end of the game, with some spending, I only had about 6000 credits. I'm not sure if I did something very wrong, but I know to buy a praxis kit, it's 10,000 credits. How does someone get that much?!
Overall, the game was a lot of fun, and I'm definitely going to replay it, especially since it doesn't have the horrible and forced bossfights of the previous game, and I would recommend it to friends that have relatively powerful cards, or those who are willing to sacrifice some graphical intensity for good gameplay.

This game was on discount when I bought it. And yes, I did read several forum posts. There were loads of horror stories on the forum. However, I thought that three dollars wouldn't be a big deal right? I mean, Codemaster's a fairly well-known group; they won't screw up anything important, right? Oh boy, was I wrong...
My first 30 minutes was graced with a horrendous setup process, Games For Windows Live (GFWL), DX installation, unintuitive interface. GFWL was particularly painful, this is simply a stupid choice for online gaming, there's a reason no other game uses it. Beyond that, I was frustrated with a soundless game and random crashes. It took almost an hour for me to get into the first level, and what greeted me was a satirical loading cut-scene with overly loud sound, a far-cry from my previous hour of silence. After that, the game just blacked out, no sound, no sight, nothing.
Following my incredibly frustrating experience, I decided to contact the Codemaster support team. To my surprise, they responded within a day, not bad for a partially "defunct" studio. However, the response was short and extremely unhelpful. I was told to restart my game and replug my headset, something that I've done more times than I'd like to. At this point, I was ready to give up. My friend made the same purchase on the very same discount event, only to find the game failing to install, and later, incapable of starting up.
I didn't even touched on the gameplay, graphics and storyline, but the hour I spent was more than enough to persuade me against my hastily made purchase. The game might be a gem, if it actually runs. But in my case, it clearly didn't.
After reading several other reviews and watching some gameplay videos, I am glad to not miss out any groundbreaking contents. Graphics and audio are generally the same as Dragon Rising, which is to say, 2009 technologies in a 2011 game. Gameplay itself suffers too, with less than optimal AI, restrictive level designs and poor weapon modeling. Lastly, the story is nothing to write (if there's any written in the first place) home about. You typical B movie plot, the swearing sergeant, evil Chinese army and a seemingly elite squad, who in the actual game, are incapable of climbing into Humvees.
Hell, even the uninstallation failed. The first time I tried to uninstall it crashed Steam. It took more than 10 minutes on the second go to fully remove this POS.

An awesome game which brings out your inner child and fond memories of the old Army Men games and imagination you once possessed as a young lad playing with toys. All maps are very enjoyable with each having it's own game mode, music and home inspired ambiance much like the atmospheres you'd create as a child out of ordinary household items for a proper setup for your toys to have an all out battle. With the maps offering variety there is not much favoritism towards any specific maps which means players do not vote for the same map or two over and over endlessly like players in other games tend to make a habit. There's a pretty cool freezer map and a pretty sweet cake map as well! If you enjoy fast paced third person shooters I urge you to get this game! The gameplay itself is reasonably basic which I have been really enjoying. Everyone is equal from the start due to the game not having any ranks, upgrades or perks which in my opinion is marvelous since that means you have to rely on skill, tactics and hustle rather than having an unfair advantage on less fortunate players. As I said, everyone is equal as soon as they play the game, so as long as you're a decent shooter you should be able to do just fine! The community has been very kind so far as I have yet to run into any rude or arrogant players, so no need to worry about immature elitists and enjoy yourself! This has quickly become one of my favorite games due to it's competitive gameplay and yet silly charm, I highly recommend this game!

The Mean Greens – Plastic Warfare:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I guess most of us (boys) used to play with Green and Tan soldiers in our early youth! Re-creating the battle of the kitchen or the most infamous battle of the bathtub where an entire division drowns to death in your human mucky water!  But now, you can do these battles on your PC, isn’t exciting…? Well it is absolutely MARVELLOUS!!!
The Mean Greens – Plastic Warfare is a third person online multiplayer shooter game where you play either a Green or a Tan toy soldier in 10 unique and well-designed maps. You will play the “Barnyard Ball” map (one of my favourites) where you not only have to eliminate as many soldiers as possible but score up to 3 goals to win the game; or the “Kitchen Run’ map where you have to push the enemy cup over the benchtop to win the round!
Your soldier will have a number of weapons at his disposal, 5 in total: machine guns, shotgun, sniper rifle, flame thrower and the all mighty bazooka to teach one or two tricks to your enemies. I thoroughly enjoy hiding behind the sponge waiting for a figurine to pass by and greet him with a small missile (rocket) to blow him out of the kitchen! FUN…! FUN…! FUN…!
Controls are really easy to use; you run, jump, crouch, roll and of course shoot at plastic figurines. The game runs very well and you will be treated with a great soundtrack. The graphics are wonderful and the game is a great price!
Plenty of dedicated servers to play on, including some Australian ones!
Positives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Fun and addictive
-	10 unique maps and modes
-	Dedicates servers
-	Great Graphics and Soundtracks
-	Great price
-	Achievements
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~

-	None!!
The Mean Greens – Plastic Warfare is truly the surprise game of this year for me!
10/10 +10% for good measure!

I'm an only child of only children, but playing this game over the past couple of years invariably makes me feel what I imagine a visit to the home of a favourite - and awesomely bent - aunt or uncle would evoke. Trine magically knows your needs and wants, and playfully prods you into the midst delightful surprises and puzzles, without ever holding a sense of obligation or responsibility over your head. You might not visit that often over the years, but you're always delighted to go back.
If that's too abstracted: It's a utterly lovable co-op physics platformer, with so much love put into every nuance I want to hug the people who made it to death. From the gorgeous, richly rendered parallax set pieces, to the far-above-par voice acting, and the brilliantly characterized animation and physical mechanics of it all (fun to watch *and* play), Trine 2 oozes charm and heart from every pore. Honestly, I just check into this little storybook world every few months when I want to wipe away the inexorable cynicism about gaming off my face and replace it with an ear-to-ear grin.
Here's to you, Trine [2]!
