Oh man.
If you enjoy platformers, this is a great game to play.
This game is amazing even if you are just playing solo, but it definitely shines as a cooperative experience.
The aethetics are GREAT! So much detail in every part of the level.
You have to switch between 3 characters (rogue/wizard/warrior) to complete different puzzles, and there is an upgrading tree that is simple, but well-done.
The instructions are very seamless and easy to use (and you even start off in an interative menu screen).
The puzzles are actually quite challenging, as you have to juggle the abilities of 3 different characters (ex: wizard creates boxes/moves objects, rogue swings around, warrior breaks things). Admittedly, I have had to resort to "cheating" in the form of my friend levitating 2 of us through puzzles we couldn't figure out.
There are also some very nice tricks you can figure out depending on who you like to play as.
For example, the ROGUE can shoot gravity arrows that can annoy your friends, slow down animations [remember aesthetics are GREAT], or slow down flamethrowers or those cannons that keep melting you in the face. That being said, the rogue has an improved jump (if it's against a wall/ledge) and the gravity arrow not only increases your ENTIRE party's jump, but also allows you to effectively leave your other 2 friends behind since you no longer need the wizard to levitate you anywhere.
The rogue can also uselessly latch onto (applicable) surfaces with her swing, and watch as your other members try to solve a puzzle or make it across a gap of wooden supports that are touch-sensitive -  which means that she could also trigger them with said swing right before a warrior's landing, causing him to fall to an untimely death.
The WIZARD can use loopholes (depending on your settings) to levitate yourself or your friends, and will also be your main character for solving puzzles and dealing with hazards since he is the only character with object manipulation. For example, you might need the wizard to hold a platform above a flaming ground of death. Or you could also pull that log just a little to the right so that your rogue misses her spider-man swing, falling to her death. There are a lot of pipe-based puzzles (for diverting air currents or flames), and the solutions for those are not always cookie-cutter - you might have to bash that pipe to get it to orient the correct way.
The WARRIOR is your tank/fighter. His shield can negate hazards like flamethrowers, those cannons that melt your face off, and he is basically the person everyone will run to when enemies spawn. Some encounters have several enemies spawn with archer support, and, as always, everyone will run to the warrior for protection. The fighting can become a challenge if you are playing solo (or have moved on ahead of your friends), so levelling up the warrior's skill tree can be useful for survivability.  There are also many obstacles that can only be destroyed by the warrior's hammer (or later, by a levelled-up fire arrow from the rogue).
Trine 2's biggest beauty, however, is the cooperative aspect.

I absolutely love this game. It's shorter and sweeter than Far Cry 3. The story pacing feels better, and it doesn't outstay its welcome. It adds in lots of glorious 80s references and the soundtrack is absolutely brilliant, including some really well placed licensed music. It's the first game in a while that's just constantly reminded me that I'm playing a video game, instead of trying to be an experience, or a movie. Not once does it take itself seriously. I found myself reading all the lost notes and the VHS tape descriptions, because it became apparent that everything was an easter egg to be consumed and laughed at, and just generally enjoyed. In my Far Cry 3 review I talked of weapon pacing and how you feel like you grow at an appropriate rate in terms of the abilities and weapons you can use. Well, all that is out of the window! And you'll see what I mean when you play it. Because quite frankly, it fits the overall theme of the game for it to be like this. You're an all American 80's action hero! You don't do "pacing", or "small".
It doesn't have any rushed or tacked on modes like co-op or any of that fluff that was present in the original Far Cry 3. It's just a brilliantly executed vision, by a developer who had a good idea, and a publisher that generously allowed him to go through with it. You have to play this game.

I was sceptical about trying WRC 6 at first, but after reading a few positive reviews from fellow DiRT Rally veterans, I decided to give it a go. And I'm so glad I did. I was hooked from the first stage.
The physics and FFB are first class: realistic and intuitive. It's how a car should behave in both low and high speeds. You can feel the weight of the car through the steering wheel and know what to do to make the car behave.
The second really impressive aspect of the game is the stages. There are only five per country, but all official countries being represented it's quite enough. And the different rallies are very well portrayed atmospherically and through the surfaces. It's clear that a lot of effort went into stage design, especially the super special stages which are modeled accurately after real life ones.
The career mode is great. I was highly motivated to finish the whole thing. With hard difficulty it required absolute focus without much practice, so I'm guessing the expert difficulty requires both. Which is how it should be.
I still haven't encountered a single bug. It seems to me a very well polished product.
Other positive things to be mentioned: the damage model, online multiplayer mode (simultaneous racing with others showing up as coloured shadow cars), sounds, tire model and achievements.
Things to work on: camera modes, more detailed car setups and maybe some proofreading of the pacenotes.
Overall it's a fantastic rally game which captures the spirit of WRC well. I have high hopes for future games of the series, which I hope will feature even more real life stages and maybe a wider range of cars and classes. I'm won't go into comparisons between this and DiRT Rally as they are both great games, and deserve to be enjoyed individually.

I just really love this game a ton, and I recommend it to everyone. That said, it has some stupidly huge flaws that I need to talk about, so bear with me.
My Four biggest complaints:
1. It occasionally lags, even in ranked mode. It can sometimes lose you the game. Everyone complains about it, so I will make this part brief. The devs completely acknowledge it, and have been working on fixing it for a while. I think they are making progress. Just try to ignore the lag.
2. The game claims to be very balanced, and a lot of players say it is. The thing is, I have currently spent 157 hours playing this game, almost all of it in ranked, and about half of the players that I have gone up against were playing Hattori. There are 23 characters in the game, so to have 50% of opponents playing Hattori is just a sign of ridiculous character design flaws. The least played character on ranked is Lord Vraxx, and I have seen, at absolute most, FOUR PEOPLE play as him. Also, the devs are constantly tweaking things, but they never change anything enough for people to play a character like Vraxx and stop playing a character like Hattori. This has always been the case ever since I started playing 5 months ago, and from the look of things, it seems like they won't be nerfing Hattori anytime soon.
3. There are some moves and tactics in the game that are stupidly powerful when used against someone that isn't a really high level player. Sometimes silver rank players can lose to newbs that just spam a single blatantly powerful special move that either comes out really fast, hits a large area, and/or is very hard to punish. (BTW, most of Hattori's moves are all three) Today I played against someone that was way worse at the game than me, and they were able to defeat me with 2 lives left. They just kept using the easy-to-learn technique of throwing a weapon downward and kicking straight down while the opponent is clinging to the side of the stage. It is extremely difficult to dodge both the weapon and the kick, and if the technique works, it can kill you even when you have taken almost no prior damage.
4. Very rarely, I have wanted to air jump or air dodge to get back on the stage, but I kept pressing the button and it just wasn't working. The game only started listening like 1-2 seconds later, but then it just wasn't enough and I died. It has happened multiple times, and it is just stupid. I use my laptop's built-in keyboard to play, so it couldn't have been a controller malfunction. Also, about half the time that someone will hurriedly try to air-down-heavy in this game, they end up accidentally doing an air-neutral-heavy. It happens suspiciously often.
This game is amazingly fun, but sometimes things like these just make me want to stop playing forever.

There have been a few consistent complaints with the game, and I do understand where they're coming from.
- There's the complaint about microtransactions being in the Breach mode, but I haven't even touched it yet so it has very little relevance to me, and doesn't particularly bother me as a business practice, as loads of other gaming companies do it.
- The choppiness: this I actually do get, and it definitely does deter from the immersive experience, and is a little surprising that it happens in some areas sometimes, but not all the time. There doesn't seem to be a particular amount of consistency for it. Recommend high settings for GTX 970 cards and the like, runs at 60FPS almost always.
- The ending, to me, didn't seem like that much of a letdown. It was definitely a cliffhanger ending that's supposed to lead into the DLC, and I do have questions that remain unanswered, but it does make me want to get the DLC in order to find out the end of the story. I'm not a particularly big fan of this sort of thing, though, so this both a positive an a negative.
Positives:
- The graphics themselves are actually quite lovely, especially with the black lines removed, and there are a lot of toggleable options, allowing for better optimization and more specific tweaking
- The gameplay doesn't feel that clunky on the keyboard, and the controls didn't take much getting used to, with a little bit of customization, I had the cat in the bag
- Character design was quite good, and the whole environment itself has a mesh of realism, like what one might expect when visiting Prague, as well as the notorious HR-like jagged design on interiors and clothing. Important characters have distinct character design, and really do stand out in the world
- Difficulty-wise, sometimes I found the game too easy, but there are quite a few sections where it was challenging to get through it without killing anybody, especially earlier on in the game. A lot of the late-game levels also have a lot of complications to get around. I would recommend not taking the stealth aug, though; it makes it far too easy.
Negatives:
- Inconsistent framerate took me out of the experience sometimes, and made me stop playing for a few days when it got so bad
- Lack of weapon variety: I really only used a silenced stun gun, silenced pistol with EMP rounds, and a silenced tranq rifle. I didn't feel like any of the other weapon upgrades were really all that useful, especially in a game where you're getting up close and personal. Perhaps in my next playthrough the other upgrades will provide more variety when I change the weapons I tend to use
- Lack of credits: While I didn't need to buy stuff very often, by the end of the game, with some spending, I only had about 6000 credits. I'm not sure if I did something very wrong, but I know to buy a praxis kit, it's 10,000 credits. How does someone get that much?!
Overall, the game was a lot of fun, and I'm definitely going to replay it, especially since it doesn't have the horrible and forced bossfights of the previous game, and I would recommend it to friends that have relatively powerful cards, or those who are willing to sacrifice some graphical intensity for good gameplay.

It's free, so you're not really losing anything if you download it, but if you do, bear this in mind:
The only thing that this mod has going for it, in my opinion, is the new gravity gun.
Well, that and the soundtrack.
What this mod does NOT have going for it is, well, a lot.
First, the levels:
There are 4 levels in the game. Each one is a chapter. Thus, the game is very short. Ther are many points at which you can find yourself stuck and unsure of what to do next or where to go.
The combat:
Frustrating. When you're not being enccountered by, let's say, 1 or 2 enemies (which is so easy I don't even consider it combat) you have giant hordes that seem unquellable. And you might think "Oh but I have the gravity gun" No. The gravity gun is not exactly an ammoless weapon. Remember how in HL2 your flashlight used the same Aux power as your sprinting ability? Well that's you Gravity Gun ammo. Congratlations! This is something I learned the hard way, and it hinders your use of it to the point that it becomes very situational and you have to resort to your average joe weapons (which, by the way, aren't anything new).
The story:
What the heck? What is this? It seems you're playing as Freeman again, you wake up on a train, then you... Progress through the suburbs or whatever? The story here is not well thought out. If you like the Half-Life games mainly for their story, then you can safely say no to this mod.
Overall, not a very great experience. You can give it a go if you REALLY want that new Gravity Gun. After all, there's no stoppin you; it's free. But if you're looking for more than just a cool new device, then don't hop into this one.

Oh man.
If you enjoy platformers, this is a great game to play.
This game is amazing even if you are just playing solo, but it definitely shines as a cooperative experience.
The aethetics are GREAT! So much detail in every part of the level.
You have to switch between 3 characters (rogue/wizard/warrior) to complete different puzzles, and there is an upgrading tree that is simple, but well-done.
The instructions are very seamless and easy to use (and you even start off in an interative menu screen).
The puzzles are actually quite challenging, as you have to juggle the abilities of 3 different characters (ex: wizard creates boxes/moves objects, rogue swings around, warrior breaks things). Admittedly, I have had to resort to "cheating" in the form of my friend levitating 2 of us through puzzles we couldn't figure out.
There are also some very nice tricks you can figure out depending on who you like to play as.
For example, the ROGUE can shoot gravity arrows that can annoy your friends, slow down animations [remember aesthetics are GREAT], or slow down flamethrowers or those cannons that keep melting you in the face. That being said, the rogue has an improved jump (if it's against a wall/ledge) and the gravity arrow not only increases your ENTIRE party's jump, but also allows you to effectively leave your other 2 friends behind since you no longer need the wizard to levitate you anywhere.
The rogue can also uselessly latch onto (applicable) surfaces with her swing, and watch as your other members try to solve a puzzle or make it across a gap of wooden supports that are touch-sensitive -  which means that she could also trigger them with said swing right before a warrior's landing, causing him to fall to an untimely death.
The WIZARD can use loopholes (depending on your settings) to levitate yourself or your friends, and will also be your main character for solving puzzles and dealing with hazards since he is the only character with object manipulation. For example, you might need the wizard to hold a platform above a flaming ground of death. Or you could also pull that log just a little to the right so that your rogue misses her spider-man swing, falling to her death. There are a lot of pipe-based puzzles (for diverting air currents or flames), and the solutions for those are not always cookie-cutter - you might have to bash that pipe to get it to orient the correct way.
The WARRIOR is your tank/fighter. His shield can negate hazards like flamethrowers, those cannons that melt your face off, and he is basically the person everyone will run to when enemies spawn. Some encounters have several enemies spawn with archer support, and, as always, everyone will run to the warrior for protection. The fighting can become a challenge if you are playing solo (or have moved on ahead of your friends), so levelling up the warrior's skill tree can be useful for survivability.  There are also many obstacles that can only be destroyed by the warrior's hammer (or later, by a levelled-up fire arrow from the rogue).

One of the best RTS games out there.  Nothing quite beats some of the moments the game brings on.  The following is a part of a game I did (in skirmish) against the ai with 6 bots vs just my ai partner and I:
As I looked at my minimap, I realized my buddy's base was quickly getting overwhelmed.  His outer defenses were obliterated not a few minutes ago, and yet the enemy was closing in around his HQ.  He was building guardsmen as quickly as he could but the onslaught of orks, chaos space marines, and necrons were too much.  His commander made a valiant last stand, but it was in vain...I was then alone.
I scrutinized my defenses and realized I was lacking.  I quickly built many turrets as my first line of defense with some space marines around a pass that funneled the enemy forces down and caused them to lose some of the advantage of numbers.  My second line were multiple heavy tanks with melee infantry further behind the pass.  The purpose of this line was a bullet magnet while my base spit out as many units as I could for a heroic last stand.  The third line was whoever else was left at the time the other two lines fell.  As I checked my units upgrades and made sure they had all they could have, then I saw a red tide on the minimap.  I realized the Emperor would be seeing us soon in the next life.
As the enemy forces through themselves at the turrets, I couldn't help but realize the corpses of the dead.  The game has an option that leaves almost all the corpses on the field, and I recommend to turn it on to the max as it adds satisfaction to the price your men are paying.  The turrets and supporting infantry could only hold on for so long.  Before the line was breached I was in about a 7:1 kd ratio.  After the line was broken, it became a 1:1.  I zoomed in close for a final look at these men, and I grinned for I knew we would all be joining him soon.  The second line held for about half the time.  The third and final line consisted of my commander and everyone else that had not died.  I waited until the enemy was within weapon's range, then I lit them up with artillery, orbital strikes, and the last two flyers I had.  Then, my men charged.  They went down valiantly with many enemies dead in the process.
I knew there was no chance for victory from the very beginning, but I watched as my commander made his final defiant yell, I was sad there was never a chance.  I was fighting for time, and I got a lot of time.  We fought until the final drop of blood was spilt, until the final breath was exhaled, until the fat♥♥♥♥♥ho sang, until the bitter end.
These are the moments that define gaming, not the scripted ones that everyone encounters, but the ones that are player-made.  The game modes where the goal is to kill the enemy commander, and you are completely surrounded on all sides and you make a final charge to kill him to gain victory, and you see your numbers fall from 30 to 23 to 14 to 6 until all you have left is two guardsmen (they die sooooooo easily) and a tank that has a third of its health left and you win.  You win against all the odds, and you smirk at the trail of the men that died for victory.  I cannot tell you of all the awesomeness that is this game.  Go get it.

DLC Quest is a humorous jab at the game industry from the perspective of a retro platform game that requires the purchase of downloadable expansions to perform even the most basic functions.
The game begins with no sound and no animation.  In fact, you aren't even able to jump or move left!  These features aren't included out of the box, of course. Instead, you are granted the privilege of purchasing these advanced gameplay features from an in-game vendor.  All of the gags you would expect to see are here, including the infamous expensive horse armor.  Thankfully, as the game reassures us early on, no ACTUAL real-life currency is involved. All transactions are conducted using coins collected inside the game.
Unfortunately, there isn't much of a "game" here.  Unlocking DLC is required in order to progress the purposely generic, but ultimately uninspired "story".  Once you get going, it's pretty much a straight path to the finish line: Collect enough coins to unlock  the next DLC pack, rinse, repeat until the credits roll.  There is no death.  In fact, there is no way to fail. In that respect, DLC Quest is, in a sense, closer to old Lucasarts adventure games.  Enemies function merely as passive roadblocks that only additional downloaded content can alleviate.
Ultimately the only real replay value is in doing speed runs, collecting coins, unlocking the DLC as fast as possible, and comparing your times against a leaderboard.  Currently the top 10 is filled with people who finished the game in 12 minutes.  I believe I spent just over twice that amount of time playing.  The recent addition of a second quest ("Live Freemium or Die") helps extend the value, but this is still a short game.
DLC Quest is a genuinely funny commentary on the state of micro-transactions and downloadable content in gaming.  It may run the joke into the ground by the end, but at roughly $3 in most digital stores, it's worth a look.  Just don't expect any sort of serious challenge.

Surprisingly, really ♥♥♥♥ing good.  I was expecting another hack off MMORPG, but LOTRO has a huge number of features thta arguably make it the best F2P MMORPG on the market right now.
First off, it's filed with pre-established lore.  An excellent job was done in making the player feel inside the LotR universe, and it shows that the develops didn't have to scrounge around for source material
Akin to early WoW, you're not a special snowflake.  You're just another player in this vast world; there are wars going on that you are only a soldier in, you can make small differences here and there but as a whole the world doesn't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about you.  And this is a WONDERFUL MMORPG CONCEPT.  It contributes heavily to the immersion, and makes the game as a whole more compelling to play.
The unique skill and trait trees.  Every game ♥♥♥♥ing has these, but forcing the player to earn the right to use traits or improved skills, even if most of them are just kill 9000 boars and gather kobold candles, gives meaning to the word 'skills'.  Your character worked to improve themselves, and it is reflected in their abilities.  These aren't things that just come along easily while leveling: it takes a large amount of game time to master skills and traits, even with dedicated grinding.  Your character is reflecting the effort and time put into the game, and that in of itself is a fantastic concept.
Lastly I just want to mention one feature that really put this game into the forefront of my mind.  Fall damage.  Most MMORPGs just adopt the WoW %health based fall damage, but this is one area where LOTRO exceeds everything else on the market.  Falling say a story or two doesn't damage your health.  Falling several stories or off a small cliff gives you an injury, which reduces movespeed immensely, removes any capabilities for dodging or negating damage, and lasts for 30 seconds.  Rather than punishing the player by forces them to do a spawn run or what have you when they attempt to speed up their travel by skipping flights of stairs, LOTRO realistically reduces the movespeed of the player by "breaking their leg", meaning that you can jump if you want to, but it is probably faster to walk down the stairs.  But keeping in tandem with the realism, if you jump off a mountain or fall off a building, you are going to die.  However it has to be an extreme height, so there is no fear of dying from simple stair skipping, and it actually causes fear if you come to close to a cliff's edge or accidentally slip off of a roof.
All in all, a solid 9/10, easily the best Free-to-play MMORPG on the market.

THIS IS A SINGLEPLAYER/OFFLINE 2 PLAYER REVIEW (for those who care about it)
THE STORY
-First of all I played MK9, and for people who are new I cannot tell you if you will understand some of what is happening and some things they refer to, but it feels like it is explaned well enough, as this game is set 20 years after the events of MK9.
-The music is fantastic and feels right at all times.
-The cutscenes are grade A quality with fantastic voice acting (it seems like they were going for a tv series feel).
-Many old characters make a small cameo during the game but then just dissapear right after for some reason
-It ties in well enough to MK9's storyline.
-The final boss is a Shao Kahn clone who just spams his same attacks and (SPOILERS (if you are stupid)) gets his♥♥♥♥♥kicked by one of the normal playable characters, deus ex machina if I've ever seen it...
-My opinion real quick right here, I still loved the story anyways and may play it again with around 5 hours of play time if you suck like me.
-The characters work well together and at no point do you ever sigh by their preformance, and for me at least if you love the universe, at no point do you ever feel the need to skip a cutscene.
-Speaking of cutsceans, do you like Quick Time Events? No? Well, flip you, because there are quick time events peppered throughout the story. I've never failed one so I don't know if you have to redo the whole thing if you fail but rest assured if you do fail the fight after you have to watch the same cutscene and then do the same QTE again.
OFFLINE 2 PLAYER
-Yes, it is only offline 2 player; if you have more friends... well now you don't.
-Epic combos seem to of been removed entirely and instead you get this interesting ability to choose your fighting style with the character you pick, giving them a slightly different outfit and a unique set of abilities. Is it good? I dunno, ask the hardcore fans... it just means that I don't get wrecked online instantly anymore, take that as you will.
-You can interact with the background of the map just like Injustice (If you've played it) to finish some cool little combos.
I may of missed some things in this Singleplayer/2 Player review but these are at least the most important to me.
Overall I will give this game an 8/10, the story is short and sweet, the characters are all entertaining, there is some love drama peppered throughout, there is no 4 player anymore (really salty about that) the ending is deus ex machina as f, they stripped all the characters of most of their abilities and added a new system of speciality kits instead, also if you stick around for after the credits you unlock the big bad man himself and get to see (SPOILER) Kitana and Liu Kang rule the netherrealm together. Should be interesting to see where they go with that.

First review I've done, here goes nothing...
Firstly, this game is a HUGE improvement on WRC5, although that wouldn't be entirely difficult. As soon as you jump into career mode, you can tell the developers have actually thought about the product they are producing. This is evident in little things such as seeing another driver start the stage before you (and its actually the car ahead of you in the timings, not a random). Another nice touch which I appreciated is the fact stages can be cancelled due to bad weather, an accident or too many spectators on the stage.
The handling and FFB feels really rewarding to me. You can really feel when you are driving on snow and ice (steering goes light with lack of grip) and on tarmac (steering is harder as there is lots of grip). The stages are much more realistic as they are longer and narrower with a lot more obstacles to prevent cutting and a lot more spectators lining the stage which really immerses you into the world of rally. In addition, the stages are accurate to that of the real rally. For example, the constant corners in Corsica, the square corners and hairpins in Germany along with fast stretches on narrow roads. WRC 5 was guilty of having constant hairpins on every rally, as if the developers have never seen a rally stage. Thankfully, this isnt the case in WRC6!
The damage model is more realistic now as well, although it could be more realistic for my liking. Punctures can occur along stages, forcing you into either struggling to the end or replacing the tire, costing a 30 second time penalty. Again, a nice touch by the developers. The best stages are the super specials which are SO MUCH FUN to drive.
The downside of this game for me is how boring career mode can become. Seb Ogier wins almost every single rally, and the AI time appear to be fake as you could lose to your opponent on a super special but still be quickest?! The developers need to look at F1 2016 to spice up their career mode. I like the categories you have to go through on your path to WRC, but once you get there my god it is dreary. Career mode should evolve, like F1 2016's. For example, in 3 years time M-Sport are suddenly very quick and VW arent.
Overall, the game looks stunning. Visibility is poor in foggy conditions which is a real challenge. Stages are nice and long and ready to kill you at any moment. Rally fans, it is a must buy. Casual gamers, you could enjoy it. I believe this game could get you interested in the world of rallying.

Pros:
The gameplay from Human Revolution is present and polished to the nth degree.
Every level can be completed in multiple ways, and rewards you using optional augs.
The entire game can be played stealthily and non lethally.
Levels are extremely intricate and layered, providing new approaches each time.
PC version has tons of graphical tweaks thanks to Nixxes (the porting studio).
Good length (~20-30 hours, my first playthrough was 35 hours but mileage varies).
Cons:
The included microtransactions. You don't need them, but them being offered is a problem nonetheless.
Preorder bonuses are one time use only. Preorder mission can spoil the story (disable it and play after the game).
The story sets up a sequel in the worst way, and as a result feels like only part of a whole story.
DirectX 12 is still lame. Stick with the DX11 renderer.
Some characters from Human Revolution were either pushed aside or had the voice actors replaced.
Animations and lip syncing can still look odd compared to most other big budget games.
Mixed:
Mouse controls felt weird, but subsequent patches added more options for adjustment.
Controller support is there but never quite feels right, in my opinion.
Sometimes alt tabbing or using the Steam overlay will cause sprint/walk to become stuck.
Overall:
I've played a few of the AAA releases this year (including Doom and Dark Souls 3). For 2016, Mankind Divided was certainly my favorite. Look past the mixed reviews, almost all entirely about the microtransactions, and you have yourself an amazing title.

The game was great. It was beatiful, it was fun, and it was deus ex. I did a "stealth - no (well, minimal) kill" style playthrough, as I usually do with Deus Ex games, and found that the game was very fullfilling that way.
Steam says I got 50 hours out of Mankind Dividied on one playthrough - but it was probably closer to 35 to 40 hours of actual playing time, and 15 hours of me forgetting to close the game. Still, felt like a lot of content.
I'd like to address the two common concerns I see that seems to lead everyone to thumbs down an otherwise great game.
Concern number one - Microtransactions and "one use" preorder swag using the microtransaction system. I realize its cool to complain with everyone else, but to me this is a non issue. The amount of loot in this game is ridiculous - if anything I wasted too much time trying to decide what to sell and scrap, considering your stash is very small, and even your explanded inventory doesn't hold much. No one should ever feel the need to use microtransactions on this game. You will collect more than everything you'll ever know what to do with just playing (at the end of the game I had 11 unused Praxis that I didn't want to spend, because there was nothing left worth while to spend it on). And as far as the preorder stuff - I personally hate pre order in game stuff (makes a game easier than it was intended), and in the case, I honestly didn't even find the preorder loot in the UI until about 15 hours in. Didn't touch it, didn't miss it.
PLEASE don't let the fact that its cool to complain about how greedy Edios / Square are, at all prevent you from playing this game.
Concern number two - the game "suddenly ends" and there is cut content for future DLC, blah blah blah. This really concerned me going into the game. And as I played, I kept waiting for this to happen. 10 - 20 - 30 hours in, and the game just kept going. I absolutely don't understand why so many people felt the game abrubtly ended. To me, you could see the proper ending comming from a mile away - the story was brought to a propper climax. And the story and leads culminating in a final mission. It was really well done, and in my opinion, this story ended exactly where it should have.
I find it really strange how divergent my experience was from others. But it was a great Deus Ex in my opinion, and if you've been a fan back from the originals as I have been, and you've also liked the modern reboot so far, I think you'll love this one.

To say that 'Deus Ex: Mankind Divided' has issues would be an understatement. The use of a SINGLE hub area is just moronic, loading screens probably made up an hour of my play time (that’s not hyperbole), and the story just isn't as interesting as Human Revolution's. However, this is still a damn good game that manages to overcome its flaws.
The primary reason for this is the gameplay, which has been improved in just about every way. From the new cover to cover system, to the game-changing experimental augmentations, to the improved level design, Mankind Divided has perfected the gameplay formula employed by DXHR. The new cover to cover system makes both controlling Adam in both stealth and combat significantly easier. And the improvement to controls don't stop there. Combat is smoother in every way. Aiming from cover is much easier, and the new ammo type system adds some depth to shootouts. The new experimental augs can radically affect gameplay. Remote hacking allows you to deactivate certain security features, the Icarus dash allows you to reach areas of the map you otherwise couldn't, and the other augs are just as useful. And all of these improvements are capped off with A+++ level design, on every single map.
However, DXMD's unimaginative story does its very best to override the gameplay improvements. You will once again play as Adam Jensen, as he attempts to track down the terrorists behind a train bombing in Prague. That’s everything. Obviously stuff happens, there are some reveals and a little bit of mystery, but the core of the story remains very simple and straight-forward. This dramatic departure from the ambition of DXHR's superb story is striking, and a clear step in the wrong direction. The voice acting and atmosphere are still quite good, but unfortunately that just isn't enough to make up for the story.
And of course there are the micro transactions. In my opinion, this is a non-issue for DXMD. The micro transactions are only accessible through the main menu, and you will have no trouble finding all the resources you need throughout the course of the game. Others may take issue with this, but I just don't care.
And that’s the story with DXMD. Is it perfect? No. Is as good as DXHR? No. Is it a superb game and a worthy sequel? Hell yes, and if you're a fan of the Deus Ex style of free-form gameplay, you will not be disappointed.

Great mod. You should know a few things first before going in, however. First of all,  it's extremely short. I felt like after a few minutes I had already acquired every Half Life 2 weapon, and I ended up stuck on the final encounter/boss for a while because I thought I had to progress somewhere when in reality you had to beat all of the enemies to end the game. The length isn't necessarily a bad thing, it's even acknowledged by the developer, but it's still something to be aware of; don't go in looking for a full campaign to last you a week or two.
Second of all, the main mechanic of the Gravity Propulsion Gun is really cool. It's fun to use and is implemented well. The only problem with it is that I feel you're barely given a chance to use it. The level design is good (lots of love and care clearly went into putting detail into every nook and cranny), but it never quite takes full advantage of the amazing mechanic they give you. To illustrate my point, most of the levels probably could have been untouched and still possible to play through without the Propulsion Gun save for minor parts like missing ladders, high ledges, etc. where you are required to jump high.
There could have been massive gaps, sections jumping from building to building, alternating firing off walls for walljumps, freefalls where you have to time your shot to break your fall, so on and so on. Using the gun feels a lot like rocket jumping (which is good), and all you have to do is hop into some jump maps in games like Team Fortress 2 or Quake to see all of the creative designs there for maneuvering around stages. Lots of untapped potential, which is disappointing. Nevertheless, this mod is still very good and worth a playthrough. Just curb your expectations and think of it more of a demo or showcase of the Propulsion Gun mechanic that I hope is picked up again in the future.

Vanilla Review:
Dawn of War Soulstorm has many, many unfinished abilities and units which take away from the overall effect of multiplayer and campaign abilities. While in itself it is still a good title and a replayable campaign for AI grinding is still fun, if Relic/THQ had actually finished their project, it would of been a lot better.
The Campaign is basically a repeat of Dark Crusade but you got Tau and Sisters of Battle now which isn't really that much. Overall balancing is okay but there is a lot left to be desired such as knockback spam being hard to counter or defend against and special weapons troopers always being the first to die even if they're in the back of the squad being attacked.
The vanilla version also does a very poor job at vehicle implementation particularly with aircraft as they're glorified glass cannons in some cases (Orks) and useless in almsot all accords (Imperial Guard).  Limiting special units in most cases where in Dark Crusade you could have more is a double edged sword and the limits should of been raised. Having the ability to only create one elite troop unit compared to three back in Dark Crusade is a major debuff in my opinion and overall takes away from the fighting experience as most of them are very weak to begin with.
The developers have also neglected balancing between every race. Races such as the Orks and Tau are extremely powerful against most other factions and in some cases you can't even win if it's against a competent player or the AI on the highest difficulty such as Orks vs Imperial Guard....you can't even win in a balanced fight particularly if it's 3v3 or 4v4 due to the Invulnerability spam on Ork units. Now if you do Orks vs Space Marines or even Eldar, it's a lot easier because the races aren't glass cannons. Imperial Guard it seems has been mostly balanced from a 1v1 stand point and team fight with non-Imperial Guard races which is a shame because they should be able to do well in team fights with other Guard players but in almost every instance, that is not the case. Sisters of Battle are extremely strong in all stages of the game and honestly minus the fact they're basically infantry only, can beat almost every faction in a 1v2 instance. Tau are glorified glass cannons and with the length of their tech tree, most games end before you can even begin to put the hurt on the enemy in a 1v1. Their entire tech tree is based off long team fights where they really shine and often end up losing in early game fights on small maps due to their higher maintenance costs and the lack of defenses. Eldar/Dark Eldar and SM/CSM have changed very little and are good at all stages, no reall balancing needed. Necrons, very very good late stages but absolutely get massacured early game in even fights. Not even balanced in a 1v1 perspective or even 2v2, they show the least amount of balancing from the developers and honestly only shine on large maps where you can't get rushed at one minute into the game.
Overall Score: 7/10
Campaign 5/10
Multiplayer 8/10
Game Mechanics 8/10
Replay Value 10/10
Balacning 6/10
Ultimate Apocalypse Review:
This is the way the game should be played IF your computer is capable of supporting it. It expands upon the vanilla build and releases several more functions that make the game more enjoyable in addition to implementing several functions that were left unfinished such as additional units and abilities.
The mod also implements the Tyranids and Inquisition (WIP) for play in addition to a few new maps but overall is a massive rebalancing project that is catered as well towards Super Heavy battles. Trust me, if you want a tank war, this is the mod for you especially if you play Imperial Guard. It embraces the doctrine of "We have a tank for that too!"
The ability for all races to now build defensive turrets and in some cases walls/barricades is an added bonus on smaller maps to help prevent rushing and the ability to further upgrade defensive buildings and resources helps solve the problem of resource stagnation in most games making it much easier to continue playing late game even if you end up losing your armies rapidly.
The mod also rebalances aircraft which in the Vanilla version were a joke and a waste of resources. In addition to the mod expanding both the capabilities of each race, it also drastically increases the scale of destruction and carnage you can witness. The mod is still a WIP which is good because it is constantly rebalanced and a few new races are being implemented.

Ever wondered to explore Middle-Earth and see the town of Bree, the greens of the Shire and the beauty of Rivendell through your very own eyes? Or perhaps you aspire to be a warrior of the Free Peoples by wielding a shield with as much expertise as shield-master Boromir or string an arrow to the bow as elegantly as the archer Legolas and leave a pile of Orcs in your wake?
The Lord of the Rings Online offer all those opportunities and more. Excellent graphics means that you really feel the whole Middle Earth experience when you walk through the town of Bree and into the Prancing Pony for a glass beer or mug of ale. And yes, LOTRO will let you do that!
Having spent the past few years of my life playing this game in my free time, I will admit that initially downloaded the game not knowing what to expect of LOTRO's idea of Middle Earth but now many years later, I am proud to say that I've got the chance to do deeds that would make Aragorn consider leaving Arwen for. Or make Boromir betray Gondor - if that makes more sense to you.
From simple solo exploring of the fields of the Shire to raiding up with up to 23 other people (24 in total) to fight the likes of vile creatures such as Balrogs and Dragons, LOTRO has it. A good combat skill and trait system allows for dynamic fights and variety of gameplay amongst the various classes. Feel like wielding a shield and turning into a unstoppable version of a defensive god or grasping a greatblade and breaking the Middle-Earth record of "number of Uruks killed"? Then make it happen by playing LOTRO.
Taking all of the above into account and adding on things like a wide choice of mounts for players, a flexible and in-depth crafting system, unique legendary items, player housing filled with the Balrog's Sword (a loot dropped from killing him) makes The Lord of the Rings Online THE MMO to play.
Take your first baby steps in Middle-Earth by giving this game a try - who knows, you might even get into the history books found in the Library of Rivendell...or even be one of the chosen few to simply walk into Mordor.
Forward onto victory! Forward...FOR GONDOR!

It's a hard one to rate but after more playtime I have decided to rate it up.  The AI is a good challenge, the story mode is awesome, there's a lot more content than the old arcade style towers.  The graphics are amazing and the gore is A+.  You can earn easy finishers so you can play random characters without learning all of their finishing combos.  And there is a lot of content for a fighting game.
As for the multiplayer, this is the big con.
Ranking system infinitely places you against seemingly "random" opponents, rather than opponents of "same skill".  I have literally never won a single battle in online play.  Yeah, maybe I'm a noob, then why the hell am I facing opponents who have 3x wins over losses and hundreds of wins?  Why am I facing literally UNDEFEATED opponents?
Trash ranking system.  Leaves a sour taste in the mouth and an incredibly unpleasant experience overall, which isn't something you want when playing a game for fun lol.  All in all, if you're okay with just the single player aspects of the game, I rate it up.  If you want to play with friends locally using two controllers, I rate it up.  If you want to play online and ranked, better learn to "juggle" your opponents endlessly in the air, because that's what they'll do to you, and if you try to play "legit" with just the 3-hit combos and power moves and block timings, you will be sourly disappointed when you get juggled by some noob.

What is Mount&Blade
In the Mount&Blade games you play as a warrior seeking for power and glory in a few different settings (Calradia, Europe and nothern Europe). You recrute warriors to your war band and fight with them in strategy/action based battles and seiges.
The genre of the game is hard to desribe, but if I would have to give it a try it's something like an ''action RPG strategy simulator'' and all within a sandbox envirement.
As it is sandbox, you don't have a goal, but I general the aim is to rule over the whole map. To achieve this you can, fight, trade, mary join a existing kingdom, create a rebelion etc. this is what makes Mount&Blade great: It is really up to you how you want to achieve your goals and what those goals are.
About this Mount&Blade
In this installment of the series you play in the fictional lands of Calradia desribed as "torn asunder by incessant warfare". Calradia has 6 factions, each specialized in a different way of warfare, creating a good balance between all factions. You can pick up some great horsemen from Swadia, accurate crosbowmen from the Rhodoks and awesome infantry from the Nords, or any combination that suits you best. Historical accuracy isn't great (although most troops are based uppon real troops), but for someone looking for a different kind of medival simulator/strategy game its real fun.
Graphics aren't great, but they are good enough to feel immersion and the game doesn't rely on its graphics anyway. The combat mechanics are fun, although I don't think this game is a good buy for someone looking for a game with a strong MP, as the MP is this game is more or less just someting you from time to time to improve your combat skill for the singleplayer.
The game offers a lot of ways to be played, from merchant to thief, from commander to manhunter. It is up to you. This is one of the strongest pros this game has. As the game is so open and sandbox like, anyone can find a way to enjoy himself, as long as you are intrested in medival games.
Although I haven't played a single mod (I dislike modificatons made in any game) the modding comunity is really active and besides the main game offers thousands of hours of additional fun.
Pros

-Lots of replay value (as it is sandbox)
-Mods offer an insane amount of content
-Offers multiplayer, which is fun
Cons
-Not the greatest graphics
-Not very optimized (mainly with big battles)
-Multiplayer is a little bit underwhelming

As mentioned numerous times already, WRC 6 is a significant improvement over the previous titles in this series. Perhaps the biggest endorsement of this game I can offer, is to say that after playing 210 hours of Dirt Rally (the benchmark against which all rally titles will now be measured), I still immediately enjoyed WRC 6. Well, almost immediately - I had to experiment with the wheel settings for about 30 minutes before finding settings I was satisfied with.  It was definitely worth it, as the game quickly went from being mediocre, to very, very good. I'm using a Fanatec CSR Elite and the feedback and feel is excellent.
Anyway, let's get on with inevitable Dirt Rally comparison. While the game isn't as visually spectacular as Dirt Rally, the graphics are a marked improvement on previous versions, and generally very pleasing to the eyes.  The game doesn't appear to be too demanding of your hardware either, and will run in 1080p at very high settings on my machine (which has a fairly modest spec sheet by today's standards). I have no complaints about the audio either. Again, probably not quite up to Dirt's standards, but more than adequate nonetheless.
The physics? Well, that will really depend on your perspective, but for me, WRC 6 falls short of Dirt Rally in this regard, as the physics simply don't have that realistic simulation feel.  If however, you prefer less challenging, 'arcade' style physics, then you'll likely enjoy the car behaviour in WRC 6 more than Dirt Rally.  I turned the settings to simulation and turned off all assists, and I find the handling to be a good balance between arcade and simulation, and for the most part, challenging enough to be enjoyable.
WRC 6 also can't compete with Dirt Rally for variety of content, the latter offering Hill Climb and Rally Cross events in addition to the standard Rally events. These additions are by no means a novelty either, they are brilliantly executed, and keep you coming back for more.  WRC 6 does however offer an esports competition, an officail online WRC if you like, which is a great addition for all of us wannabe WRC drivers.
If it's starting to sound like a one-sided fight, and a clear victory for Dirt Rally, well it's not quite that simple. If, like me, you're a WRC fanatic, then WRC 6 trumps Dirt in one key area - official content. You get all 14 rounds of the 2016 championship, all the official drivers, teams, cars etc. which is very appealing for hardcore WRC fans. The stages are fanatstic too.  Rally enthusiasts will be pleased to know that the stages are now properly narrow, and some of those stages are now also seriously long, and will really test your concentration levels.
Objectively, WRC 6 falls short of Dirt Rally in almost every way, but it's a game that seems to be greater than the sum of its parts, and for me, is at times even more enjoyable than Codies' recent masterpiece.  Time will tell if WRC 6 has the enduring appeal of Dirt Rally, but at the moment I'm loving it, and can't see myself getting bored of it anytime soon.

The minute I saw the gameplay footage, I just knew I had to play this game. After about 10 minutes of fumbling around for a server (there are serverside issues), I finally got in a game. And I was in for a treat.
There are 10 maps, each has a unique theme and gamemode. There are 5 weapons, and you start out with all of them when you spawn. The weapons are all unique, from the simple assault rifle to the one shot-kill rocket launcher (which is a bit op). There are no power-ups, no killstreaks, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Period. Weeeeeelll, except for the rocket launcher, because you get one shot with it per life (unless you survive long enough for its long cooldown to reset), and so every time you respawn you get a shot. Often gameplay progresses as:
1. Shoot someone with the rocket launcher
2. Someone shoots you with the rocket launcher
3. Respawn and get another rocket launcher shot
So theres the only balancing issue I see. The only way I can see to fix this is to make the Rocket Launcher a powerup or killstreak bonus, or some other way.
EDIT: They nerfed the rocket launcher- cooldown now carries over between deaths. This is a noticeable improvement. Thanks devs.
Additionally, there are some gamemodes where it is impossible for either side to score, and 90% of the time it ends in a tie. Those maps are Kitchen Run and Barnyard Ball.
In Kitchen Run, neither side can make it to the cup because the map is so linear. I'm thinking you should add some more paths through the donuts at the midway point to mix things up, because the donut area is just a huge bloodbath where very few make it past. Let alone do any players make it past the stove or sink.
It is so hard to score in Barnyard Ball because the ball always ends up on the edges where the flippers aren't, and the ball always gets stuck in the corner. I'd suggest making the edges and corners of the table at a slight incline to keep the ball somewhat closer to the middle area where the flippers are.
Also, there is NO progression system. I am opposed to unlockable combat bonuses, but here is my simple idea for progression:
It would kind of work like Rocket League, in that you get a random cosmetic after every fully completed game. There could be categories of unlockables, like hats, gun skins, and "backpack" style items.
Hats would be monochromatic to match your team color.
Gun skins would be patterned, like tiger stripes or camo.
Backpack items would be small real-world items, like paper clips or pencil-top erasers. Maybe even those little toothpick flags you get in martinis.
Those are just my ideas. This game has so much potential, and the devs currently have a fairly big audience, but I don't want to see this game die like Titanfall and so many other games have. You guys have a captive audience, now keep us entertained! :3

EDIT: Oct 26    I must change my rating for recommending this game to warn all who may consider buying. At first the team was interactive with the customer and I truly believed the few "bugs" would be fixed. Sadly I believe the main"bug" of rapid frame drops and micro stuttering is not something this team is experienced or cares enough to fix, and it is deal breaker for anyone interested in this game because if anything it has gotten worse just like last years attempt at "fixing" it with 2 versions of V-SYNC, neither of which fixes the problem. Yes it does help, but in 2016 and this being their second attempt at this title, they have failed the customer again. So in closing-unless by some miracle they fix this game breaking issue-along with some other "bugs" like the pace note calling being rubbish and sounding like some crazy mad man is in the car screaming certain calls usually too late, save your money . I have above the recommended specs for this game and run it on medium and still have the stuttering and frame drops, so its definately not my rig. Have a GTX970 iCore5 6500 16 GB of DDR4 2133MhZ ram, so you be the judge on why it still runs crappy?
WRC 6 first off is NOT in the same league as Dirt Rally, but, it really cant be and still be sold to the masses. Rally is a cliche already, and to make it as real and difficult as Dirt would not help sales. I will say that I own all 6 WRC titles and WRC 6 which was made by this same developer is a HUGE improvement over last year. The cars seem to be a little more in touch with the road and the different surfaces. the tracks are quite different than any previous title and vary enough to keep you interested. Now ehn WRC 5 came out last year I purchased it and gave it a recommend, then they tryed to fix it and did more harm than good. This year there doesnt seem to be as many issues as last year except for the V-Sync , screen tearing issue. Not as bad for me as for some others, but, still present and the most dissappointing issue about the title. I have a GTX970 and Windows 10 64 bit, iCore5 6600 and msi Motherboard, 16 GB DDR 4 2133 MhZ,  not the best, but pretty good, and I dont have hardly any FPS drops or screen tearing issues as I have heard some complain of  the game has a lot of different ways to play, hot seat being one of my favorites, and you can start at WRC JR and work your way up in career mode. You can design your own championship with any class and put the rallies in any order or just your favorites. All in all, good FFB and not bad physics if you choose sim mode.  I am very hopeful that the few issues there are will be given the proper attention and be fixed, the main problem being the PACENOTES. They dont come on time even adjusting the timing in menu and sound ridiculous, takes away from the immersiveness of the rally. The FOV and no rear view nor seat adjustments are unconscionable in a new title when they should be included as a no brainer. The rear view is what I think is a big issue mainly when you are playing head to head against someone, and i always like to take a gander back once in a while in the game just to see what i hit and the damage it caused.  In my opinion (and I own all of the modern games RRRE  Dirt Project CARS Assetto Corsa Automobilista) to name a few and enjoy sims more than arcade racers, but, this is good enough to own if you enjoy racing games and want the WRC lisence experience. I would say that if you liked GRID Autosport and its sim-cade experience, than this is as good at least as that.

Ok I'll keep this brief.  Bought this game having already played DIRT RALLY loads using G27.  I had to tweak that game a lot until I was happy and only when I stumbled upon the amazing Irish REAL RALLY DRIVER settings (can't remember the guy's name) - much LIGHTER settings, less is more, get that wheel light and movable rather than all heavy and stodgy.
Was initially immediately dissapointed with WRC 6, it felt terrible - FFB felt plastic WAY WAY TOO HEAVY and also relying WAY too much on the self-aligning torque of the wheel itself rather than any actual feel from the road/tyres etc.
HOWEVER - after tweaking around with the wheel settings and logitech profiler. and the in game settings I got things feeling pretty close to what I was used to in DR and AFTER A FEW STAGES WAS HAVING ALMOST AS MUCH FUN AS DIRT RALLY, although there is clearly less detail in the feel and the graphics aren't as immersive.
I am now happy with this game and don't regret the purchase, in fact it's nice to have a Rally Game which is slightly less involved than DR and also a little easier once you get used to it.
If you're happy with lighter FFB settings on your wheel for Rally Driving (and you should be, less is more in Rally Driving!), this game CAN be made to work.    Here are my settings for G27:
Logitech Profiler (Excatly the same as 'REAL RALLY DRIVER' recommendations for DR):
Overall Strength: 57%
Spring Effect: 0
Damper: 0
Enable Spring 0% (not checked)
Degrees of ROtation: 655
Use Special Game Settings (UNCHECKED - unusual, but works for me)
In Game Settings;
Accel Sens: 20
Accell Dead: 0
Brake Sens:20
Brake Dead: 0
Steering Sens: 30
Steering Dead: 0
Force Feedback: 5%  (yes light as a feather guys it's what you need for decent Rally Driving!)
Levle of Vibration: 65%
Max Wheel Angle: 900  (yes this doesn't match the profiler , but it works, and grades the FFB right for me).
Well each to his own, I think if you prefer HEAVIER wheel settings WRC 6 probably cannot be made to feel good because the weight is achieved in a terribly crude way in their FFB, not sure why it is so poor.  But  for LIGHT settings it;s not so much an issue.

Ok, maybe I am a little crazy, but for FUN, I think this is better than dirt. Quick summary:
PLUSES (vs. Dirt).
- Controls and handling much more fun using a controller than dirt (I could never get settings with Dirt I felt comfortable with). See below though.

- Decent damage model (but see below)
50/50 with DIRT:
- Graphics. Dirt in some ways better (particles, some effects - windshield say, and headlights), but I think WRC 6 graphics are close and have their own advantages. I prefer the WRC cars, helped by the offical liveries, and they get dirtier without the mod you can get for Dirt. Stage graphics are even IMHO.
- Sound (apart from co-driver!). I think the WRC sounds are good, and I like the crowd atmosphere.
DIRT IS BETTER:

Both Sims 2 and Sims 3 are the best games in the series, although Sims 3 has a lot of bugs. Most of them are easy to fix though. I will write a list of bugs and how to fix them, and then the major game breaking bug I'm still trying to fix.
These are glitches I ran into in my 58 hours of playtime with all expansion packs installed:
1. Sims getting stuck in a frozen position.  How to fix: use cheat "resetsim first and last name"
2. University seems to be stuck in loading screen. How to fix: Edit town right before going to University, although you can also wait it out, but it loads for like 30 minutes.
3. Can't adopt stray cat or dog even though you are BFF with it. Fix not confirmed, but might work: ask stray to leave, and when it returns the adopt option will appear.
4. Sim stuck in sneak mode after getting grounded. How to fix: Either send your sim to boarding school, or go to edit town, evict your family with their house, bulldoze the empty house, place the family and house back where it was.
5. Can't use bed. How to fix: The same fix as glitch number 4. Not the boarding school fix, the eviction fix.
6. Can't get mail. How to fix: use the buydebug on cheat and testingcheatsenabled true, shift click the mail box, click object, click delete it, go to debug buy menu and buy a new mailbox.
7. Grim Reaper not taking away dead sims. How to fix: This glitch means the grim reaper is stuck, just do resetsim Grim Reaper in the cheat menu to fix it. Reset the dead sim where the reaper got stuck too if you can find the stuck reaper.
8. Bowl of food or any object getting stuck in your sim's hand. how to fix: resetsim first name and last name.
9. Certain sound effects stopped working. How to fix: save your game and load it again or relaunch the game.
10.  The worst most game breaking glitch of all, and the one I only know a one time fix for... Sims stop aging when your new generation sims have a baby, even though aging is on. I tried a few stuff that the devs said would work, but it didn't work. I fixed the issue once with the help of a youtube video, but that fix only works once. If your aging stops again, it won't work. That trick is to go to main menu and copy your saved town by clicking copy town next to the delete button, and then play the copied town. Aging will be back in working order until your 3rd generation's baby grew up into a toddler. That's where I'm stuck at the moment, and I searched for a solution for quite some time. People say either use mods or start a new game and delete the old save. I refuse to delete my save though, I played 58 hours with my family. Also, I don't want to download any mods, because the mods changes some things I don't want to change, plus I don't know how to mod games in general. I hope you found my fixes helpful though, and I hope one of you guys can give me a permanent fix that always works once the sims stop aging, because I really want to continue playing with my family.
Why do I still recommend this game? Because it's excellent and the world feels alive and completely dynamic and open world.  It not only feels that way, it is that way. Literally. For example, while you are living your life, other sims will live theirs, and you can see them do it. They move, get married, have kids, adopt pets, age, die, go to visit others, visit the park and other places, etc, plus you can affect their lives by interacting with them, like you can break up a couple by kissing someone in front of his or her lover, etc. I bought all the expansions in the sale for about $74. Great game, lots of content, and if it's 75% off, affordable if you want to buy all dlc.  As I said, the only bad thing about the game is the bugs. The aging bug in particular. I heard some people had success moving them out and back in, but I haven't tried it yet. Anyways, if you got the money and you like sims or the genre in general, you will love this game. Just use my glitch fix list if you want a smooth experience.

Having ruthlessly torn this game to shreds as I am like to do with other games that have an exploration focus, I feel like I should weigh in some regarding the games issues.
1. Microtransactions: while they didnt bother me during the game, it's something I disapprove of based on principal. If I paid 60$ i should have the whole game yes?
2. Story pacing: Very little to speak of. It meanders and it frolics around prague with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s of loooooong loadtimes whenever Jensen steps onto a subway (more on that later). Jensen has these super important secret agent missions with worldwide implications, and dicking around prague is far more interesting. The side activities seem too vital, and the main objectives feel pushed to the side. Besides, this game feels quite scaled down from it's predeccessor, Human Revolution. In that game, you were flying all over the world, taking down illuminati conspiracies and black ops teams to stop a global catastrophy. In Mankind Divided your flying all over Prague to save four buildings in london. It ends abruptly, I feel like 2-3 missions were cut at the end.
3. Prague: as pretty as the hub is at first, it feels streched VERY thin by the end, especially if the player has been doing all of the side missions/ points of interest. If the devs had made a second hub even half as big as prague they would have avoided this complaint. Kudos to the Devs however, they managed to cram a TON of content into the area.
4. Load times: I would venture as far as to say that about 1/5th of my playtime was spent on prague subways, and my computer is an expensive box, circa~ 2014. The optimisation feels atrocious at times.
This is still a good game for fans of stealth/ exploration/ cyberpunk, and the graphics are fantastic, but I would wait for a sale, or at least a game of the year edition or something of that sort.

This game has very much aged well and is still one of the best Free 2 Play MMORPG's you can play up to date. With enough servers to hold all of Asia the playerbase is lacking but other wise it really feels that you are playing in a Middle-Earth. Still holding the famous areas in the books and movies such as the Shire this game stays faithful and true to its roots while having hidden lore. Gameplay wise the game feels like a standard MMORPG, the movement feels a little stiff and there is a small time delay when attacking. The leveling system has a god touch to it giving you the choice on what skills to level up and what route on your character to take such as if you want healing moves and skills you can level that up instead of a tank route. The exploration and the map in the game is pretty massive and can take a while to get from point A to B. While getting from one point to another I found myself in situations where I would have to sneek my way through enemies who were much stronger than me, some might not like this but I found that this gave the game a little bit more realism since in real life you usually wouldn't fight someone much stronger than you, you would usually find a way around it. I do find that this game, like others gives a Pay 2 Win aspect but it's not as bad as you think it usually has to deal with horses and other means of transportaion/ mounts. I recommend grabbing friends to play with this since bosses in quests can be difficult by yourself depending on what class and level you are, you can even make a guild and buy a house if you grab enough people and money. If you want to troll your friends become a tank character and challenge them to a 1v1 and destroy them, trust me it has some feeling of accomplishment in it. The music in this game sounds average, not giving masterpeices but also not giving the game a bland feel to the game when questing. I give this game a 7/10 it would be bigger but it doesn't have a big enough player-base as it should to feel like you're actually in Middle-Earth along with stiff controls, but if you're looking for a new MMORPG grab some friends order some pizza and play this it might just suprsise you.

After about 450 hours of playtime, I feel safe writing a small review on this game.
No subscription required, you pay once and get into "premium mode", (which is pretty cheap) which allows you to unlock all cosmetics, premium content, and even expansions, for free via achievement rewards.
- Very active playerbase on several servers (notably Brandywine and Landroval, the latter being a RP server).
- Content is actively released, with patches coming out on a frequent basis.
- Explore Middle-earth, from the Blue Mountains to Mirkwood and Gondor.
- The main storyline is actually enjoyable (unlike most other MMORPGs) and is very well-made, from start to finish.
- Quests and events are ideally structured in a LOTR concept while avoiding clashes with tolkienist lore.
- Crafting is really fleshed-out and is more fun than in most other MMORPGs.
- Detailed housing system, you can even craft your own furniture.
- Graphics are nice to look at, even though they're outdated by a few years.
- World events and holidays are present and come often, but never fall to being an annoyance.
- Subscription fees are lower than the typical MMORPG; $10 a month.
- The western coastlines of Eriador (Lindon) are not going to be developed.
- A lot of places seem underdeveloped.
- Lack of variety early-game.
- Only about 50% of Middle-earth has been developed thus far.
- PvP is somewhat shallow.
- F2P players will run out of content around level 30; they will have to consistently grind to unlock new content after that (It takes about 6-18 hours of grinding to unlock a zone as a F2P).
- The /dance emote is horrible. Unlock a new one as quickly as possible.
This is a game that should be noted by any fan of the MMORPG genre.
It's a perfect game for any LOTR fan to play alone or with friends. Great quests, and a large community (on most servers).
I would highly recommend this game: 9/10.

As I'm experiencing hardware problems I can't finish the game yet, but I strongly feel the need to recommend Dreaming Sarah to anyone who might be interested. As time goes I might update my review.
This game definitely draws inspiration from a certain cult classic (which I haven't played myself), but tells its story from a different
perspective. The whole atmosphere is what sets it apart. The smoothest controls possible, seamless interaction with environment, so far very intuitive cues as to what to do and where to go, even without the
. It's also been a very long time since I heard music so powerful in conveying surroundings and emotions.
Dreaming Sarah's particular pixel art style is easy on the eyes. Doesn't impose itself on you, but lets you admire calming, eerie, solemn, and perilous sceneries for as long as you want, all splendidly drawn and implemented.
If you are a fan of interactive art, where things happen because you as a player are in a game, then this is for you.
If you enjoy lovingly made visuals and sound, then Dreaming Sarah will definitely impress you.

If your the type of person who would jump off a cliff if someone asked you to, this might be the game for you.
The game is all about base jumping on a acid city replica of Boston, Massachusetts, some natural mountain landscapes and even places which look like they have been ripped out of the movie '5th element'.
The object is simple 'don't become a flattened pancake'. The other objective is to get a 5 star high score so you can earn 'teeth' the in-game currency (that's what we going to use when we run out of paper?) which you can spend to unlock more levels. Each level you complete you get treated to some funny news announcements or instructional videos. One video teaches you the do's and don'ts of accidental time travel, another video teaches you grandma's secret ingredient in her choc chip cookies being human remains and the list goes on. Most of these are either novel or groan out loud weakly executed attempts of humor.
There are a number of ways to build up your score. The main one is to kiss a building (get so close you can plant your smackers on it) and to hug them (free fall down at a constant close distance), but you can also do other things such as give a two fingered salute to red spectators (Mr Bean is Professional at that) and a thumbs up to blue ones, you can also graffiti tag certain buildings on your way down, smash into a bird, hit various glass colored plates for money, or perform the very tricky thread a needle move.
Most of the time you will struggle to do any of this as you will be too busy in a g spin of certain death since the controls are ridiculously hard to master. Hit a building and you become a human pinball against concrete flippers. I dare you to smoke a joint and try this with rift. You will be vomiting up your lungs as your characters nasal passage begins to smell the back of his brain thanks to the constant concrete jungle your treated to.
With all these things going on and it's unique game style you would think that this would be thumbs up material. It ISN'T. The game gets tedious and laborious fast. It gets too difficult too quickly, you might get 5 stars on two of the levels if your lucky. While it is possible to get 5 stars on the other levels, still you will soon discover that you will need to spend this life time, and your next reincarnated life time, or your next eternal life on a paradise earth, or your next life time being burnt alive forever and ever, but look on the bright side least you don't have to get five stars on this anymore.
The other reason it's thumbs down is because there is another version on Steam which is exactly the same, but contains more content with more 'polished' controls since it uses a different game engine. The other game is called 'AaAaAAAA!!! - for the awesome'. So if your interested "Go! .... Go Jump off a cliff!.... What are you waiting for??? .... JUMP!!!!"

I bought this game a long time ago but never reviewed it. My problem with this game was that you couldnt look where you were supposed to go without speeding up. And controlling your speed was critical.
.....So the game is simple; jump off of a building, avoid obstacles, direct yourself though bonus areas for points, or just follow the fastest route.
.....Unfortunately, looking in a given direction moves you in that direction. So you have no control over your body, just your head. So if you look straight down, so you can see where you're going, you accelerate down. Faster and faster until you can't change direction fast enough to survive. Looking up or to the side slows you down, but then you can't see where you're going.
.....On the other hand; while you can't control your body, it can kill you. For example, you are directed to skirt certain objects for bonus points, but if you got too close, your body would hit them and you died. The margin for error was tiny, and extremely frustrating.
.....I have this game listed under those games that should have been fun, but weren't.

It's a hard one to rate but after more playtime I have decided to rate it up.  The AI is a good challenge, the story mode is awesome, there's a lot more content than the old arcade style towers.  The graphics are amazing and the gore is A+.  You can earn easy finishers so you can play random characters without learning all of their finishing combos.  And there is a lot of content for a fighting game.
As for the multiplayer, this is the big con.
Ranking system infinitely places you against seemingly "random" opponents, rather than opponents of "same skill".  I have literally never won a single battle in online play.  Yeah, maybe I'm a noob, then why the hell am I facing opponents who have 3x wins over losses and hundreds of wins?  Why am I facing literally UNDEFEATED opponents?
Trash ranking system.  Leaves a sour taste in the mouth and an incredibly unpleasant experience overall, which isn't something you want when playing a game for fun lol.  All in all, if you're okay with just the single player aspects of the game, I rate it up.  If you want to play with friends locally using two controllers, I rate it up.  If you want to play online and ranked, better learn to "juggle" your opponents endlessly in the air, because that's what they'll do to you, and if you try to play "legit" with just the 3-hit combos and power moves and block timings, you will be sourly disappointed when you get juggled by some noob.

Featuring both offline and online play, the goal is this board game adaptation is to accumulate victory points by (primarily) activating industries. Cotton mills and ports are activated by selling cotton at a port, while coal mines and iron works are activated once all of their resources have been used by other buildings or upgrades. Shipyards are automatically activated once built but require upgrades before they can be constructed. Money (the income of which is increased as industries become activated) is used to construct buildings in specific locations on the map, but only if a card displaying the city or type of industry is in hand. Canals, and later railroads, are used to connect cities, allow for more construction, and transport goods. Upgrading buildings will produce more victory points when activated, and loans can be taken as well. Halfway through each game, canals and level 1 buildings disappear, leading to a second scramble to develop. It takes several games to understand all the nuances of Brass, but the game does support multiple strategies for victory. The AI is good at the game as well, providing a very capable opponent. There are some stability issues with the game locking up during AI turns and crashing upon exiting, but overall Brass is a decent computer adaptation of the board game.
