This is my first and only negative review about a racing game, or any product.  Having said that I will start with the positive bits.  The physics are improved over WRC 5, but not as much as people say in their reviews.  I love the special stages, and wish I could import them into Assetto somehow, but that's not the point is it? The game is fun as an arcade game, but in our age of Dirt Rally, Assetto Corsa, and Rfactor 2, no developer has business creating a rally game where you don't need to use the hand brake.  Using it made me slower on the simulation setting, so I just tried turning and braking like in WRC 5 on the same simulation setting and I was able to do a perfect drift each time.
Ok, that was the positive part, if you can call it that.  The physics and feedback people talk about is nothing but a constant rattle of the wheel.  My fanatac was just rattling no matter what the terrain was, or how big the bumps were.  This fake feeling of feeback from the tires and road just became annoying after a short time.  This game is not in the same league as Dirt Rally in any area except SS tracks, and for my money nowhere close to Sebastien Loeb Rally Evo either.  What SLRE had going for it was one very simple little thing, the feel of weight transfer of the vehicle when braking.  I believe that they nailed that over any other rally game in history, and i'm sure it's thanks to Loeb, but people trash it cause understandably they were expecting the greatest rally game ever made, because of how great he was.  I won't compare this to RBR.
The cartoon like graphics don't bother me so much.  In fact, they make the environment more lively and pretty.  However, what developers need to realize is that those types of graphics make colours bleed into each other, which makes it hard to see the road.  The reason realistic graphics work is because it creates a visual contrast that allows you to look further down the road.
I actually feel kind of bad giving this game a bad review, because generally I love racing games, simracing games, and especially rally racing games, and would love to encourage developers to make more of them.  I hope that the develper listens to the community and gives us a proper rally game that feels like a rally game.  If they only fixed the fake ffb (fffb), and fixed the physics so drifts don't feel assisted in simulation mode (so you have to use a handbrake to go faster around hairpins), I would completely recommend it.

For a fan-made short game I have to say I enjoyed this.
I would recommend it to anyone who is a fan of the half-life series. The game follows a linear path with some set pieces throughout similar to what you would expect (to the game's credit). The game does a good job of setting the atmosphere and tone something inbetween Ravenholm and the opening City 17 section.
There are some great ideas here, but I will list some both things done well and criticisms (understand, this was made by a small team, it is free, and it willt ake you 1-2 hours to finish depending on your pace (rush through vs explore):
Pro: As mentioned earlier the atmosphere, good set pieces (one in particular was very well done and fresh), new music fits well with the series previous, I actually finished it from start to finish and wanted more -- I felt as if I was playing the Valve official title.
Cons: Story could have used some... more (I suppose that's what they were going for, but you'll see what I mean
, difficulty was tuned too easy and I couldn't up it... I appreciate not being frustrated, but there was almost zero challenge here taking no damage from anything. If you have no history with the half-life series, this game is worth playing, but don't expect to be blown away -- it is a bit dated (half life 2 came out so long ago)... however a testament to the source engine that it can still hold up without feeling unplayable.
Overall, I wanted more. So well done to the developers if you are reading this.
I suppose Half-Life 3 is going to elude us since Valve is unlikely to divert resources away from Steam which is their real source of cash, so I'll be happy anytime someone takes the time and effort to put together a project like this.

If you enjoy Diablo 3 you'll probably love this game. Almost identical interface and very similar play style. I like Torchlight II mostly because it's more Diablo, but much more colourful.

Great gameplay, great pacing, great diversity.
Don't be fooled by the mere four class choices. Each class has an astounding variety of potential builds and weaponsets (that is, if you're not going for super hardcore Elite or min/maxing). You can be an Embermage with a deadly hammer. Or a wand-totting, glaive-tossing Outlander.
Combat is quick and fast-paced, but not brainless. Charging mindlessly into monster hordes will most definitely get you killed. Melee classes are a blessedly wonderful challenge to keep alive in this game. One thing to note is that this game is much more fun with friends.
All that said, the unique art style of Torchlight II may not be for everyone. The story appears deep, but its seriousness is slightly compromised by its cartoonish art (I kind of laughed at/brushed off everything). Still, that's not the main focus of Torchlight II, to me at least. Get it for its gameplay. Story's just the icing on the cake for this one.
10/10 It won't disappoint you, especially if you are a fan of hack and slash.

First of all: I like the game.
Even though I played
a ton, it took me a little while to adjust to the UI and controls although they are virtually the same as in the old one. Once you learn the parameters of what you can do and when and where to do it in this game, then it becomes easy again.
Second of all: I think it's a showcase for exceptional greed that there's already a DLC out even though the game has only been out for 1 month at the time of me writing this. They must've held back the release of this content to earn extra money. - The "once per save" purchase of praxis kits is another sign of this greed that screams to the heavens that Square Enix is infected with greedy business men, instead of primarily gaming minded individuals.
- I liked that the controls were pretty much the same as they were in Human Revolution.
- The main mission(s) and story was alright, though they didn't feel as epic as they did in Human Revolution.
- The side missions (that I found) are pretty interesting. One in particular blew my mind, since I could've so easily missed it if I hadn't bumped into something accidently, stopping me in my tracks and noticed it, instead of doing what I usually do and sprint around between objectives that are already active.
- There's a ton to explore and it seems to me to be the main meat of this game, to get excited about finding new paths, hidden areas and figuring out the mini puzzles of how to get to them.
- How many different ways there are to do objectives. Sometimes it's almost a bit too much how many different ways there are to complete them. One thing in particular that I liked was that I had seemingly failed some side missions, when looking at when other people on my friendlist had completed them in their playthroughs, but in some of the cases you get a second chance to rectify things.
- Great music!(!!!!)
- Great work by the dev team, that seemed to be held back by their greedy publishers. ->
- The greed of Square Enix. I really hate that those money grubbing individuals that first came up with the tiered pre-order scheme, then this "praxis kit"-one use thing and now this early DLC, are having $$$$$-$ign$ in their eyes, to the point where they ruin the game. Btw you don't need to buy those praxis points at all, but the way Square Enix seems to be going, they'll probably tighten the noose in future releases, so you can only barely get through games without buying extra things in their online store.
I can understand that Square Enix want money for their products, but when the game itself, that is fairly short unless you dig into every nook and cranny, costs 50€, then a 12€ DLC 1 month after the release is just greedy.
- It feels a bit "consolly" to me, with a sometimes bit clunky and big UI and the way you can make Jensen move from his hidding places via a path-line. The hacking minigame also feels a bit clunky and big in the same way, but it can be excused I guess. The map was also not the best. All in all it's a not that bad, but weighed on the negative side for me.
- Lipsynching was subpar. The lips and speech simply didn't fit eachother. Perhaps it's a 2029 augmentation that makes speech-impaired people able to clearly sound out words, even though their mouth movement is all over the place. And a few animations were not that good as well. The new "wallpunch" was a bit "meh" for instance, where the rubble would stay in the hole and Jensen's punch didn't feel quite as "1-inch death punchy" as it was in Human Revolution.
- Just one city hub, Prague, that is reused in different ways as events unfold. You do get to visit other places, but only as closed instances.
- A few bugs, some annoying ones, like one I had where I would stay in zoom in mode after every hack I did. I could be helped by unholstering items, but was annoying none-the-less. I think I crashed once during one of the first days after release, so the game is otherwise stable though, for me at least.

An iconic and amazing series and MD delivers in terms of combat, conspiracy and the atmosphere that we have grown to love from this series.
However... we have a flaw.  A flaw that stops this game reaching the height of praise the majority of its predecessors recieved.
This flaw is apparant on loading the game in the form of an unwelcome "Shop" selling praxis points for real money.  And it must be noted these points (which I absolutely recommend you do not buy) damage game balance and are only valid for 1 playthrough.  Next we have the addition of "Breach Mode", a tacked on mode that is both uninspired and a cash grab.
All this would be more of an annoyance if it had not impacted the main game, which appears far shorter than it should have been.   To add insult to injury the first story DLC is nothing more than a glorified advertisement for Bleach mode, more evidence of unwanted interferance from a publisher that is damaging the integrity of this great series.
The game is still very good despite these flaws, however due to the negatives above I must give it a negative review - not because I did not enjoy it because at its core it is glorious and it has clearly been made by an amazing development team.  We must send a message to publishers that unwanted implementation of ingame shops and manipulating dlc to push freemium aspects of a single player game are not wanted.

I really liked Deus Ex MD. I've been a fan of the series, yes, including Deus Ex Invisible War, since the first release in 2000.
For people complaining about paying for stuff in the game, the only way I even found out about that stuff was by people complaining in reviews. I haven't even found out how to do that in game and I've beat it entirely. People are giving this game way too much crap for something that clearly isn't forced or well shown.
For the actual game, it was great. The gameplay is close to Human Revolution but not exactly, you can clearly see improvements in systems and more emphesis on stealth while still providing great combat choices. Hacking is great as always.
Spoilers are below.
Your choices matter like in the previous games and they show you the consequences for those actions. Just like in every Deus Ex. One thing they did remove is any other city in the game. You go to other places but the main place is prague which includes 4-5 seperate locations. The city is huge and there is a ton of side missions with things to do but one thing I loved Deus Ex for is that you got to see the entire world as it would be in the future, not just a city. One of the things missing is a good tie to any of the other locations. You don't get side missions in them (that aren't alternatives to your current objective) and you don't feel that connection to the world of knowing people and having favors owed to you all over the world.
With that small exception this game still holds up as one of the best in the series. I would say it's better than the first in some regards and certainly better than Human Revolution which is not an easy feat.

I really hate to give this game a thumbs down. I really do. But as of this writing the game simply feels unbalanced and a little rough. The game is gorgeous, exciting, and very promising however. It is sorely lacking a local splitscreen or bot mode. I kind of wanted to just sort of drop in on a game and play casually for an hour or so...but no. That doesn't happen in this game. Newcomers in this game get SLAUGHTERED. The rocket launcher is completely OP and such a cheap kill that it just feels unsatisfying. Meanwhile the flamethrower I'm convinced actually does nothing. The grenade physics are extremely dodgy. I always felt like I was kinda dropping a grenade in a general direction instead of actually throwing it. the "join game" option on the main menu is completely broken. I was only able to play using the server browser. Game was dropped almost at the end of each match I played.  I admittedly didn't play very long, but the combat is pretty simple and there are only a handful of weapons (sniper rifle, flamethrower, rpg, machine gun, shotgun). Gameplay was just frustrating and unsatisfying even when I got a kill. The only reliable feeling waepon is the machine gun. Even the sniper rifle is extremely unwieldy and severely limits your vision in a way that defeats the purpose of using it. Level design is amazing on the other hand.
Bottom line is this game needs some ironing out in the gameplay dept. It needs a local or single player bot mode so it could flourish as a party game (rocket league, towerfall, toybox turbos etc) and offer players the chance to practice and have fun with the game offline. It also needs a class system or something...mannable turrets, vehicles, more weapons. Something to break up the monotany of "obligatory RPG kill, dodge, roll, crouch, grenade spam, get shot, repeat". I thought I was getting a fun "sarge's heroes" style party game shooter but its much more punishing than that and difficult to have fun playing tbh.

Thanks to a close friend of mine, this game is now on my nightly play list. To think such a simple concept could present amazing hours of entertainment and laughs. I'll go over my personal pros and cons of this game and hope it helps you decide on what's best for you.
Graphics:- Don't like the colors fool you, everything in this game is done for a reason and it shows. The models look great, very much on the level of the army men in Toy Story, these soldiers run, jump and roll like you would expect them to.  The level designs are very original and immersive, you truly feel like a small toy inside a large world.
Sound:- WOW, just wow, if there is anything that you should take the time to appreciate is the sound.  The BG is just fitting for all stages that you play on, from the Christmas jingle on the railway to the swinging tunes that pump you up as you race across the table to push a giant cup, yes a giant cup.  If that weren't enough, on the birthday cake level, attacking sides are greeted to a jazz "attack the cake" verse while defenders hold the line with "defend the cake." Its those little details that really make you smile as you play along with the ecosystem of the game.
Gameplay:- When it comes movement and gun play, the game holds strong. A simple enough scheme, fire and alt fire, its one of those where its easy to play,not too hard to master. Within a few rounds you should have a great feel for all the weapons and know when to use each weapon for the situation at hand.
Replay:- Loads of it, as the outcome of each match can be very different.  From capture the flag, to lighting candles on a cake, to scoring a goal on a large Foosball table, there's a ton to do and experience in this addicting game.
Cons:- People complaining the game has no future. The game has only been out a week, but i can tell you that this game is here to stay. I've had the honor of having a dev or two in my channel asking for feedback, that alone shows that they care about their game and wish for it to be enjoyed by all.
In the end, you should really play this one and see for yourself if you like it or not. I do feel that this a fantastic game for the price they are asking. The devs care and are listening as they too want to make sure that you're getting the best bang for your buck!
Cheers

WRC 6 is a definite step up in many areas compared to the previous installments in the series. Gone from WRC 5 are the graphical glitches and sudden FPS drops, as well as the very unrealistic sounds of the cars.
It's not "dirt rally quality" although it's not trying to be. It's very much focussed at the arcade/casual crowd from consoles, however it does do a very good job for an arcade game. FFB and wheel options are ok with a G27 but it feels much better with a gamepad I've found so far. With more tracks and cars than WRC 5 had, as well as a visual overhaul of the routes you race on and improved car handling physics, it's a decent game I've had fun playing.
How much you want to pay for it is up to you, but it's certainly not a game to avoid because of bugs or bad gameplay like previous games in the series.

Deus Ex (original) was a phenominal game because it married open-ended, intelligent gameplay with an open-ended, intelligent story.
This game expands slightly on the gameplay choices by offering new augments. Taking down guards and stacking them high is as satisfying as ever, whether you do so lethally or non-lethally. Creeping around hacking computers and reading emails is still fun. Crawling through vents, busting walls and leaping across electrified pools to find secret areas and alternate routes to objectives still makes you feel as though you're an ultimate badass exploiting the world to your whim.
But whilst the depth of gameplay is still there, the depth of story has utterly disappeared. Gone are the epic plotlines about worldwide government conspiracies, manufactured viruses, shadowy organisations, aliens and illuminati. Gone are the torturing moral choices and non-linear decisions. What we have here is a simple cut-and-dry case of a terrorist attack, which over the course of a few acts you uncover and then have to stop. There are no moral decisions, and no choices - even the two minor decisions you are asked to make during the game can be mitigated or bypassed.
The environments look beautiful on the surface. But there are only 3 or 4 of them. The majority of the game all takes part in the same small city, which despite some lighting variety in the red light district and the sewers is all fairly similar.
The screen filter effects are carried across from HR, which seems to be hiding a multitude of sins in the texture art and engine. Keycard models are assymetric, but they've used the same texture for both sides of the model (leaving a black triangle visible on the reverse). Walls tend to look poor up close. The stalls in Golem City were rushed. The red dot laser sight isn't ray traced - it's just a red sprite in the middle of the screen. Attention to detail is just poor throughout, which means that these gorgeous environments don't hold up to scrutiny.
This, added to the very obvious attempts to wean more money from a AAA-priced title (paid companion mobile app which adds Praxis and the option to directly pay to unlock more Praxis) leave a really bad taste in the mouth.
TL;DR - fun gameplay, disappointing plot, ultimately unsatisfying. If you enjoyed HR you'll probably enjoy this almost as much. If you loved the story of the original Deus Ex you'll be very disappointed.

I got this game as part of the Yogscast Jingle Jam 2017 Humble Bundle (bit of a mouth full) so can’t really tell you what I paid for it individually, I can tell you I probably wouldn’t hand over the usual £4.79 asking price. Having said that, I spent 3 hours playing Dreaming Sarah, completed 22/22 Steam achievements and I did enjoy it for the most part. Also, 100% of bundle proceeds go to charity (over $3.5m in the first week!), and how can that ever be a bad thing?!
The game is a 2D puzzle platformer with some lovely pixel art, The colours and style give the game a trippy vibe and the subject matter and environments get increasingly psychedelic. I encountered everything from a dimension full of eyes to a pink moon that appeared to have been claimed by Brazil. It can feel a bit surreal, which I have no issue with, but unfortunately, it spills into the gameplay itself. There is a lot of backtracking for items, going to and fro between areas and no real logic being applied to the solutions. This just leaves obscure answers with no real clues or reasoning to help you reach them. For example, while exploring a mouth (yep!) I encountered a bloody globule-like creature (maybe an ulcer?) blocking my path; I removed said creature by killing it with some sour orange juice  . . .
My first impressions of the music were that it sounded like a kinda of funked-up, trip-hop relaxation music that you might hear whilst having your chakras dry cleaned or you safe place Feng shuied! However, it wasn’t distracting or annoying and it fitted well with the retro art style and the themes of the game.
Dreaming Sarah was a nice enough experience, short and sweet, but it really didn’t offer anything new. The puzzles we’re a bit too random for my liking and the story is mediocre to non-existent with a pretty weak and overdone ending. You will not be surprised by any cryptic plot twists playing this game! If you got it as part of the same bundle then go for it, you’ll probably enjoy it, but personally, I wouldn’t recommend buying it at full price.

Soulstorm is the latest and most-played expansion pack to Dawn of War. It offers the most balance, though it's still one of the less balanced RTS games, and it has the most races.
The Warhammer 40K really comes to live in this game, with memorable quotes from units and mouth-watering visuals as lasers and rockets fly. Units have special kill animations during battles in melee, making them visually impressive whether you're zoomed out or zoomed in. Each of the many factions plays very differently, from the Orks and their unit-swarming powers to the Necrons and their utterly free, but slow, units.
There's a replayable campaign in Soulstorm, similar to the one offered in Dark Crusade, but most players will find their playtime in skirmishes and online. I would like to say that I agree with the people who say that this is a step up from the last game, unfortunately I cannot. I wanted to give the WRC titles another shot as I always enjoyed them in the past but I don't feel that right now I can recommend this game. The graphics are still very poor compared to other titles.  I have to admit, even on my system running a GTX 1070 with everything cranked up, it still looked like an old xbox 360 title.  The screenshots posted on the store actually look nothing like the game.  I hate to say it, but it feels like false advertising.
I always liked the fact that you start off in the junior leagues in the WRC titles and work your way up but the actual driving physics which should be the most important aspect feels so off.  Yes the cars feel weightier but you cannot justify the snap oversteer/understeer that you feel.
Comparing this to Dirt Rally is unfair. Codemasters have been doing this for years and honed it.  Dirt Rally is as close to a simulated rally experience you can get here on Steam, this isn't a simulation at all even though it has a sim handling option.  Treating it as a stand alone racer, I don't find the experience rewarding and although it is better than WRC 5, it still has a long way to go before it is as enjoyable as the original titles.
I feel that what is needed is a new focus.  Rather than churning out a new itineration every year, take the time to actually get the car physics right.  I admire the fact that you have 1:1 scale stages but what is the point if you feel like every turn is laboured.  Do what Slightly Mad and Codemasters done and get this into Early Access and let us racers actually make this the game that we all hoped it would be. I was seriously hoping for better and I hope that things get sorted out otherwise I can just see the WRC titles just not existing and us all just going back to Dirt Rally.

I was looking for some early review performance-wise like but since I was unable to find any, I decided to buy the game and try it on my own. Wasn't guite sure how it's going to perform on my Lenovo Y50 with i7-4710, GTX 860, SSD & Win10, so here it is.
What seems to be a huge improvement over the last year's WRC 5, here you have the list options available from the in-game menu which is useful if you need to tweak the game while in playing. I tried few options already mosty in tutorial races and so far I can only say that I can run the game in high settings on 1600/900 resolution at 60 FPS most of the time with random drops to 55-58. Barely noticeable comparing to WRC 5 lagging when my laptop by some reasons couldn't maintain the stable frame rate. I don't mind running in lower resolutions so as you can guess now by doing so I don't spot any FPS drops. There is also much more options to be tweaked comparing to WRC5. However I do miss a proper AA mode, FXAA seems to be a bit off to my liking. Overall I must say after less then 60 minutes within the game, the optimization seems to be more friendly than WRC5 or SLR. What may also matters to some of you, I find the performance better than DR, but that might be due to a higher game requirements for Codemasters game overall.
I wasn't really playing for long but driving with XBOX360 controller seems to be well optimized as well, it's easy enough to drive even on pro settings without giving you that terrible impression the previous game had. Voice acting is done nicely, the copilot doesn't really scream as he used to have in last's game. Sounds of the engine are, well, far from what DR has to offer, but it's definitely an improvement. I might say a bit more if I play a bit more.
So if you hesitate if you want to buy it and you're bored already with DR, try it.
EDITED:
So after few more hours in the game I have to say I gave up 900p for 720p in order to keep my stable frame rate at 60 FPS (still same Lenovo Y50). I have a feeling that vegetation density is the bottleneck for me at this game. Actually I do play on both settings & post process effects set on high with vegetation set as medium. I hope there will be a patch coming soon to improve the performance, but hey, the game is only/already few days old so it should be/should have been fixed somehow.
Speaking about the graphics, I must say the interior camera (the one I always use on rally games) sucks badly on night stages, I mean it's simply really ugly. I think I switch to far side view for this game. In all fairness, I'd love to drive some other cars like classics, but I know it's the official WRC game so I won't keep my hopes too high. Anyway, game is still recommended, however I do wait for performance patch. Please.

The good:
Car handling is very easy to adapt to and behaves differently on each surface. (I am using an Xbox 360 controller)
There is a sense of speed and some sense of weight distribution.
The engine sounds have improved.
The game performs very well at a constant 60fps on the highest graphics setting. (RX 480 Sapphire Nitro 8gb)
There are many stages and countries to visit.
The bad:
Driving over gravel always makes me think the exhaust is dragging on the ground because of the terrible noise it makes.
Graphics are not so great, but are decent for what the game is. I think most of us who are interested in this game will probably worry more about the driving aspect than looking at pretty scenery.
Nothing looks natural. Not in a graphical sense, but I get the feeling everybody I see in the game is some sort of an early build android robot.
The ugly:
The pace notes are just awful. After you get past the robotic and comical way they are said and yelled to you while you are driving, you will also learn fairly early into the game that a 3 turn could actually be a 5 or 1. I have taken 3's in 6th gear and other times had to drop to 2nd, pull the e-brake and power out of the outside of the turn to save myself. Just be cautious when he says 3, he's probably lying. Also since pace notes are such an important part of rally, I think the creators should have put more time into making them at least bearable to listen to.
Overall this is a good game and very fun to play. I'm going to be playing this one a lot. This is definitely a good addition for rally game fans and those looking for a more official and professional rally experience.

The game's atmosphere is EVERYTHING. The 80s Sci-Fi twist on Far Cry 3 is what stole my heart and despite a short game time it has some of the most interesting and captivating gameplay I've experienced in modern gaming.

Remember when you watched Commando for the first time? John Matrix had just gotten to the enemy outpost and was right about to raise hell and rescue his daughter. He suits up, prepares a small arsenal, then goes out to wage war. You remember quite vividly the bits where he shoots the knife at that guy's throat, where he blows up half the island with a single claymore mine, where he kills a squad of baddies with a pitchfork and a rotary saw blade, where he mows down a small army with a machinegun that seems like it never runs out of ammo. Soon it all comes down to the final confrontation between Matrix and that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with the stupid moustache and the chainmail vest. One knife fight and witty quip later, and the bad guy is dead, his daughter is saved, and order and freedom are restored to the world while Power Station blares in the background. All the while, you're thinking "What if I could be John Matrix? What if I could save the world, kill the bad guy, get the girl, and look like a badass while doing it? Wouldn't that be awesome?"
If this is you, then Far Cry 3: Blood Dragon was made for you.
For everyone else? Eh, it's still pretty good. Even if Blood Dragon's 80's Action Movie VHS feel doesn't resonate with you, the game is still plenty enjoyable. In a single sentence, it can best be described as Far Cry 3 with superpowers. Your guns are ludicrously powerful, you can jump a full twenty feet into the air without so much as breaking stride, you can sprint faster than most cars, and you have enough health to keep standing after a robot throws a dragon into your chest at mach 6. The basics of the gameplay are still the same. You clear out outposts, hunt animals, do side missions, and complete story missions. If you've played Far Cry 3, then you've played Blood Dragon, but you haven't really experienced it, and that's the real difference here.
The retro-vibe is captured damn near perfectly. Blood Dragon is essentially Action Movie: The Video Game. Michael Biehn of Aliens and Terminator fame nails down Rex Power Colt brilliantly, and the soundtrack by Powerglove is one of the best I've heard in a videogame since Hotline: Miami. At its low price, it's certainly a title worth picking up. If you liked Far Cry 3, you will either like or love this game.

Trine 2 is well reviewed at this point, so there's not much need for me to go into detail like my other reviews.
My first thought about Trine 2 is "WHY CAN'T MORE GAMES BE THIS PRETTY?!" Even though technically it doesn't have the highest quality art assets in terms of poly count, textures, and graphical tech, T2 more than makes up for it with it's art style, variety of detail and color, and a mostly organic feel that doesn't look too "gamey" (I.e tiled backgrounds, symmetry, etc). Nearly every frame of gameplay in T2 is screenshot worthy, and the developers probably had hard time choosing screenshots for store fonts.
You have physics based gameplay that is less like a 2D Mario or Sonic, and more like a LittleBigPlanet or NightSky. I'm not very fond of physics platformers versus solid, gamey platformers honestly, but much of the platforming is pretty forgiving when it comes to making jumps and the placement of checkpoints. There were some slightly frustrating puzzles or segments in the end game, but games are supposed to be harder by that point and the game is supposed to make you think more or react more quickly. There were a couple moments where I had to consult a guide to know what to do. I bought this game because I knew i enjoyed the first game demo on PS3..
I was able to complete it in roughtly 9-10hrs. After playing it completely, this is something that would be better with friends. You can definitely play this online with randoms, but it never felt like random players communicated well, and sometimes you have to deal with drama, as I had one player call another player a ♥♥♥♥♥ or something along those lines for no reason, while typing nonsense in another language. There have been a good handful of moments where I wish I had somebody to help me grab an experience orb (which gives you XP for Skill points that lets you buy abilitiies for your characters), but after playing online with random players, I decided to just play by myself, since any of my friends have already played this game.
The core mechanics are a mix between Character switching platformers like The Lost Vikings, The Cave, Ed, Edd, And Eddy, and Thomas Was Alone and physics platforming from LittlleBigPlanet. Solve various physics based puzzles and platform segements between the varied skills of your characters. It feels good to solve a few puzzles, though, the combat is very simplistic and button mashing at the most exciting segements - many of the boss battles are exactly the same except for the final boss.
Trine is a beautiful and fairly nice game. It's a pretty good platformer on its own, though, you can probably miss out on this unless you are able to orchestrate a game between friends or competent and communicative friends. This game is often on sale and is well reviewed by most critics and players.

Operation Flashpoint: Red River is kind of like a mixture of ArmA, MOH and Ghost Recon. You command your fireteam (like GR) except in a more complicated way similar to ArmA (stance, dispersion, noise dicipline etc.) There are ArmA features like bullet drop, the importance of stance when aiming, military jargon that is relevant to the task and some adherence to military tactics. The AI (unlike ArmA) are actually somewhat lifelike, and they behave much like the AI in say MOH BF3/4 and GR. Unfortunately, the environment isn't breakable (like BF3/4), however you can reduce buildings to rubble with high explosives but that is it. Suppressors aren't that useful because of the way the campaign is played (open ground and daylight) but fortunately they do not reduce damage like in some games. The weapons are rather innacurate, almost to the point that they are unusable. The M4A1 carbine is good for distances up to max 20m away (the ACOG magnifies too much). The M249E2 SAW is about the same. The MP5A4 is good for targets up to 10m away. The M14 is best with the Leupold Mk 4 because the ACOG sits too far forward on the weapon and the peripherals interfere. The M107 is useful for any range, but if targets are within 100m, then aim using the graduations above the middle of the crosshair.
In conclusion, I would recommend it to anyone. It's fun by yourself (the AI are competent) and fun with friends or even strangers (the online community are quite pleasant).

Following the developer’s description, Brawlhalla is a 2D platform fighter: if you know and loved super smash bros, then you’ll probably like this game. The game currently is in EA, but actually is one of the pretty much complete ones with lots of content; during playing I also didn’t encounter any grave bugs or crashes.
In a bunch of different platform-arenas, of which I really like the artstyle, you try to kick your opponents of said platforms to score; falling off or getting kicked off reduces your score. To do all that the game offers a nice amount of 23 heroes, 6 of them always in free rotation. To get a hero permanently you either have to buy them for the ingame gold coins you earn through fighting, as login reward or through missions OR of course by spending real money, about 4,5€ per character -  alternatively you can get all heroes in a bundle for 20€.
The heroes vary in their stats (attack strength, attack speed, defence, movement speed) and which arms they use: some use a pistol/sword combination, others for example spear and rocket-lance; all of them vary in speed, reach and attack moves.
Those weapons randomly drop during the match, but you can of course also fight with bare fists. There’re also some extra “toys” like grenades or spike balls you can throw at your opponent, useful to prevent them from landing on the platform again after you kicked them off.
In general, it’s not hard to get into the game, but there’re a lot of twists and combos to be learned to get good at it. The lack of a tutorial makes the start unnecessarily hard though. At least it has a training mode where you can check out ALL heroes as well as taking a look at ALL skins, quite nice. In addition, you can fight singleplayer matches versus bots in 3 different difficulty settings.
Some training is certainly advised, especially when you want to play ranked matches. Cause even when the general mechanics are easy to get, it’s really a “hard to master”-game where you not only use light and heavy attacks but also slides, mid-air combos, jump attacks and more to get rid of your opponent. It’s worth keeping an eye on the opponent’s health bar as well as hit-boxes and weapon reach.
In addition to the mentioned standard game mode, there’re a couple of, well, party-modes like a snowball fight or one called Brawlball, where you need to get a ball into the opponent’s goal.
Due to its F2P nature, the game of course also offers a couple of customization options: skins for your character as well as his or her weapons plus taunts. Following the developer’s description, Brawlhalla is a 2D platform fighter: if you know and loved super smash bros, then you’ll probably like this game. The game currently is in EA, but actually is one of the pretty much complete ones with lots of content; during playing I also didn’t encounter any grave bugs or crashes.
In a bunch of different platform-arenas, of which I really like the artstyle, you try to kick your opponents of said platforms to score; falling off or getting kicked off reduces your score. To do all that the game offers a nice amount of 23 heroes, 6 of them always in free rotation. To get a hero permanently you either have to buy them for the ingame gold coins you earn through fighting, as login reward or through missions OR of course by spending real money, about 4,5€ per character -  alternatively you can get all heroes in a bundle for 20€.
The heroes vary in their stats (attack strength, attack speed, defence, movement speed) and which arms they use: some use a pistol/sword combination, others for example spear and rocket-lance; all of them vary in speed, reach and attack moves.
Those weapons randomly drop during the match, but you can of course also fight with bare fists. There’re also some extra “toys” like grenades or spike balls you can throw at your opponent, useful to prevent them from landing on the platform again after you kicked them off.
In general, it’s not hard to get into the game, but there’re a lot of twists and combos to be learned to get good at it. The lack of a tutorial makes the start unnecessarily hard though. At least it has a training mode where you can check out ALL heroes as well as taking a look at ALL skins, quite nice. In addition, you can fight singleplayer matches versus bots in 3 different difficulty settings.
Some training is certainly advised, especially when you want to play ranked matches. Cause even when the general mechanics are easy to get, it’s really a “hard to master”-game where you not only use light and heavy attacks but also slides, mid-air combos, jump attacks and more to get rid of your opponent. It’s worth keeping an eye on the opponent’s health bar as well as hit-boxes and weapon reach.
In addition to the mentioned standard game mode, there’re a couple of, well, party-modes like a snowball fight or one called Brawlball, where you need to get a ball into the opponent’s goal.
Due to its F2P nature, the game of course also offers a couple of customization options: skins for your character as well as his or her weapons plus taunts. Most of them look really cool and funny, so if you always wanted to fight with a guitar-axe this is your chance. The prices vary from around 2 up to 8€ per item.
I readily admit that even after a few hours I’m still far away from considering myself good at this game, which is mainly due to my lack of skill in these kind of games though ;)
I’ll therefore stay away from giving any strategy tips or explaining more about the fighting technics – there’re however a lot of useful guides and video tutorials by players which can be found in the community hub. I’m having fun with Brawlhalla anyway though and definitely recommend checking it out  it’s F2P after all.

WRC6 is a huge improvement over the previous game in the series. They really paid attention to every last detail which makes rallying a joy and delivered a great fun and challenging rally game. If you're a complete casual or more of a hardcore fan, there should be something for everyone in here.
So I've been playing this quite a lot just in the couple days after launch, and I must say I am very impressed. It's interesting what a year of work can bring if you work on the right bits and pieces. People should note tho that this is not suppose to be Dirt Rally 2 or something, mainly because it's based at a much wider audience than DR is. But just because of that, it doesn't mean it's a bad game either. In fact, it's a blast! Things that should be noted are:
PROS:
- Very detailed and well made/updated tracks - There's 14 different rallies, including China, so there's plenty of environments to race through. A big variety of destinations (something DR actually lacks...) with great attention to detail.
- Fun for everyone - Considering it's a licensed game, it has to be made so it can suit as many people as possible. And I must say, great job on achieving that, because with assists, even the most casual rally fans can have a go without major issues, while cracking it up to simulation mode, brings a challenge even to the more hardcore audience. Even after playing around 200 hours on DR at the time, I must admit I find this game more enjoyable, it's the perfect ballance of fun and challenge.
- Graphics/sounds/physics - a bunch of well improved elements which make the game that more enjoyable.
- Splitscreen - Not for everybody but I personally really appreciate this feature. Thank you! :D
CONS:
- Co-driver - Although he does get the job done, there are times he cannot manage to deliver the pacenotes in time. It often happens, at least in my case, that I overtake him and he can't keep up. So there's something that'll need a bit more work.
- Replay cameras - The onboard cameras that are used most of the time aren't really anything special...would be nice to see trackside cameras through most of the stages.
- Track variety - Now bare with me on this...I know I mentioned tracks under pros as well, but there's a few things that should be noted, if not else maybe for next years game I suppose. Track selection is great, BUT there are only a few per rally. About 3-4 plus a "Super Special Stage" if the rally even has one. Not to mention some tracks are more or less the same layout than in the previous game, maybe extended a kilometer or so. So quick suggestions to devs, do what codemasters do, make the tracks available in reverse as well. BOOM, instant double rally lenght. Maybe could be considered for next year.
Overall, WRC 6 is a great "simcade" like racing game. If you're a rally fan and are looking for a game which delivers both fun and a good challenge, this game should be one to consider. I'm giving it a solid 9/10 considering they only had a year to develop it all as well. Good job Kylotonn, looking forward to future titles already!

For some reason it's hard to find a game that releases in a good state for the PC, The dev's have managed to pull it off with this,  With WRC 4 still having an audio bug even today and WRC 5 having the stutters which is the last thing a racing game needs I was a bit worried that I'd be wasting my money buying this straight away but we're in luck.. It's running really well, The visuals are nice, The handling too so I've no complaints. Great game

I will warn you ahead of time that this game frustrated me. I'm simply reviewing my experience and stating that I would not recommend it. I say very little about the game in and of itself.
First off, there's two levels of DRM. Steam AND Uplay. When you can't find the play button in the second level of DRM you're being forced to use you have to really want to give the game a chance to find out how to start it. Perhaps I'm quick to judge the game itself since I'm not a fan of Far Cry 3, but "toggle crouch" removes the fluidity I love from shooters, not to mention the F.E.A.R. difficulty AI (on normal) that never misses even through solid objects.
I'm frankly not interested in progressing past this mission where you have to defend against enemies that rush for the objective, don't miss, and none of your weapons are suited to dealing with the threat. The trailers had me convinced this was a run-and-gun but what I got was a "duck behind cover and play Splinter Cell" experience.
Graphics were fine, mind you. Nice visuals; however, I can't say I felt like a badass as conveyed in the trailer because... well, I didn't.
In the end, though, I wouldn't recommend this to any friends on an admittedly shallow and simple premise:
Dry humor with frustrating controls and forced use of Uplay DRM? No thanks.

One of the greatest open world games ever created. I mean look, for better or worse this is still a good game. It's still a *really* good game.
Does it feel way too short for a $60 game? You bet. That's why I bought it for $30.
Does its limiting you to maybe 5 areas make the game feel cramped and stifled? Hell yeah it does.
Does the story end only half-resolved, leaving you in a situation where you're either going to have to wait for DLC to wrap it up (Spoilers: System Rift is not that DLC), or worse, wait 4 years for another game to wrap it up? Absolutely.
Is the PC port absolutely awful, causing unforgivable load times? YEAH, IT KINDA IS.
Are all those things bad? Yes. Yes they are.
But that doesn't really change the core of the game. I might be more forgiving because I paid half price, but almost ALL of the issues i had with Human Revolution were fixed in this game. (Most of) the environments were detailed as hell, they were sprawling, and I didn't feel cramped in them. The side quests were more open-ended. I actually played the whole game without a single boss fight! Not one! I talked my way out of all of them! I (almost) went the entire game without killing a single person. The characters inside TF29, Jensen's employer, are all annoyingly flat and poorly written, but the game's side characters are where its writing shines. The cult side mission alone sold me on this game not but an hour or two into playing.
There are a lot of flaws with this game; a lot of flaws that, were this any other game, were the game, at its core, any worse (in any way), would be fatal. But as it is there's JUST enough about this game that's enjoyable make its flaws something you can kinda gloss over. More importantly, however, the flaws all lie with choices Square Enix made, not choices Eidos made when making the game. The issue isn't "the writing is bad", it's "the story gets cut short because the publisher wanted to milk you for money". The issue isn't "the game itself is broken" it's "Square is greedy"
IMO, wait for the game to go down in price or just buy a key for half price. Not paying full admission makes the game a lot easier to swallow.

I decided to point out the best and worst elements in this game in a quick summary:
The good:
- This game could be really fun for a 4 Player Co-op. But I never tried that.
- Bullet drops are accurate and satisfying.
- Visuals still hold up okay, specially in later levels (I might be easy to please in this case). The mountains are neat.
- Good length for the Single Player considering recent games in the genre.
- The Briefing before any mission is nice. Really loved the soundtrack giving you a "danger" feel before going to battle.
- Level of customization for different sets of classes. You can level them up and get new perks.
- You can give orders to each soldier in your squad. It's great to flank enemy positions, suppress and ambush if you take the time to understand how it works.
- No health regeneration. If you get shot you need to stop the bleeding first then patch up
- You can get killed with one or two bullets.
The Bad:
- The AI is a hit or miss. Either they can be effective or they warn you to not shot because they are going to be in front of you. This happened more than it should.
- It requires Games for Windows Live if that' is an issue/deal breaker for you.
- Because the Story is focused on one area, there's not much variety when it comes to different war scenarios.
- Checkpoint can be cruel at times considering how easy it is to be killed. Most of them are fine, however.
- Responsiveness from your AI when you order them to enter a vehicle can be really slow.
Best Knox quote:
"I'm going to beat you so hard that not even Google will be able to find you."

First thing you have to know, this game looks like it has been Inspired by the Lost Vikings series made by blizzard so this is one good reason to not skip it.
A very good and challenging game, but not enough difficulty curves to select.
(Normal mode) You either never die since you can return in your last checkpoint's spot to heal your dead partners
-OR-
(hardest) You die and you must restart the whole stage coz you can't get far without the archer and the mage. This mean the first time, you must advance to take all the bubble. Second time, you must focus on not getting killed and killing the boss that you don't know yet how to kill; not to mention that each stages are very long, but i still embrace this challenge, i just don't rush the game as a result. On that difficulty setting, i suggest to not even focus on picking up bubbles once you have enough to unlock (Ice Arrows) And (Ice shield). You won't get burned-out that way.
Gameplay:
great combat system, great physics that you can exploit very well with tools sush as the batman's hook and summoning magical boxes along with your surrounding and everything you must do to exploit them. The movement and everything couldnt have been better.
Puzzle: It's a puzzle game as well and a pretty hard one. Not anyone, even at hard mode can figure what to do in the longrun.  Each puzzles are fun to do; it's not one of those puzzle games where you want to rush to the next thing just to get over it.
AI:
I only play hardest mode so my opinion is based on that difficulty only.
The enemies are very hard, no delays between their attacks, they move pretty fast, they can climb on almost anything so they will follow you platforms after platforms and 1 of your hero gets killed in 3 hits. With this game, you will be scared of goblins for the first time and they're not even small; they're as tall as your heroes. 1 Goblin is hard enough to beat you down 1on1, but you will still get outnumbered and trust me, you will rage quit.
Story:
First stuff, good voice actors and the storyline while you shoudln't take it too seriously, it's still good enough for the ride.
10/10: Good and accessible for everyone. You can even play it with 3 friends local or online.

It is the second year now for Kylotonn Racing Games and Bigben Interactive.  There has been definite improvement since last years WRC 5.  Is it on the same simulation level as Dirt Rally no however this being the official WRC game they are aiming to be more accessible.  They have a multitude of difficulty settings which allow you to go from the arcade to simulation which is fairly close to the level of Dirt Rally which I am impressed by.
The engine sounds have gotten better and the pace notes are back to what most people know with a 1-6 which is nice.  Handling feels good if at times a bit loose but I have only played the Junior WRC in career where setup changes are not allowed.  The stages also feel more like the real world counterparts this year which is also a huge plus.
Downside would be the damage model feels too forgiving but then almost all games are like this.  For example in the video I run into a fence and have next to no damage from the impact.
Overall I would recommend this even if you have WRC 5 as they have done a good improvement over last year unlike most yearly releases as long as you know it is a more simcade than simulation.

WRC 6 reminds me a lot of the old WRC games under EvoStudios back on the PS1 & 2, otherwise known as the glory days of WRC gaming.
Let's just get one thing out the way first though... one cannot logically compare this game to DiRT Rally; I love DR, but WRC 6 is a licensed game, therefore must appeal to a wider audience. DR is a passion project, and Codies had more creative freedom with restrictions largely limited to vehicle licensing. Expect a ceiling.
Anyway, it's clear to see that WRC 5 was largely just a stepping stone on to better things. They didn't have long to make that game either, and the result was evident. However, WRC 6 has improved in all areas, from visuals and sound, all the way down to quality of content.
Stages are narrower with unforgiving elements (mostly between 6-8km long, with some a little shorter or a little longer), pacenotes are less robotic (yet still c&p) and more accurate, car models are better, and most importantly the cars themselves feel like they have more weight and contact with the road surface, and generally the feel and appearance of car physics are much more polished.
Damage model has been developed to be more realistic, which means it's more progressive and dynamic depending on where you hit the car. You can also suffer from punctures during the stage, in which case you will need to stop and change the wheel.
Cockpit cam is a little more zoomed out, and you can now freely look around the car, and take a peek at the drivers body if you wish.
Still on cameras, the chase cam has also been improved, if that's your thing. It's very much like the early 2000's WRC games; more fluid following, compared to how stiff and horrid is has been in recent years.
Performance wise, it runs perfectly. I'm getting 60fps solid with most of the settings on the highest quality. Alongside performance WRC 6 is also a nice looking game, and far better than the titles in recent years. It looks a lot more natural by way of colouring and post fx, and car and stage textures are very good.
This is the first time I've been this happy playing the first few hours of a WRC game in a long, long time. I'm just glad I can finally say that again.

Summary:
WRC 6 is an improvement on WRC 5. It's not Dirt Rally, but it's a decent simcade rally game.
Rating:
7/10
System Specs:
Windows 10 Anniversary Update
i7-6700HQ @ 2.60
16GB Ram
Samsung 850 Pro SSD
GTX 1060
Controller:
XBOX One S BT
Pros:
- Handling:
Handling is good on an XBONE controller. No visible controller lag, responsive to minor adjustments, works well.
- Stage length:
Stages are surprisingly long and complicated.
- Damage modeling:
You can break just about everything and it has a physical affect on the car.
- Licensed:
All the licensed rallies, teams, and cars.
- Performance:
At Very High settings / 1080p / Vsync A, I'm getting a solid 60FPS with no drops and no stuttering.
Cons:
- Graphics:
While they are an improvement over last year's graphics, there's still visible shimmering and the visual fidelity isn't up to par with say AC, F1 2016, Dirt Rally or Forza Horizon 3.
- Sound:
The sound is mediocre. There's a distinction between the gear whine, engine sound and popoff, but the engines sound pretty weak and there's no real aural difference between cars.
- Co-driver:
The robotic co-drivers are dated at best. They serve a function, but the Dirt games have done co-drivers better and smoother.
- Measurements:
(This is the American in me speaking, so metric-using friends, I apologize). There's no way that I've determined to switch from Metric to Imperial measurements (m to ft, kmph to mph, etc).
Overall, this is not a bad game, and with the 20% promotional discount is a decent price. It's a marked improvement over WRC 5, and while it's not on par with Dirt Rally, it's very good in its own right. It's a mix of sim and arcade that is approachable and works well as a licensed game. It's also very important to point out Kylotonn is NOT Milestone, and they've done a good job of fixing the problems from last year while introducing some decent improvements.

Trine 2 is a side scroller puzzle game with the use of 3 main characters who have different characteristics and attributes e.g weight and weapons etc. These difference between the characters broadens the play style which is given to the players as players can decide on the best method to complete each level. Moreover, the game also features a 3 player co-op mode where a group of players take on the journey together with either 1 character each (to harden the game) or all 3 characters for all (easier play).
Trine 2 succeeds is bringing challenging puzzles where players need to think co operatively in order to proceed through the game. This is done through the different mechanics implemented into the game as the game progesses with newer/stronger enemies alongside the increasing harzardous environment. However, many puzzles could simply be completed without much effort when playing co-op through the use of more than 1 mage in the game. (levitating each other through puzzles instead of completing them properly).
The graphics is perfect for the type of game as the game is set in a beautiful fantasy world with vibrant and colourful environments filled with many amusing things to observe in the background. I have to say that this would be one of the greatest things Trine 2 has manage to cover as I have spent alot of time just looking at the beautiful world which has been created in this game while anticipating the next themes of the levels.
The multiplayer is very enjoyable when played with friends due to the messed up ways and trickery we have found while completing the game. Adventuring together is also great fun as the need to work with each other may create great memorable or funny momments (especially when trolling each other lols). Exploring together and finding secret locations is also an experience which I have found throughout the game.
All in all, I have to definately recommend this game to those who love puzzle games as well as those who love co-op games. Trine 2 is alot more fun when playing co-op with a friend rather than solo as players can mess around and have fun togther while completing levels instead of playing alone and trying to figure everything out alone with less strategic plays (plus some of the levels are pretty hard to complete when playing 1 character at a time in solo).

I came into this game thinking it might be a little to hack n slash, a little too "been there, done that."  However, I was pleasantly surprised to find that it is different and intriguing in a few different ways.
First, I figured you chose between a typical warrior, rogue, or wizard as your class, and that you were saddled with that class the whole game.  But you play all three classes at once, switching back and forth between them seamlessly with just a button press.  Each class has their own skills and weapons, so It opens up a variety of ways to accomplish tasks, solve puzzles, and kill enemies.  There is no "one" solution to a situation.
Second, this game is GORGEOUS.  I have never seen a 2D game that looks like this, and quite frankly, the magical quality of the world puts even many well-textured but plain 3D worlds to shame.  The backgrounds are so alive, colorful, and detailed, it is as close to 3D as 2D will get.  If your rig can run it with AA and all options maxed, prepare for a treat (medium rig should do it, even my macbook air runs it great with just AA turned off).
The storyline so far does not seem prevalent, but that is not the point of these games for many people, anyway.  The one negative for me comes in slightly clunky combat; controls don't feel perfect, and hit detection seems a bit odd, especially with the warrior and his blocking.  It may just take a little getting used to though, I haven't played much yet.
Overall, I highly recommend this to anyone who likes side scrollers and to those who put a lot of stock in visuals, because these are something else.  It is a prettier, more fun, and more open version of Limbo, a fantastic game.

Coming off it's success of Trine, Trine has lost none of it's glamour, and in the process has added only everything wonderful. I really enjoyed the first trine. It's story, music, gameplay, all of it was generally delightful, allbeit short. Trine 2 follows wonderfully in it's footsteps.
Here we find our three heroes not really looking for adventure per say, but the Trine once again find it for them. This time they are taken off to save a world of enchantment and a battle between sisters. In the process they find themselves fighting goblins. There is no reason to argue with story line here, as the story is short, succinct, not complicated, and enjoyable for the game.
In terms of gameplay, Trine 2 builds on it's predecessor, working out many of the physics kinks that were so lauded. The characters do basically the same thing, with the addition of a few extras - the knights glide, and magnet shield, the thiefs special gravity arrow, and ability to hide herself, and the wizards magnetic objects, and ability to trap enemies inside boxes, as well as ability to pick up enemies. All in all, the gameplay of this game is smooth and for the most part without problems. 9.5/10
In terms of graphics, Trine 2 looks superb. The artists who worked the concepts of this game have done a phenomenal job yet again. The colours, the look, and the increased depth make this side-scroller look even better. The graphics themselves could be a little nicer, sharper, and slightly more realistic in some areas - the characters for instance - but all in all this game is more than pleasing on the eyes. 9/10
Music in this game is one thing that I really enjoy. The embience coupled with the wonderful sound track is above par. Music is a lost art when it comes to video games sometimes, but Trine 2, like it's predecessor, does an excellent job of creating wonderful atmosphere and putting the right music at the right time. And just add in here, the narration of Trine 2 is just as fun as the first. 9.5/10 (BTW, I'm a music teacher)
Co-op is such a hard thing to get right. It's hard to know when it's too much, or when it's not enough. It's a good thing that co-op over the internet was added to this game. It makes it so much more fun to play that way. The only drawaback to this games co-op is the same as last times, the controller configuration. More often then I would like to admit, the control configurations seem to be out of wack. Responding to the wrong thing, or not working at all. Multiple keyboards is still an impossible task sometimes. The co-op itself is fun to play with friends, but if the work on controller configuration were fixed the co-op would be even more fun. 8.5/10
Overall, this game is wonderful. It can be short, or long, depending on what you plan to do with it. It can be easy, or you can challenge yourself, as I have, to find new ways to beat certain areas. If you find it too easy, put it in hardcore mode, on hard, then give it a whirl. Enjoy the colours, the embience, and try and find a friend to play this game with you. You won't win any major tournaments while shooting dozens of people, but you will find yourself enjoying the fact that you've made it through a game using your brain.

Mankind Divided is a huge improvement from Human Revolution, allowing a far wider range of actions, having more secrets to uncover and providing possibly the most entertaining offering of sidequests a game has offered me so far. The game's visuals are well designed and thoroughly polished, although many of the animations suffer from odd twitches and stiffness.
The voice acting is confidently delivered, the world sounds just about right and even the music has a lovely way of evoking the original Deus Ex I so love. However, there are some fairly annoying audio balance issues, which can render dialogue too quiet, a background noise too loud or, in some cases, a bit of a bug can leave entire cutscenes entirely mute.
Bugs are the main issue for me, anyway. The game seems to stumble on it's own genius, in that by allowing the player so many ways to approach certain situations, the developers have created such a web of triggers and variables that they simply could not test everything properly. I had to reload a save on a couple of occasions due to the game simply not triggering the cutscene required for me to proceed in the game, the final area of the game suffering of this the most, causing me to end the game on a low note, rather than a high one.
Another issue this game has is the fact that it is clearly the middle part of a trilogy (because everything has to be a trilogy). The game picks up from the previous story, piles on a huge number of new characters, plotlines and elements and then finishes with the vast majority of those left unsolved, to be picked up in the sequel. However, since I enjoyed Human Revolution and enjoyed most of Mankind Divided, I have to recommend it just for the fact that it is a solid piece of entertainment and a fine attempt to pave the way for what I hope will be a grand finale in the next game.
Man, I hope they have the grace to give that game an actual, proper ending, though...

Dreaming Sarah is a pixel 2D plataform game that cames with a generic story but with it own special things that keep the player until the end, even the player already knowing what's going to be revealed.
The game follow Sarah in an amazing, cute  and creepy journey to find what happened to her, when actually Sarah is exploring a place that can change all of the humans future decisions on their lifes. At first we wake in a forest and without information of her past we start the game. As the game goes we start to see creepy things, dead bodies, weird plants and creatures. There is around 12 scenarios to explore, all with it own characteristcs and mistery.
The game looks an old game from SNES and the sound effects give this feeling to the player. The soundtrack it's good, isn't marvelous and totally amazing that will grab into your head forever, it's good. It can be really good during the gameplay, but you'll never feel that music can transmit other feeling than a good music that fits in the scenario. My favorite  music is the underwater music, that's really good to listen.
The scenarios are, for me, beautiful, it can be somehow generic as others scenarios, but how music fits into it can tell a lot about that place you're walking by. With a lot of details, but same sprites, the scenario is what can keep the player on the game, going to a innocent forest to another dimension inside a TV.
The game controls, for me, are old. Using the Up, Down, Right, Left keys instead the W, A, S, D keys that nowadays are more used, can be a problem. Yes, we can change it on menu (Extra point), but everytime we close the game and continue, the configuration are back to default (lost extra point). Not saying that taking 1 minute to readjust it can kill the game, it's just annoying, but the game can be finished on 1 run of less than 2 hours (not because that, think about asking refund) but sometimes you don't have enough time to play 2 hours straight. Also other thing that annoys is the F12 button (For the ones who don't know it's the default Screenshot key for Steam) this key opens the code window of Construct2 (Engine of the game) so everytime you screenshot, it pops a window of codes on your face, and if you don't close it, the next screenshot is automatically from that window and not the game. Not everybody likes screenshots but some do and that annoys, and can't change it.
The game has 2 endings, but isn't something that can change everything. The final of the game reveals a thing that during the gameplay we can figure out by ourself, thanks to the weird scenario we are, what's going on. The endings are all interpretative, and the comunity has some nice theory. But we all know what the game is about.
Dreaming Sarah is a nice game, but it story can be generic, the diference to this game to others is what the player see and say to himself "that's amazing". Amazing scenario, good music, ending that we all already expect but diferent feeling for each player, Dreaming Sarah it's a good game, and cheap, that worth our time.

Best DLC of 2013 for me, hands down. Nothing can compare to a game like this for someone like me. Growing up I saw a lot of movies from the '80's, especially actions movies. Robocop, Terminator 2, Aliens, Judge Dredd, they all make some level of a cameo in this game. Whether it is a weapon name, a line from a random scientist or even an achievement title. In fact, the way readies the next shell in his shotgun is the same way Arnie did it in Terminator 2. The crazy world design- especially the colour palette, make this world fun to explore. Hunting is still prevalent with all of the animals being cyber versions of themselves, but they aren't much different. The weapons are over the top and ridiculous. The voice acting is covered in cheese and the dialogue is what you'd expect from those kinds of movies. It's a grand ol' time.
In this neon cyber world you play as Rex Power Colt, a Mark IV robot with a bad♥♥♥♥♥Terminator 2 style eye and more lame puns and jokes than you can have teeth in your mouth. After Vietnam 2 Rex Power Colt saw the end of his life but was then reincarnated in mechanical form- as a cyborg designed to be cool and do awesome stuff. He is your stereotypical '80's action movie hero right down to his looks and the way he speaks.
The gameplay is pretty much the same as Far Cry 3, but you're not as weak as Jason Brody. You don't lose half of your health when you fall from 3 feet, in fact, I never found a height in that game that caused me harm. The weapons can start off as your standard-fair variants but soon evolve into weapons of pure joy. Why have an old shotgun when you can give the thing four barrels and make it fire incendiary rounds that explode and burn everything? The leveling system has been overhauled as well. Instead of acquiring EXP like you would in Far Cry 3 you instead get a total amount of EXP that you need to just get to level 30, which is the max. Stealth plays the same so much can't be said about that. The blood dragons offer a nice twist on the game as they are nearly blind and use their hearing to locate prey. They can be distracted with cyber hearts torn from the chests of murdered enemies which you throw like a ball for a dog. Instead of bringing it back, they eat it offering you some time to leave or hit them with a cheap shot. They are large and fire lasers out of their mouths. The only weak point they have is on their chest; however, they are quadruped creatures so you have to make them stand on their hind legs to hit the scar on their chest. They can be either a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥or a massive help if you need it. Depends on how you want to play.
The story isn't really much. Take every old '80's movie stereotype you've ever seen and mash them together. You now have t he story for Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon. It's good to get you from one place to another so you can shoot more stuff but don't take it as anything more than a tongue-in-cheek play on itself.
The world is a bright and vibrant sensory overload of colours that will make you want to vomit rainbows. A neon blue bow, glowing red eyes on cyber sharks, big blue beating hearts you tear out of enemies... to put simply: lots of colours everywhere. Everything just looks cyber and futuristic. It really does fit its own design very well. Rex looks and plays like a cyborg that was once a man who saw combat. It's a great change of pace to see a world flourished like this instead of the standard brown and grey dirt filled areas filled with generic Chinese or Russians soldiers that you find in far too many games.
Too keep this review from running on like my one for Far Cry 3 I will end it shortly.

Far Cry 3 - Blood Dragon is a good enough game. It's a little short; I wasn't expecting the scope of Far Cry 3 (which I encourage you to play before this game) but was hoping for something nearing half of the 35 hours I put into that game. I used a fifth of those hours to 100% this game; but then again, I did max my level out early with exploration and side quests as a priority over doing story missions and I played on easy difficulty.
Having admitted that, there is only one island this time, only a dozen types of wild animals, and only a small fraction of the number of FC3's collectibles. You could probably count the number of story missions on one hand with the final mission being quite long. Maybe there were 7 or 8 so make that two hands.
You pretty much have to get to level 30 before trying the final mission for the best advantage; and also because rounding up collectibles, ticking off achievements and maxing your level (30) is all the post-story game has to keep you interested, and has no real benefit to the last mission's trial (that you can't back out of once started, but the game tells you this).
The same rare visual bugs return from FC3 but they're not annoying or game-breaking like some other games and it's a noticeable but very minor qualm.

A highly enjoyable, casual multiplayer shooter with a fun and lighthearted style that endears itself to me.
The Mean Greens is a 5v5 multiplayer shooter which sees the two teams, the Greens and the Tans, square off in one of many different and surprisingly unique gamemodes. What makes it stand out is the fact that you play as those cheap little plastic toy soldiers that you would see being sold at the dollar store, and the maps take place in all sorts of everyday household locations, ranging from the inside of a freezer to an arts and crafts table even up to a large saltwater fish tank.
The gameplay is simple enough. You've got your standard 2 teams, an objective and the undeniable sense that you should just go over there and shoot their plastic nuts off. There are no classes or character progression systems, each and every player has the same loadout as you do at all times, meaning there are no picks and counter-picks, just an evenly matched lineup in which the best team wins.
Although, there are some cheap-shot handholding weapons like the rocket launcher which in essense is a one-shot one-kill weapon. But it's relatively balanced since there are no ammo pickups on the maps, and once you shoot the rocket launcher it will go on cooldown for a ridiculously long time before you can use it again. In fact it is quicker to just die and respawn to get the rocket launcher back. Many will think the rocket launcher to be a cheap weapon, and they'd be right, but its use does require some thought and timing, since you cannot instantly pull it out and fire away, instead you have to wait for a moment for your character to get it ready, giving enemies ample time to shoot you down or close the distance so you cannot kill them without killing yourself. The cheapshot weapons like this may seem like they could ruin the game and cause the most skilled players to get constantly wrecked by the biggest shooter virgin alive. But it actually doesn't ruin anything, since you also have the same weapons as they do, making this in my opinion a very casual multiplayer game.
(As of patch 1.4, the rocket launcher cooldown is now spread out between lives, meaning you can no longer die and have it ready to go after an 8 second respawn time instead of waiting a minute or so to have it back)
The gamemodes and maps are fun and visually interesting in their designs, bright colors and massive backdrops create some outstanding environments that aren't too distracting from the gameplay itself. You've got your standard multiplayer maps like King of the Hill, Capture the Flag and Free-For-All, but also some unique gamemodes that takes full advantage of the fact that you're playing small toy soldiers in a big world. Like the birthday cake map where the objective is for one team to use their flamethrowers to light as many candles as they can before time runs out, while the other team has to defend the cake, switching at the end of a round, with whatever team having the most candles lit wins.
Does it have its flaws? Yeah... The third person perspective I feel doesn't really do the game many favors, it's difficult to see which weapon you're holding in the middle of an engagement, for example the M-16 and the sniper rifle, since they lack a distinctive silhouette when your soldier is holding them. Also, because of the third-person view the most important HUD elements are subdued, being difficult to notice when you're in the middle of a firefight. How much ammo is in your currently selected weapon or how much health you have doesn't show all too well in the middle of gameplay.
I feel like this game would benefit so much more if you were allowed to at least toggle between first and third-person views, like you could in Tribes: Ascend, and I really think the HUD needs an overhaul. But all things considered, it's nothing that completely ruins anything, because like I said, it's casual multiplayer. If you're looking for some simple, easy to pick up and play multiplayer fun with an interesting design twist, then the Mean Greens - Plastic Warfare is right up your alley.
