Prague itself could easily be a level pulled out of a Hitman game with some techy props added, it's very generic, filled with NPC speaking a corny slavic accent (I think Prague bothers me more than it should because I'm a Western Slav myself and I'm used to everything it has to show, but this is where having multiple hubs would help the game). Due to the unchanging scenery, running around the city becomes a chore towards the end. With same locations all the time it feels like a going-to-work experience - I already get that in reality. Even simulation games offer more escapism in this regard.
The side missions, I'm not sure if doing away with loading screens for side locations was a good idea, though everything is integral to the mission hub, it now ends up sharing it's dreariness (see above).
The mechanics are ok, though playing through everything as you go, Jensen becomes a powerhouse, and towards the end unstoppable.
I feel as Mankind Divided is to Human Revolution what Invisible War was to Deus Ex. I would suggest that the developer invests time in a series of strong story driven, multiple location based expansion set. I would parallelly suggest that the player base purchase a 'Director's Cut' or similar later re-release containing all the content. At this stage, unfortunately the experience is rather generic in all the areas you've come to expect to be great from the acclaimed titles in the series and right now this a Deus Ex game only by title and some game mechanics but could just as easily be one of those 'quite ok for an indie game' titles if you removed the name.

AaaaaAAaaaAAAaaAAAAaAAAAA!!! – A Reckless Disregard for Gravity is a game in which you play a virtual basejumper who jumps through a series of maps attempting to rack up points by staying close to obstacles, spray-painting buildings, flipping off people who dislike you, and breaking plates with points on them while still landing safely. The levels are mostly very stylized (with a few which are meant to mimic natural landscapes). The game is very entertaining for the first bit, but is best experienced in bite-sized chunks. Once you've done a few levels, take a break and come back later - it can get repetitive rapidly, and while the later levels definitely add a lot more to keep track of, the core mechanics remain consistent.
It's a pity, because the later levels are the better ones in the game, but ultimately, since the replayability is based off of the levels you've unlocked it doesn't feel like there's a great deal of depth beyond what you see on the surface.
I had a good time with it. However, I've only played about 5 hours and I feel "done" with it - I don't have any particular desire to go back into it. If you're looking for a neat, stylized experience? Hard to do any better. Just don't expect a whole lot of play time for your dollars.

Trine 2 is one of these games which you kinda neglect at first, thinking "Huh, that looks really weird, why did I even install it?" but after five minutes, you are completely sunk into the game.
In Trine 2, just like the original Trine we control three heroes: Amadeus the Wizard, Zoya the Thief and Pontius the Warrior. All three of them have unique abilities which complement each other - Amadeus can levitate most objects in the game, Zoya can grapple and swing around, while Pontius' shield protects him from most harm done. If you are playing singleplayer, you can control only one, though you can shuffle between them any time.
Even though Trine 2 has pretty interesting solo game, the core comes when playing with friends - the co-op is endless fun and becomes a bit more strategic, opening new ways of completing objectives.
All in all, Trine 2 is amazing and very fun to play game. Pick it now, you won't regret it.

나름 괜찮은 FPS 게임이다.
중국을 대상으로 벌이는 전투는 신박했으며, 중국의 인해전술의 무서움을 제대로 느껴볼 수 있다.
무섭다기 보단 심히 피로해진다.
본디 아르마와 아버지는 같으나, 아르마가 이 작품의 뿌리에서 분리(퇴사)되어 만들어진 정신적인 후속작인 반면, 이 작품은 초기의 모습을 거의 버리고 '라이트'함을 계속 꾸준히 증가시킨 계통으로 보면 된다.
사뭇 진지한 밀리터리 물이고, 여타 다른 쉬운 FPS에 비해서 난이도가 좀 있는 편이지만
다른 빡센 작품들에 비하면 아주 쉬운편.
(레드 오케스트라, 아르마를 해보라...어렵다)
게임 자첸 평이하게 만들었고, 그래픽도 준수하나..
차량 이동 파트에서 너무 시간을 잡아먹기 때문에 전투를 하면서 전혀 긴장감을 느낄 수 없다.
브라보 분대에 소속된 주인공 중 한 명을 맡아서 하는데, 이 때 자신의 역할을 선택할 수 있다.
소총수, 스나이퍼, 공병 등의 역할을 선택하고 그 역할로 진행하면 해당 역할에 대한 레벨이 오르는데 이 때 퍽이나 무기 선택 폭이 다양해지는 방식이다. 달리기, 정확도 등의 스킬도 따로 키워 줄 수 있다.
혼자서 하게되면 AI 3개를 통솔하는 브라보 팀의 분대장이 되며, 코옵을 하게될 경우 1P가 분대장을 맡게된다.
AI들이 생각보다 멍청해서 좀 고생이 심한데, 분대장(또는 플레이어)이 내리는 통솔 명령을 시기적절하게만 잘 써주면 치료도 해주러 오며, 공격, 대기 등 세밀한 명령이 가능하다. 근데 신경을 전혀 안쓰면 애들이 안 움직이거나 너무 멍청해져서 고생이 심해진다. 하다보면 애들이 이미 죽어있을 정도.
총 10개의 미션을 진행하는데 처음엔 플탐이 적어도 후반을 갈 수록 미션 하나 당 플탐이 많이 소요되는 것도 특징. 이유는 맵이 넓고(아름답다), 서브 미션이 생각보다 다양하기 때문이다.
전쟁이라기 보다는 특수 부대 임무를 띄는 느낌이 강한 편.
혼자서 하면 재미를 아주 못느낄 가능성이 농후하지만, 친구와 같이 한다면 '코옵'이라는 마법의 작용으로 생각보다 재밌어진다.
GFWL 제거 예정에 없는 게임이지만, 2014년 7월 1일에 종료한다던 GFWL 서비스가 연장됨에 따라 가지고 있다면 지인들과 분대를 짜서 플레이해보는 것도 좋을 것이다.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is beautiful visually with a story that strikes anyone with a heart to the core. It is a great example of a game that remains interesting without combat-centric mechanics. If you like narratives, some puzzles, and an overall well sewn together experience, then you will love this game.
This is the best "short" game that I have played yet.

I'm writing this review fairly late, but hopefully it's helpful to someone. Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons makes a great case for being the supreme example of video games as art. Not for the graphics, although I find them lovely. Not because of the story, although I find it touching. Rather, this game provides a perfect marriage between its gameplay and its theme. And the cohesion between the two creates a unique work of art that other mediums simply cannot touch.
I know there is a long battle in the game criticism community about the merits of gameplay versus narrative, but I don't think that you have to "take a side" when it comes to this game. Just play it and experience it for yourself.
Also, I actually played it with my wife, splitting the controls between the two of us. So if you want to try playing it with two people in the same room, it's certainly doable.

If you rolled the skydiving game from Pilotwings in LSD and sent it hurtling into the future, you’d surely end up with something similar to A Reckless Disregard for Gravity. The game is set in a psychedelic, alternate-reality version of Boston, Massachusetts in which buildings are nonsensically scattered throughout 3D space. This convoluted landscape provides the perfect playground for base jumpers with a reckless… you know. You play as one such base jumper from a first person perspective. Each level sees you taking a leap of faith from the tallest building, navigating your way through an architectural maze, then gracefully landing on a platform at then end. On your way down you rack up points by maneuvering dangerously close to obstacles and smashing through glass panels. As you progress you’ll unlock other abilities such as flipping off protesters and giving your fans a thumbs up. Snaking your way through a deadly obstacle course while chaining together the appropriate gestures is incredibly satisfying. It takes some time to get used to the controls, but the payoff is worth it. I would have liked to have seen joystick support, and the menu system could use some serious work, but otherwise A Reckless Disregard for Gravity is a clever game with a fun sense of humor that will leave you itching for one more jump.

A basejumping game with a style similar to the old school skateboarding games. (This game makes me think of the old Playstation title Grind Session.) The gameplay couldn't be simpler. W,A,S,D for movement and space to deploy your parachute. Try to get as close to the buildings as possible without actually crashing into them, and try to collect as many points as you can on the way down. What's not to like?
A Millenium Falcon simulator with a great sense of humor.

With so many retro games trying to capture the feel of the 80s, it's ironic that Blood Dragon, from big budget publisher Ubisoft, does it the best. Everything here is a checklist of the era that I grew up with, and in such a tongue-in-cheek delivery that had me laughing out loud way too many times. It was clear that everyone involved had a lot of fun making this game. Micheal Biehn, who was sadly phoning it in for a recent blockbuster game  (And who wouldn't if you knew the game I was talking about), is incredible here with his self-deprecating portrayal of the 80s action hero that he helped create.
Gameplay wise, while I'm not a big fan of open world games, the playing field of Blood Dragon is almost perfect to me: Not too sprawling with a an intimidating amount of repetitive minigames, but not too small that that game ends too soon. Although there came a point when I felt like things were getting tedious, lo and behold I finished not only the game, but all side quests and collectibles! A big feat for someone who skips these things in open world. Far out, Far Cry 3. Far. Out.

I installed the game being not convinced at all, thinking it's be just another Brawl copy...
Then found myself spending quite some time on it !
The first impression you get is quite wrong : this game isn't a Brawl copy with close to no items and bland characters.
The fight are a lot quicker and more difficult as your level goes up.
The weapon system is interesting, and the fact that every character uses a different set of weapons makes it easier to choose who to play.
The balance is also pretty good, all characters are viable so just play who you think looks cool and have fun !
I also really love the skill-cap in this game, which is very high : the game has a few combos for every weapon that you will have to learn and master by yourself.
The game isn't P2W, since you get gold quickly by playing, add to that daily quests and login rewards. Basically if you play regularly you can get a character every 12 days or so (if you play a lot it'll be quicker than that ;)  ).
After ~180 hours i had unlocked every character without paying money, and have way enough to buy the new ones everytime they come out
The game has a hero rotation, like LoL or Smite, which changes every week, so even if you don't have many heroes to play, you'll still be able to try new ones regularly.
Mammoth coins (the in-game currency) is very expensive, but it's mostly there to buy skins (you can buy characters as well, but it's much cheaper to buy the all-characters pack directly (i didn't buy it))
However the game suffers from a few problems :
1) LAG , GODDAMNIT... This is a very recurrent problem, it affects some people more than others for no apparent reason, and can be game-ruining most of the time. A buddy of mine has frequent lag spikes when playing, i don't and we live 50 meters apart... what the hell ? Note that he does not have a lag issue in any other games...
2) TOXIC COMMUNITY ! If you can't stand your opponents boasting and spamming "ez" "rekt" "hattori pro" after winning , or "f*** you" "spammer" after loosing, then you probably shouldn't pay any attention to the chat. Nice players are a rarity in this game, you've been warned...
3) Mammoth coins price : now, now, i know this is mostly for skins and stuff, but still. Paying 6€ for a skin in a game like this feels way too expensive (the price gets better if you spend 20€ at once, but then you might prefer to buy the character pack instead, your choice)
But overall the game is fun, especially (in my opinion) when played with friends in 1v1v1v1 or in coop 2v2.

I installed the game being not convinced at all, thinking it's be just another Brawl copy...
Then found myself spending quite some time on it !
The first impression you get is quite wrong : this game isn't a Brawl copy with close to no items and bland characters.
The fight are a lot quicker and more difficult as your level goes up.
The weapon system is interesting, and the fact that every character uses a different set of weapons makes it easier to choose who to play.
The balance is also pretty good, all characters are viable so just play who you think looks cool and have fun !
I also really love the skill-cap in this game, which is very high : the game has a few combos for every weapon that you will have to learn and master by yourself.
The game isn't P2W, since you get gold quickly by playing, add to that daily quests and login rewards. Basically if you play regularly you can get a character every 12 days or so (if you play a lot it'll be quicker than that ;)  ).
After ~180 hours i had unlocked every character without paying money, and have way enough to buy the new ones everytime they come out
The game has a hero rotation, like LoL or Smite, which changes every week, so even if you don't have many heroes to play, you'll still be able to try new ones regularly.
Mammoth coins (the in-game currency) is very expensive, but it's mostly there to buy skins (you can buy characters as well, but it's much cheaper to buy the all-characters pack directly (i didn't buy it))
However the game suffers from a few problems :
1) LAG , GODDAMNIT... This is a very recurrent problem, it affects some people more than others for no apparent reason, and can be game-ruining most of the time. A buddy of mine has frequent lag spikes when playing, i don't and we live 50 meters apart... what the hell ? Note that he does not have a lag issue in any other games...
2) TOXIC COMMUNITY ! If you can't stand your opponents boasting and spamming "ez" "rekt" "hattori pro" after winning , or "f*** you" "spammer" after loosing, then you probably shouldn't pay any attention to the chat. Nice players are a rarity in this game, you've been warned...
3) Mammoth coins price : now, now, i know this is mostly for skins and stuff, but still. Paying 6€ for a skin in a game like this feels way too expensive (the price gets better if you spend 20€ at once, but then you might prefer to buy the character pack instead, your choice)
But overall the game is fun, especially (in my opinion) when played with friends in 1v1v1v1 or in coop 2v2.

OFP: Red River is a very average shooter, and nothing more. When it comes to realism, it's somewhere between Call of Duty and ARMA with one-hit kills, large maps and bullet drops etc. If you excpect something like the first OFP games, you will be disappointed and I recommend trying ARMA II and ARMA III instead.
The single player campaign is very dull and annoying, and this is mostly because of the dumbass AI. You basically have to fulfill the role of fireteam leader, combat medic, anti-tank and anti-air soldier and also the sniper. Your fireteam is only good for suppressing enemies and they occasionally succeed in busting a cap in the a*s of a random chinaman, but usually they just annoy the hell out of me by getting shot and not fixing me up when I get wounded. The enemy AI is as stupid as the one of your teammates, and most of the firefights feel like being at a shooting gallery popping seemingly endless amounts of infantry from a distance.
The story is pretty basic "hoorah murica get sum" action with the U.S Marines saving the world, first from the evil imaginary taleban-Tajikistans, and then from the Chinese Army.
The best moments of the game are when you have room to improvise and can use the vast landscape to flank the enemy, but unfortunately these moments are too few. Most missions are just shooting couple of enemies, sitting on the back of a HUMMVEE and repeating it all over again.
The co-op feature pretty much saves the games, since if you have a couple of friends you don't have to deal with the dumbass AI all the time. There is also a leveling system with some customization available and you can unlock new gear and weapons for four different classes, which is nice and rewarding.
If you enjoy FPS-games and want something more slower-paced than Call of Duty and Battlefield, try this one out. It was featured in one of the Humble Bundles a while back. It's still very buggy, although it has been out for years and it also forces you to use GFWL, which sucks.

570 hours ago, me and a buddy were at work, and he told me about this game, after our shift was over we went back to our homes, and i downloaded this game. 567 hours (as of this review) later and here I Am.
I fell in love with this game, I was seeking a decently paced, entertaining WW2 game, and I found it; in this game.
I played constantly, invested both time and money in the game; with veteren subscription, I played until my eyes bled, it made me late for work more than a time or two, and caused me to drag tail on a few shifts, but well worth it.
But the ever evolving GUI, and game changes, additions seemed to push me away from the game. I call that period the Dark Days, because for some reason; either by design or accident, I landed on dark maps, or fog maps, or some hybrid mix of the two, and could not see anything on it at all.
Fast forward and now its gone final, and i have revisited it for almost 40hrs this week and can say they have done a fabulous job on the game. It seems well polished for what its evolved from. I do think the new character select/mod screens are not nearly as good as some of the early pre-final versions though; and think it needs some decent cleaning up. In fact thats what was really frustrating, i really liked the way the older character screens looked, i now have to click on things to see, that i should see there by default. But thats personal preference. I've grown used to it already.
But; all in all, i'm not going to fault the game for any oddities i experience online, it comes with the nature of online game play. But by and large its a stable game, I think its truly above and beyond what Battlefield 1 is; or tried to be. Its got substance to it, theres a decent Meta to the game as well when it comes to load outs, and character selection/evolution.
But most of all, its fun, and the teams are sizeable, theres all skill levels of players, and all sorts of great guns, and vehicles (you can drive TANKS!) and its Free To Play! It costs nothing but some time to try it, if you give it half a chance, you'll quickly want to play it more and more.

it's The Mean Greens Plastic Warfare released in late 2015 for the PC with a PS4 and Xbox One release planned but with no announcement for a release date quiet yet as of this review.
Plastic Warfare is your not so standard 3rd person shooter, the game is purely multiplayer based, so sadly there isn't any single player or campaign mode to be found. You either create or pick a lobby, pick a side; either green or tan, you vote for a map, and the greatest war of our time begins... The fight for green or tan supremacy.
The game over all as of this review currently only has 10 maps, each map having it's own specific game mode assigned to it, ranging from capture the flag in a fish tank, to defending cookies on a train going around a Christmas tree, to my personal favorite two teams attempting to thaw out their toy dinosaurs in a freezer with flame throwers.
Each game mode and map consists of teams of 5 versus 5, theirs no specific classes or anything like that, you basically spawn with 5 weapons at your disposal, your standard rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle, missile launcher, and flamethrower; each with a set amount of ammo that will replenish with a cool down effect once used up.
But is it any good? Let's find out with...
THE GOOD
-Maps and game modes are the star of the game and extremely unique and fun to play in and explore
-Simple and easy to learn but effective gameplay with tons of variety in the game modes
-Looks fantastic and runs smoothly even on mid-tier computers
Probably the best part about Plastic Warfare is easily the map designs and concept of the game itself, heavily reminding of games from years past such as the Army Men Series and Toy Commander on the SEGA Dreamcast. Plastic Warfare's maps are absolutely fantastic, unique, and a joy to explore, but not only that the game modes that accompany them are just as creative.
Everything from trying to capture your enemies flags on rubber ducks in a bathtub, to lighting more candles than the opposing team for a birthday cake, to as I mentioned earlier trying to thaw out a plastic dinosaur, all while still including classic game modes you'd expect such as capture the flag, but however now in a fish tank, to your classic death match mode but now set up on a game board originally meant for dice rolling and for plastic army men, to plenty more the variety in game modes and maps in this game are fantastic.
The gameplay overall itself is simple enough to pick up and play straight from the start without much of a learning curve to it, I don't expect this game to attempt to become an e-sport or anything but the gameplay itself is effective, each weapon you're equipped with all have their uses and right times to utilize them, none of them I thought felt over powered or unbalanced which for a new release title is a pretty good feat to achieve and depending on well your team works together you can easily dominate the match if the other team is just focused on thinking it's nothing but a death match mode.
Now graphically Plastic Warfare looks absolutely fantastic, running on the Unreal 4 Engine the texture work and environments across the 10 maps look great, not to mention all while running extremely smooth even on a mid-tier computer like mine.
The environments are bright and colorful as well with tons of attention to detail and great ideas for the map designs, the character models of the army men stand out enough to spot and shoot them as well and the animations are passable, but over all the game simply looks and runs great.
The soundtrack as well is pretty decent, each map has it's own specific theme, most of which are pretty decent, but I personally hated the birthday cake map's soundtrack after about 30 seconds of hearing it. But over all the soundtrack pretty great.
But now let's discuss...
THE BAD
-Matchmaking is a bit of pain and connection issues
-5 vs 5 Is a bit lacking and I feel some maps could have increased the player count
-Texture pop-in and other minor graphical issues
During my 3 to 4 hours or so I spent with The Mean Greens probably my biggest issue with it, is simply the matchmaking was a bit of a pain, not to mention a few connection issues.
Trying to actually FIND a game for me personally at times was a bit of a mess, probably because it was the weekend, I'm not sure, but I had a number of host was lost connecting issues and was booted back to the main menu more times than I can count after failing to connect, so then I had to go back into the server list again and wait some more while it refreshed again which became a tad bit annoying.
Then throw in match making issues and trying to actually play with my friend, it just added to the annoyance of it all, once we were connected together, the game had trouble even finding any matches for us once we got the party system going, which more or less forced us to simply create our own lobby and server and wait on other players instead.
But honestly that's probably one of the only major complaints I have with this game and I'm sure it'll be fixed with future updates or at least here's hoping as this is a game I could easily see myself playing some more of in the future.
My next issue, much more minor and opinionated, I felt some of the maps could have benefited with a higher player count than 5 vs 5, as there were times I had a hard time even finding people on some of the larger more death match focused maps such as the Art Table map, but I'm sure with modding from the community and future updates this will also change.
Graphically I only had the odd stutter or weird frame rate inconsistency here and there, but that's more than likely due to my mid-tier computer set up at the moment. However I noticed despite running on max settings the game still did suffer from some minor pop in issues here and there when the maps first loaded in.
But now it's time I give...
THE OPINION
Now if you're like me and you stumbled onto this on the front page of Steam, it probably caught your eye, it sure did for me and I can definitely recommend this to anyone who maybe interested, the gameplay is fast paced, simple yet effective, and fun.
The maps and game modes are gorgeous looking and unique and if you've got some friends looking for a game to play over the next weekend or two this wouldn't be a bad choice and for only $10 it's fair on the price.
I had a ton of fun during my roughly 4 hours with it and couldn't recommend it enough, hopefully the match making gets improved with future patches, I can definitely see myself playing this more in the future.

"
" is a game based on a simple concept: jump off a high point, do some sick tricks to earn points, and land on the ground safely. Despite many positive aspects, the game is marred by several technical and aesthetic choices made by the developers.
* Unique use of humor.
* Excellent sound track and sound effects.
* The base-jumping mechanic is a new, innovate way of playing games. It is a joy to jump from your starting point and hear the rush of the wind blow across your avatar's ears.
* Flight controls are good enough to seem realistic but forgiving enough to let you make a few mistakes and have fun.
* Plenty of unique ways to score points: getting close to objects, staying close to objects, giving spectators a thumbs-up or an obscene gesture, and spraypainting graffiti were all things I found within my first hour or two of play.
* For the world's first base-jumping game, the game feels remarkably NOT like base-jumping. Rather than zooming along the side of tall skyscrapers and landing on the ground, the player instead navigates an obstacle course of abstract, floating blocks that stand to "represent" buildings and lands on a final circular block that is meant to represent the ground. If the player overshoots "the ground," he continues to fall. Yes, you can actually miss the ground. Interestingly, the levels that feature base-jumping off a mountain feature a well-modeled and detailed mountain that actually resembles something like a real mountain. (If you are going to use aestheticized shapes to represent real-world objects, why not do it consistently?)
* Every aspect of the game, from the UI to the action portion, looks and feels like a first-generation iPhone game. From the big, finger-friendly buttons conveniently placed on opposite corners of the screen, to the simplistic level design, to the generic graphics.
* The simple level design gives the game a very low difficulty level. I understand the point of the game is to score points and not just to reach the bottom of the map, but I wish there were a few more levels where it would be a challenge to reach the landing pad.
* Although there are several dozen levels (80), the variety of them is lacking. Each level is essentially the same as the last; none of them seem more or less fun than any others.
* No backgrounds in any level. Every level has a simple color gradient for a background. How about at least a simple sky wallpaper?
* The game has a horrible name. There is no way I am going to talk to my friends and be able to mention this game by name, which hurts word-of-mouth recommendations. It's as if the developers
chose this name because they wanted to come first alphabetically, and then later released  "1...2...3... Kick It" when they realized that numbers precede letters in Steam's alphabetizing system.

First and foremost, Sims 3 is a nice game. I don't like how much dlc it has but the base game itself is fun. Since it's on sale, I went ahead and got the bundle. I suggest you do the same before it's too late. The price for everything kept me from getting this game for the longest time and now's the time to grab everything. Personally though, I'd just grab the base game and maybe the bundle. One other complaints I have by the way is that the game tends to crash from time to time. In about 3 or so hours I've had two crashes. It doesn't break the game for me but it that bit definitely isn't fun.
On to the game itself, it's precisely what you'd think it is. A Simulation. A simulation of the day to day lives of people. I like to think of it as a doll maker that let's you take it a step further by letting you watch your characters come to life and follow their dreams, aspirations, and then die a hilariously human death. The game can feel a little off putting upon first starting it up. After my first hour, I felt rather unsure of what to do next. I had created two characters based on a favorite book of mine, "Good Omens," and then had them move into this house out near the country. I contemplated whether or not this game was for me but when I was a child my sister had Sims 2. I remember enjoying it so much that it got me to stop playing World of Warcraft for a few days. That was truly quite the feat back then! After spending some more time with Sims 3, I now know why it temporarily broke my addiction back then. Because the Sims too is a fun and addictive just like my all time favorite game WoW! Now then, Sim 2 isn't Sims 3 per-say but it's just as I remember it. You got a few characters, have them go to work and do basic upkeep, form relationships, etc... Every little virtual day they grow more and more. Heck, after a few hours with this game I feel hyped up to go clean my house, continue working on my skills, and follow my career. Let's play the Sims first though heh...
All in all, I recommend Sims 3. It's a classic game franchise that's both fun and relaxing in nature. Perhaps one of the nicest things about this game is that it's a game anyone can enjoy. There's no tremendous learning curve, no brutal challenges, and no end in sight! Unless you count crashes but still... Play as you wish and there's no rush. If you've been looking for something to relax with, maybe get a little creative, or perhaps take a break from constantly dying in other games, then Sims 3 is for you!

You know that guy who slaughters all the noobs with highly advanced weaponry that makes everything feel unbalanced? I'm that guy. I was the dude who looked up all the stats for every gun, knows the armor thickness and speed of every tank in the game, and consistantly topped the leaderboard. I played for a while, not as long as some, much longer than others. And I had a lot of fun. I paid about $15 once because I figured all the problems in this game could be fixed if I helped out a little bit, but all the rest of it, the OHK sniper rifle, my super high level American, I got that all through grinding. And it wasn't even a grind sometimes, I had fun.
But I can't recommend this game. If you don't already have at least my amount of time in this game, you're done. It used to be that you started with one soldier from each faction and had grenades to go with your starting weapon. You had something to get you up on your feet. Not any more. I've seen the expenses of every item go up nearly double. It went from being bordering on unreasonable to almost insane. But I already had the good gear on one of my characters, so I kept playing. Firing thirty bullets from my rifle cut into half my earnings and other equipment brought me near to breaking even. So I had to nerf my own character to continue playing, and I couldn't go back to my nub characters without being so badly killed I didn't have fun. "Git gud" doesn't apply here. I've been on the other end of the slaughter. There is nothing a new player to stand against someone with better equipment except take pot shots at a distance and hope to scrap together some XP, which isn't fun. And if a game isn't fun, its not worth playing.
The real nail in the coffin is the technical issues. It got so bad that I couldn't stay in a match for more than a minute before the entire game went bonkers. After a couple days of this, I just stopped trying. It really isn't worth the trouble.
TL;DR
It was fun, now its not because grind/technical issues/not new player friendly. Give it a shot if you want, could be your cup of tea, wasn't mine. This is an opinion, just like every review. Treat it as such when you are making your decision, and bear in mind its free-to-play, so there's no harm in trying it yourself.

While this game is incredibly fun and addicting, there's just not enough people that play. As an avid LOTR fan, I love the game, but to me, it's lagging behind all the other games. This game, in short, has a very small community; you can't even find a dungeon unless you wait a half hour or more. I do, however, like the story aspect to it, as it follows the storyline as the books tell it and not how the movies tell it. It does not have all the features as the leading MMORPGs do, but it could definitely be a competitor if there was more time and effort put into advertising the game. Even if it doesn't have a ton of features compared to other MMORPGs, it is free to play, with the option of paying for expansions in-game. The free-to-play aspect is rarely seen in today's gaming world, but it is also very restricted. This game has a great potential and there is an immense amount of people who love the LOTR franchise as well as the related Hobbit franchise.
Like I said earlier, this game is very addicting and has potential, but I'm not going to recommend it. My recommendation for if you want to find a good MMORPG is to look somewhere else. Yes, I'm going to say it; look towards World of Warcraft. It is much more addicting and has a much bigger community base than LOTRO. Also, Elder Scrolls Online has just been released for the PC and will soon be released for the PS4 and Xbox One. ESO has a lot of potential and should definitely be considered.
Your opinion on LOTRO may be different from mine, so download it for FREE and give it a try.

Brothers-A Tale of Two Sons is an adventure game where you play as both an older brother and a younger brother who are desperately searching for a medicine that will cure their sick father. There is no dialogue in the game, but you are able to understand exactly what the brothers are "saying" when they are communicating. As you play through the game, you will begin to notice the strengths and weaknesses both brothers have. I won't spoil anything, but as an example, the older brother is blinded by his attraction to young beauty and the younger brother will do some stupid things sometimes, such as knocking something over when trying to sneak past a sleeping giant. Brothers is one of those stories where you are always surprised by what's around the corner. The world you step into is full of fantastical creatures, odd rituals and scary moments. It shows the connection 2 brothers can have with each other when it really matters. As a younger brother to a sister, I can very much relate to what the protagonists can do and will do to protect their sibling. The visuals of this game are amazing, from looking over massive mountain ranges, to creeping through small caves, you will be astonished in how good this game looks. The music is great! It's timed at the perfect moment when you enter a certain area and it never gives anything away. Finally for the verdict: Brothers is an excellent game full of heartbreak, action and surprises around every corner, it will blow you away with it's excellent movie like visuals and gameplay, along with keeping you guessing with it's soundtrack. I would pick this game up any chance you get. 10/10 in my eyes.

Very nice expansion, Sisters of Battle and Dark Eldar compliment the current races very nicely. SoB's are like the Space Marines but they have a lot more special abilities, especially with their Faith rescource. Some of their abilities are veeeeeeery nice. The Dark Eldar are also extremely fun, and they have a special resource too, Soul Essence. The Dark Eldar use theirs differently (its on a toolbar, rather than the SoB's being on units), and they actually have some useful, if not a little overpowered, abilities.
You can also now place turrets anywhere in open territory, which is pretty nice for setting up things like checkpoints, bottlenecks and kill zones, especially when using the IG (Imperial Guard) and their heavy weapon squads in tandem with the turrets.
The campaign runs differently as well. Instead of one planet, you fight over 4 planets, with webgates transferring between planets. Without them, you cannot transfer to any other planet other than your starting one (Unless you're Dark Eldar, as they get an ability to travel to ANY gate). You get your Honour Guard, and you get your garrisons as well. AND, each race has their own abilities, such as the T'au having a cannon that damages the defending area, or the Chaos Space Marines who ignore broken supply lines.
What's better, they run their servers off their Company of Heroes servers since Gamespy tried to money-grab off them, and the new MP is pretty sleek and pretty. Odd lag spike but that always happens in any game. Overall, 8/10.

Dawn of War Soulstorm is the final piece of the Dawn of War 1 "series." It added 2 factions (Dark Eldar and Sisters of Battle) and 1 new unit for each race. The comparisons to Dark Crusade are inevitable so let's compare and contrast. Dark Crusade's persistant bases give you a reason to prolong a match so as to build up a good base for the next fight. Unfortunately, it also means that defenses can be insurmountable creating a World War 1 like stalemate. This was done away with in Soulstorm which created much shorter more offensive gameplay.
Other complaints I have heard is in regards to the voice acting as opposed to Dark Crusade. Well, actually, this is true. There is significantly reduced dialogue in this one compared to Dark Crusade. Which is a genuine shame considering how much I enjoyed the back-and-forth of the two commanders as I assaulted a stronghold.
Would I recommend it though? Short answer. Yes, just look at my time played. Of course this game is worth the money, and then some. If you need a great RTS or love Warhammer 40K, grab this game. Just do it.

A common strategy is to place a heavy gunner, LMG, on suppressive fire, a sniper on overwatch and than send one soldier to flank right or left while you flank the other direction. Instead, just like 3 or 4 bullets from the assault rifle kills you.  Again, made worse by the fact every single person gets a rocket launcher.
The player count is redicoulously low. Just 5 v. 5.  I think the minimum standard these days is 8 v 8, with most games eager to reach rediculous player counts.

What do I think about this game? Well...
First off, the only part of the game that has any real meaning is the ending and one area of the game that you have to find an item at, which I shall not spoil. But I will say that why this item is in this situation makes no sense. Everything else is just Alice in Wonderland. Also, ducking is pointless. SPOILER ALERT:
Speaking of finding, that's a lot of what you have to do in this game.
Some objects must be found in order to advance, some of which have no significant meaning, such as the blockhead doll or the bag of seeds.
Other items straight-up take you back to the first area, such as the bus pass, and are only useful for backtracking to find an item or tool you need. You could spam the compass to find what you need, but sometimes it will lead you into an area and stop working.
I should probably clarify what tools are. Keep in mind that tools are different than items in that they are used by pressing space to access the tool menu rather than advance the game. They aren't called that in-game but I'll use that name here since there is no distinction.
The way some tools are implemented is questionable. The umbrella, glasses, magnifying glass, watch, and paint bucket being in the tool menu are pointless because unequipping them downgrades your character. Let me explain each.
Remember how I said that you need to press space to access the tool menu? It is also used to toggle your tools on and off. This is irritating because sometimes you can press it a couple of times on accident to unequip the umbrella, which again, outright removes the ability to slowly fall, and is sometimes is a pain to reequip this necessary item or find out that it's unequipped when you need it. And the fact that space is the same button used to equip items and (from what I've played) there isn't any other way to get out of the tool menu, so you need to either select an empty tool slot, or use an item that you don't equip, such as the compass.
Do I reccomend this game? I really wish there was a grey area, but I feel there isn't much justification to make a purchase with the above listed gameplay and "story" faults.
You don't buy this game for challenge or story. You're buying an experience at best.
EDIT: I should mention that I was able to finish this game in one sitting with the 106 minutes that is displayed in my library. You should probably get this in a sale for that length.

While this game is incredibly fun and addicting, there's just not enough people that play. As an avid LOTR fan, I love the game, but to me, it's lagging behind all the other games. This game, in short, has a very small community; you can't even find a dungeon unless you wait a half hour or more. I do, however, like the story aspect to it, as it follows the storyline as the books tell it and not how the movies tell it. It does not have all the features as the leading MMORPGs do, but it could definitely be a competitor if there was more time and effort put into advertising the game. Even if it doesn't have a ton of features compared to other MMORPGs, it is free to play, with the option of paying for expansions in-game. The free-to-play aspect is rarely seen in today's gaming world, but it is also very restricted. This game has a great potential and there is an immense amount of people who love the LOTR franchise as well as the related Hobbit franchise.
Like I said earlier, this game is very addicting and has potential, but I'm not going to recommend it. My recommendation for if you want to find a good MMORPG is to look somewhere else. Yes, I'm going to say it; look towards World of Warcraft. It is much more addicting and has a much bigger community base than LOTRO. Also, Elder Scrolls Online has just been released for the PC and will soon be released for the PS4 and Xbox One. ESO has a lot of potential and should definitely be considered.
Your opinion on LOTRO may be different from mine, so download it for FREE and give it a try.

This game is just not fun.
As someone who has put many hours into this game, I can say for sure that it just gets bad.
First off: when you first get the game, it can be pretty fun and is easy to learn, making it pretty fun to play with a couple friends. Casual play is nice, but nothing special.
Competitive play is different. If you play this game as often as someone like me or possibly more, then you will realize just how bad this game is. Usually you end up facing the same legends over and over again, creating a lack of variety. Also, the light and aerial attacks is shared between weapons, so if characters have the same weapons, they only have three different moves. This creates a lack of distinction between characters and repetitive gameplay. There is almost no variety between characters, as even most heavy attacks are just copy/pasted from other legends. This is my personal opinion although some may not agree: the weapon throwing mechanic is terrible. As you climb the rankings into gold and platinum, you will see more and more people only throwing weapons at you in order to start combos or stun you for a heavy attack. It ends up just being not fun to gift these people, making the game more boring, as you can never seem to get close to these people. Sure, a well times air dodge could work, but the weapon spawn rate is so fast that they can immediately take a weapon and punish the dodge. It does seem creative and sets brawlhalla apart from other fighting games, but ultimately adds to the redundancy of the fighting.
Brawlhalla is a casual game and should not be played for a long time. If you play a lot and climb high, then you will see how bland and boring the game becomes. Now I only play this game as a way to pass the time, like old people play solitaire. That is how boring the game has become for me.
Another huge problem is the community. Higher ranked people are nice and will actually try to help you, but in ranks like gold and silver, almost everyone is a jerk. When you lose, they'll brag and spam a phrase to make fun of you, even if they only beat you by a little. If you win, they'll call you out for spamming or just complain and say you got lucky. It makes for an overall toxic community with players staring out. Brawlhalla is a free game though, so perhaps I should not harshly criticize it. It can be fun for a few hours at most, but the core concepts of the game make for bland, repetitive and clunky gameplay, and the community will just make you mad.

Excellent game of WWII grand strategy.
This is a sequel to Time of Wrath, which I did not play, and they did make another game called strategic war in Europe, which is a game that can be played much faster and its not as detailed as this game.  There is also storm over the pacific which I also own, and its also an excellent game covering the Pacific theater.
What I like about this game is there is enough detail to feel like I have lots of control over my nation, but not so much detail that I just give up trying to play it.  I have enjoyed games like Hearts of Iron II, and Decisive Campaigns Case Blue.  However HOI III was too much, and so games like war in the East and Gary Grisby's other games were just too much for me, as much as I wanted to like those games.
This one though, its just perfect.  FIghting as the Russians against Germany for over a year and a half in my second attempt has been excellent.  I had to change the difficulty to very easy, and Im still struggling to hold on to Leningrad in June of 1942.  There is a thrust toward Stalingrad, and a new one going toward Moscow which will be tough to contain.  This game is fun and challenging for both new wargamers and veterans like me.
The graphics have many options, so you can adjust the map and the units to achive the look that you want.  I think the screen shot of the graphics and my belief that the game would be too simple and have poor AI is what kept me away from these games.  Don't let that stop you.

I guess if I had a real serioius problem I might have to buy the game again trhough Matrix.  So that is the one caveat, the support is really poor. Time of Fury (ToF) is wasteland interactive newest ww2 grand strategy game. Some of you may be familiar with their other tiles, Strategic war Europe, Time of Wrath to name a few. While there are some issue this game seems to fix a lot of the problems with the earlier titles.
Basic
Players can choice from  variety of scenarios ranging from the fall of Poland, the invasion of France, a grand campaign and many others. Turns are a week long and each scenario has different lengths. Players can then choose which countries they wish to control, both major and minor countries can be controled and players can control as many as they feel they can handle.
Units
The game has Infantry, Mechanized troops, armor airborne fighter, tactical bombers, strategic bombers and a variety of navel units. Players can conduct research in the varies units and develop stronger better versions (more attack power). When purchasing a unity players select the unit type, the size (corps or army) and the level (1-4 depending on what they already have unlocked. The price and time before deployment will change based on the player selections.
Diplomacy
There are diplomacy options but it is the basic, convince a future ally to join sooner or an enemy to join later; over throw a government or if your nation allows hold elections in your own country.
Navy
Navy action is simple and basic. You build a fleet and send it to a sea zone. You set the fleet to be either regular (attack enemy fleets) or raider (attack enemy conveys). The computer will randomly decide when there are navel engagements which will take place between the last plaer turn and the first player turn.
What has changed since other Wasteland titles
Well first the interface seems much more user friendly
You also have an increased number of options during the game. For example when Belgium do the French arm the retreating survivors  (add a unit but loss production points) or do they send them on their way. The Germans also have the option to actively look for volunteers for the army or simply stay with recruitment stations
The bad
There are two minor issues with wasteland games.
1. Multiplayer is PBEM (NOTE there is hotseat play at the same computer). Now this is an old system and some may feel it is outdated. With a campaign being over 400 turns I doubt many people are going to
have the time to sit and play very long in a single seating. So while I do not see it is a problem some people may have issue.
2. Game balance
The developers choose to create a more open world than historical acute one. What I mean by that is that it is possible for Romania to have tanks more advanced than the Russians.  There is still no way Romania alone could beat Russia but they may not have the crappy units they had in real life
One other thing with balance, and what I do not understand, is that Russia will not see the economic and military boost after Stalingrad there are no reserve from Siberia coming and it is doubtful the Russian army will ever see the number increase in troops they did in real life.
Final thoughts
ToW is not a bad game, and it is clear Wasteland learned from their mistakes. Sure it has some issues but most are minor and do not take away the enjoyment of the game. Some people will say 'The graphics look old" well these types of games are not about graphics but the play experience.
So if you looking for a decent strategy game with a good bit of depth, but not as deep as hearts of Iron I say give ToW a try.

This game is just not fun.
As someone who has put many hours into this game, I can say for sure that it just gets bad.
First off: when you first get the game, it can be pretty fun and is easy to learn, making it pretty fun to play with a couple friends. Casual play is nice, but nothing special.
Competitive play is different. If you play this game as often as someone like me or possibly more, then you will realize just how bad this game is. Usually you end up facing the same legends over and over again, creating a lack of variety. Also, the light and aerial attacks is shared between weapons, so if characters have the same weapons, they only have three different moves. This creates a lack of distinction between characters and repetitive gameplay. There is almost no variety between characters, as even most heavy attacks are just copy/pasted from other legends. This is my personal opinion although some may not agree: the weapon throwing mechanic is terrible. As you climb the rankings into gold and platinum, you will see more and more people only throwing weapons at you in order to start combos or stun you for a heavy attack. It ends up just being not fun to gift these people, making the game more boring, as you can never seem to get close to these people. Sure, a well times air dodge could work, but the weapon spawn rate is so fast that they can immediately take a weapon and punish the dodge. It does seem creative and sets brawlhalla apart from other fighting games, but ultimately adds to the redundancy of the fighting.
Brawlhalla is a casual game and should not be played for a long time. If you play a lot and climb high, then you will see how bland and boring the game becomes. Now I only play this game as a way to pass the time, like old people play solitaire. That is how boring the game has become for me.
Another huge problem is the community. Higher ranked people are nice and will actually try to help you, but in ranks like gold and silver, almost everyone is a jerk. When you lose, they'll brag and spam a phrase to make fun of you, even if they only beat you by a little. If you win, they'll call you out for spamming or just complain and say you got lucky. It makes for an overall toxic community with players staring out. Brawlhalla is a free game though, so perhaps I should not harshly criticize it. It can be fun for a few hours at most, but the core concepts of the game make for bland, repetitive and clunky gameplay, and the community will just make you mad.

This game, since I started playing it in late 2015, has always been fun. Sure there were a few times when my bullets didn't hit or my equipment didn't work, but it never affected how I played.
A lot of negative reviews state that the grind is awful and the starter weapons suck. As a person who has played almost thousands of matches as a newbie, intermediate and a pro, I can tell you that the starter weapons DO NOT suck, even unmodded. It only takes 3 shots to kill someone with your starter weapon. The grind is half true, usually you need about 1000 points if you want to make a good profit. Repair costs aren't that much if you don't mod the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of your weapon.
Other things that negative reviewers tend to say are that the spawncamping issue is a huge problem. No, it's not. In my thousands of matches, I've only been in a few where I have been spawn camped. And even then, I found a way around the campers.
Thing such as hackers are almost non existant in this game. I have never seen one hacker. Not one. The "hackers" I've encountered were genuinely better than me.
I have a computer with an I3 530 Dual core processor and a GTX 660 (This is not my main computer, it is more of a backup computer than anything), and this game still runs at 20 - 30 FPS. If you crank down the graphics a bit, it goes up to 45 FPS. This game isn't badly optimized at all. There's only a few technical issues that I've ever encountered.
Hit reg is not an issue, granted I have noticed that some headshots don't register. Other than that, I have not seen any issues with the hit reg.
Movements and driving are VERY responsive. When you drive it takes a few seconds for the jeep/motorcycle to start up, then you start moving. It's not because it's unresponsive. This is a WW2 game where vehicles tended to break down, not a racing game where cars start in an instant.
I highly recommend this game, at a solid 7/10, it's a good game. Don't listen to the negative reviewers who have <10 hours on this game. I have 160 hours on this game, PLUS about 300 hours from when the game was still browser based. And that number keeps rising.

It was thankfully forgiving, though, since the brothers couldn't fall off ledges or be separated from each other off screen. Marvelous use of babbling, non-dialogue (think The Sims) and visual cues to convey the world and gameplay.
The characters also have enough of their own personalities that you genuinely start caring for their well-being and nudge them along so they'll finish their quest.
Overall, a nice change of pace and a brief enough story to get through in a couple of hours. It was actually just long enough.
Plus, you get to ride mountain goats! What's not to like?

I feel compelled to offer a review here because I feel the PC version of this game is getting too much negativity. I will first cover that I have not experienced any game breaking bugs and i'm running a PC that is going on 5 years old. I think if I can run it fine, most people should. Obviously, if you're a PC gamer, it is your responsibility to keep your graphics drivers updated and so on. If you are not, that is on you, not the developer.
With that said, the major bugs I have ran into:
-  I cannot save sometimes no matter what I do (killing everyone, etc. to ensure my alarm state is gone). The only resolve is shutting down the game and loading it back up.
-  I ran into a bad graphics glitch only on computer screens where I could not read them but I was able to fix this by playing with resolution settings.
Now, with that out of the way let me touch on the actual game play. The combat feels extremely good (and i'm playing with a Steam controller). I've been maxing out my hacking and sneaking abilities so that I don't have to kill anyone. It is very satisfying, for instance, to complete the entire Palisade Bank without killing one person and hacking all the cameras, doors, robots, lasers, etc. Then just walk through this huge empty building after. For me, this is a perfect stealth game. I'm also a huge fan of the Metal Gear series but I feel this is better than MGSV as far as stealth goes just because the environments are so much more interesting. There are multiple floors, all inter-weaving and connecting, making a huge building one giant puzzle. I feel a stealth game does not really need to be open world, but more so extremely detailed sections to infiltrate, which Deus Ex really nails.
Where Mankind Divided goes beyond the other Deus Ex games is in it's main city. If you were yearning for more to do in Human Revolutions city, this is exactly the place to be. There are hours upon hours of places to explore like apartments, shops, sewers, subways, and more. The city is bustling with locals, police, gangsters, dealers, hobos, etc. It really feels alive. Honestly, i've already spent about 20+ just in the main city, which is all by choice. If that's not your thing, you can certainly rush through the story. But I will say you may be disappointed because the story is not a good reason to play this game. It is roughly 8 hours (if you only do story missions) and really that's where this game falls short. Think of this Deus Ex as almost a sandbox but with more refined areas to explore. You will look at the details in this game, because that's where it is most interesting.
The augmentations or leveling system is pretty good, if not better, than Human Revolution. You are given a few more options but I will say that you will never become TOO good at any one thing. Everything still feels just good enough that the game will throw you challenges. It is cool that they can bring back all the old augs and they can still feel so useful. I guess that is really a testament to how well Human Revolution was too.
The weapons can be customized with silencers, lasers, etc. You can add different ammo types like EMP to incapacitate machines. So far all the weapons feel just right, through I've mostly used my stun gun because it's just so damn useful for my play style. I mostly sell everything I pick up and it's made me a little too rich, to be honest.
Some of the animations still need work, especially facial and speech animations. They still look last-gen. (especially after playing Witcher 3) But the graphics are so gorgeous that it makes you not care. Lighting is top-notch. Environmental detail is really good. It's just characters tend to look a little off in an otherwise beautiful world.
The in-game pay to win options some people are complaining about is really picky. They are praxis kits on the SE store, never suggested for you to go buy them like annoying apps do. You wouldn't even know they're there if you didn't load up the store. They are out there if you want them but I highly recommend you do not buy them because: a) You don't need them, the game is not THAT hard. b) Don't support paid pay-to-win dlc... ever.

I give up. After spending a good portion of the morning/afternoon doing every concievable thing I could and resorting to Google to look for someone, anyone who had my same problem, I'm done. From what I can gather, it seems a small minority, myself included can't seem to play past the logos with the recent patch. I'm finally done trying to make any sort of progress with this game. Screw it, I'll play it next year when all the DLC is released and Eidos maybe stops breaking the game some more. Was a fun ride going through Prague at the speed of a powerpoint slideshow. Okay, I can't recommend this game. But I like it... a lot.
First off: I had TONS of performance issues. (No, I didn't just crank everything up and hope for the best...) I couldn't find a 1440p configuration that my SLI 980s could flourish on. I got a TItan X shortly after and this solved my performance issues. The graphics aren't THAT GOOD to warrant the poor performance on what should still be a capable setup.
Gameplay impressions: Wow, this is Deus Ex! I can do so much. I can sneak, fight (lethal or non-lethal), hack, break, circumvent, etc. The game is just FUN. The gunplay is great, the stealth is even better. The non-lethal options are often more effective than the lethal options!
The augmentations are done a little better this time around, though it still feels like power is drained too quickly for some abilities. Also, some abilities are redundant. I found the arm-cannon that shoots shockwaves almost totally useless while the tesla gun and nano-blade launcher were great for stealth or non-stealth. Overall though, I found myself wanting to try each augment and went into NG+ to max out my character.
The story is ...not that great. Unfortunately, the story ends just as the game was getting good. There are only 2 story DLCs planned for release (I think) so I'm guessing we'll have to wait for a sequel to get significantly past the current ending. (I'm hoping not.) Also, most dialogue is AWFUL and I found myself missing most conversations since they were so boring. Adam Jensen is also painful to listen to. He's the ultimate cringey edgelord, but in a loveable sort of way.
I can't recommend this game, though. Square Enix is really making questionable business decisions. Single use DLC in a single player game? Come on... The weapon variants they give you end up causing clutter to your inventory anyway. They won't even follow you into NG+ unless you take them with you into the final boss fight!
If you can get this game for cheaper than 20 bucks, I'd recommend it. Avoid all of the DLC. But THE GAME IS FUN and I'm hoping for a sequel or DLC that expands on this promising framework. I'll just wait until that DLC is dirt cheap before I buy it.

If you enjoy sand box games, creativity, or working mechanics to produce a result.. you will find many lost hours here.
I won't lie, this game was a little confusing at first which left me not really wanting to play. I watched the video tutorials by the developer, checked out the wiki, and searched the web and steam forums but still found myself lacking in much information. The things I questioned, the developer happily not only answered but explained in details. I decided to compile a
with information to help newcomers get started a lot quicker than me. As well as included details about the achievements.
Once I got the hang of things I quickly became consumed by accumulating the whole world, building automated systems  and producing as many resources and cash as I could to level my world. And mind you, the world feels endless so far. I really enjoy that you can basically collect almost everything you destroy, minus resources that require building a Mining Tower to collect.
I forgot to mention this when I initially wrote my review, one major positive for me is that you can construct your things in any of the materials/textures you collect. I love having that kind of variety.
There are "ship yards" in the open world to salvage random pieces and parts. Four AI factions with different resources and plans to collect and learn. As i have explored my world while i encounter some buildings from the same factions, they don't look exactly the same, but are made of the same materials so I can gather them if needed for reproducing in the Research Lab.
The missions seem pretty cool. Scattered through the world at notable looking structures. Giving you something more to do besides harvesting everything. I have not had the pleasure of PVE team missions or PVP arena as I haven't found anyone to play with. So you guys should pick it up and holler :D:
The only real negative mark for me is that even with running a decent system (specs below), I get a lot of delays. Not enough to deter me, but sometimes it does give me PMS and sometimes it just straight up crashes and exits.
Most notably if i pan to my base too quickly without a hesitation the game exits. Probably cause of all the stuff I have going on there.
Also has seemed like, the more i have built, the more i have automated, the more ships i have gathering crystal resources, the bigger the delay is when i manually click on blocks to collect them with my ship in range to loot. I can click out a whole asteroid with no delays if my ship is not in range, but then there is a large delay when I bring the ship in to auto "vacuum" up the blocks. I suspect its the game waiting to catch up with what just happened.

I've enjoyed playing this game for a very long time, but instead of it feeling like a classic, I'm left with the same disappointment you can expect with pretty much every Mortal Kombat game ever made. The content is wonderful; that isn't the issue... The issue is the complete absence of character balancing and juggling gone completely off the rails. I know every fighter, and can execute almost all of their moves, but this game has serious issues when it comes to juggling. A better name for MKX would be 'Juggling Abuse Simulator,' because that's all every fight boils down to in the end. Some characters don't heavily rely on juggling, but they have absolutely no chance of beating those who do.
For those not familiar with juggling, it is a method of keeping your opponent in the air for as long as possible, and being able to attack them without them being able to do anything to counter it. You only have one way to escape a juggle in MKX, which is your two bar EX breaker, but it won't help. The worst players in the world will spend their entire lives coming up with the lamest combos imaginable, ones that offer you absolutely no way out, and have infinite resets, so that when you DO finally hit the ground, they have a 50/50% chance of starting the combo on you once again. Since some of these ridiculous combos end up doing 50% damage... you can get the picture... That's basically it. I really like the game's content overall, and the fighting system is extremely fun... until you end up facing a juggle ♥♥♥♥♥, and you simply have no chance of winning unless you juggle ♥♥♥♥♥ them back... and I'd rather be doing something better with my time. Personally, when I do one of these combos on another player, I feel like a complete jerk, because I know how messed up it is, but don't expect anyone online to admit it.
So, if you wanna drop a lot of money to have a good time... for a while... then go for it. I have certainly had my share of fun, but if you think you're going to use skill and actual fighting to win fights against juggle ♥♥♥♥♥s... think again. A prime example of this problem is Kotal Kahn compared to Takeda. Kotal has very slow attacks, and a slow projectile, but his combos do massive damage, as he is extremely difficult to use until you learn his moves. He is well designed. Takeda, on the other hand, has a lightning fast teleport, whips that can strike you and open combos on the other side of the stage, very fast, HUGE juggling combos, and a lightning fast low projectile. (can't be blocked unless you're crouch blocking) Can you guess who you'll be fighting online? Takeda. 87% of the time. It gets old after a while, as the game allows you no way to defeat a character that laughably unbalanced unless you do the same thing. Not even the ALIEN or PREDATOR has a chance, and in my book, that's very bad game design, and why I'm not recommending MKX despite enjoying it.
*Update 11/30/2017*
I feel the need to let people know that despite the flaws I've mentioned in great detail, Mortal Kombat X is still 5x better than Injustice 2 because the spamming in that game is beyond atrocious. Deadshot single handedly ruins the game, and is so ridiculous that he makes Takeda look fair. So if you want to try one Netherealm fighter, definitely get MKX between the two. I'm looking forward to MK11 and fully intend to give it a thumbs up if they manage to balance it. It doesn't have to be perfect, but they really need to focus on balancing above everything else to compete with Street Fighter and Teken.

Tight storytelling framed by an impending environment that I can explore and engage.  Fortresses with ample nooks and crannies hidden away.  A healthy complement of augs old and new offer multiple approaches to any situation.  Just look at the eyes and not the lips during the cutscenes.
I must add to me the  side quests are strong and necessary to get the most out of the MD experience, including a murder mystery that rounds out the pathos embodied in the brutal vision of a post-incident Prague.  The world is sizeable enough for paths it puts before you and while there are a few opportunities to revisit a site or two--having a slightly different aug loadout each time I passed thru meant I rarely used the same trail twice and in-turn uncovered a variety of payouts with each pass.  While I will say I want more to explore with these newly acquired skills and as such the end did leave me feeling as things had come to a clsoe just as I started to wield power--to me this was a manageable amount of story.
There are interesting additional modes that come into play and offer another perspective--albeit relatively limited in ways--that are nonetheless shiny and fun in their own right--ultimately I eagerly await to see how  the DLC will pan out.
As someone who has been waiting for a strong single-player experience for sometime--Eidos delivered with Mankind Divided.  I clocked in a meticulous 50 hours--but the average player may burn through this in 20-30 hours.  While I despise the micro-transaction world--I decided to invest in a few Praxis Kits to beef him up from the get-go and I am very glad I did--after all Jensen has already been thru HR and knows how to hack.
Everything looks superb for me out of the box at 4k for me on a Titan X.

Improves on everything that was great about Deus Ex: Human Revolution. They added some really cool new Augmentations ( I think the Icarus Dash is pretty cool personally ), and there's a bit more variety in guns.  They even improved my favorite weapon from HR - the stun gun, turning it into a stun pistol with multiple shots and made it so you can put attachments on it.  There are a lot of options now for non-lethal and lethal play, and more than ever you feel like a walking weapon.  With the special types of ammo I actually find myself carrying guns, despite being non-lethal, to deal with robots.
The new crafting system is simple, unobtrusive, and versatile.  Explore, gather parts, use them to improve your weapons or make items like biocells and multitools.  If you're the type who explores every nook and cranny then you'll have a lot of these and you'll always have what you need to tackle any situation.  Speaking of exploration this game also improves on that.  I was actually surprised with how extensive some of the side paths can get.  If you like looking around, and like to be rewarded for exploring, then you'll have a good time in this game.
The main story is a pretty standard "stop the terrorists" kinda deal with no real surprises. It's the stories of the side missions that really fill the game out.  By the end of the main game you'll feel like you have more questions than answers - it actually feels like the game stops halfway, or maybe two thirds, through the story.  My guess is they'll give us the rest of the story via dlc cause that's the world we live in now.  Got my season pass!

Deus Ex deserves to be chalked up to more than what is painfully offered to the players here.
I was hooked at the start, then out of nowhere I realized how disillusioned I was with the fantasy of what I wanted to experience in this game and it had fallen flat on its face.
The plot is void and exploring throughout the game begins to expose that there's nothing deeply offered for playing the experience. Not much after re-entering Prague and entering the red light district did the truth hit me that the game wasn't going to offer much depth or complexity to the story telling or immersion I could let off the hook.
There's an entire universe to be offered in sciene fiction and cyberpunk and we're using "mafia" and "big brother" narrative tropes again? Please, this is a predictable and hollowing mess. This game is sold to us as being on the edge revolutionary and quite frankly it's not.
The sidequests offer little to no exposing of a deeper plot. I mean, imagine how different it'd have been to reward the player experience by revealing the narrative on a different complexity or secrecy from sidequesting or discovering areas within the game. Instead we're offered a broken and sub level plot which is honestly just shameful. I spend hours exploring, unlock territory only to be rewarded with neuropozyne or a hollow secretary note?
The gameplay isn't up to par with what other games can do and level design is uninspiring. It's great we get really sharp looking textures, but that really doesn't mean anything to me if the game itself isn't stimulating. Most disappointing effects that don't push the envelope of what the future could mean in experiencing next level gameplay, we rarely experience a raw and adapting challenge that suffers from very strong repetition over time. This is what ultimately led me away from the game, everything feels dated to me.
This game just doesn't cut it, remove the hype and what this is supposed to mean to science fiction and gaming. It fails to live up to its prior reputation. Normally I'm not nearly as harsh, but this game represents something more to me in the mind than most since it's the "Cyberpunk" game to reach a larger audience. Someone in the gaming industry could completely blow this game out of the water with the possiblities and I truly hope they do.

My first playthrough took over 90 hours and I loved every minute of it. Exploring Prague, discovering all of its little secrets and stories, studying the level in order to find the most optimal of routes leading to the completion of an objective - all of that was an absolute delight. I enjoyed it just as much as I remember enjoying Human Revolution the first time I played it.
Gameplay, I thought, was much improved over its predecessor. The movement is more fluid and both stealth and guns feel a lot more authentic. On a more negative note, the AI could really use some work. First, the detection problems: Sometimes an unsuspecting NPC won't react to your actions, even if said actions involve hacking into a computer or punching their comrades in the face right next to them. Other times they will be alerted to the tiniest of sounds coming from the room above or below them. Combat AI is even worse. Enemies constantly run into your line of fire and rarely try to flank you, meaning playing through the game aggressively is a breeze even on the highest difficulty and without activating any of the combat oriented augs - you just need a decent gun (such as the Combat Rifle), enough ammo, and a good cover spot. That's why, if you want at least a bit of a challenge, I'd stick to stealth, and refrain from activating certain augs (such as the Cloaking System, Smart Vision and Tesla). Even with the aforementioned detection problems, it's still the way the game was apparently meant to be played. On the subject of stealth, in future DE games, I'd like to see instances of NPC's moving through the level in a more random manner rather than just following dev placed waypoints on the map.
Level design was also taken to the next level. The levels feel less gamey, but no less fun to explore. The game is still filled with vents, but this time they're almost completely optional even for stealth players. Still, I'd like to see less of them in the next game, since you can pretty much (if you want to) avoid every enemy in the game just by using vents (and they're not hard to find or gain access to either). Also, at first I thought having only one hub world was a step back from HR, but after having experienced both games, I can safely say less hubs and more detail is much better than more hubs and less detail.
Plot wise, the main quest was enjoyable enough if a bit uneventful. I enjoyed the conspiracy bits and the way it rewarded exploration in that players who just blindly follow the main objectives don't really get the whole story, since information relevant to the story and the character of Jensen is often hidden in pocket secretaries, computers and sometimes revealed just by listening to NPC chatter. Still, I wished it lasted a bit longer and that more would be revealed. It seems like just as the plot starts to get really interesting, the game ends. I wanted moar. :rage:
The side quest, however, are excellent and reminded me of some of the RPG's of old in terms of quality. There aren't that many of them, but they're all memorable in different ways: either by complementing the main story, fleshing out the main character or telling a story of common individuals just trying their best to survive in this unforgiving, yet strangely appealing world. Quality over quantity is what is all about here.
If not through quests, you can also learn more of the world and its individuals by simply exploring abandoned or not so abandoned places, talking to random NPC's, and so on. There are also these unlogged micro quests (such as making sense of a certain murder, uncovering a smuggling operation, finding answers related to main or side quest before even receiving the said quest, and so on), which will only be apparent to those who explore and pay attention.
The publisher's shady practices notwithstanding, I can safely say that any self-respecting RPG lover is missing out by not playing this game. In the age where almost everything (from food to entertainment) is designed to offer instant gratification, this game feels like a welcome surprise (especially considering it's not an indie game). Games such as these are a true rarity and should be revered instead of shunned if there is to be any hope of similarly engrossing games ever appearing in the future.
